children.title: Extreme-Point Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations based on blockwise extreme points for bounded convex components.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite generator representation of a bounded Dantzig–Wolfe block polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polytope with extreme points \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\). Then
\[P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_jv^j:\lambda_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_j=1\right\}.\]
Consequently, replacing a block variable \(x\in P\) by \(x=\sum_j\lambda_jv^j\), together with the convexity equation \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\), is an exact representation of that block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point of a bounded block polytope is exactly a convex combination of its extreme points.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
\(\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}=\operatorname{ext}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_jv^j:\lambda\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1\right\}\).

notation.meaning: Extreme point of the block polytope

review_flags: Standard Minkowski–Weyl specialization, but no supplied locator directly supports Dantzig–Wolfe extreme-point representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but the record provides no citation with an inspectable polyhedral-theory or Dantzig–Wolfe locator.

children.title: Extreme-Ray Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations based on extreme rays for recession or unbounded components.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-and-ray representation of an unbounded pointed Dantzig–Wolfe block polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron with extreme points \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\), and let \(r^1,\ldots,r^M\) generate the extreme rays of its recession cone. Then
\[P=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_jv^j+\sum_{\ell=1}^M\mu_\ell r^\ell:\lambda,\mu\ge0,\ \sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_j=1\right\}.\]
The \(\lambda\)-variables represent point columns, whereas the \(\mu\)-variables represent recession columns and carry no convexity normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointed unbounded block polyhedron is generated by convex combinations of extreme points plus nonnegative combinations of extreme rays.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, polyhedral, and pointed.
\(v^j\) and \(r^\ell\) enumerate its extreme points and recession rays.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^M\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the block polyhedron

review_flags: Standard Minkowski–Weyl result, but no supplied locator directly supports the point–ray Dantzig–Wolfe form.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The point–ray representation and content kind fit the leaf under the stated pointedness assumption, but no supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Point–Ray Regime Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determining when point components, ray components, or both are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Point–Ray Regime Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions determining when point columns, ray columns, or lineality generators are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\), point columns alone suffice exactly when \(P\) is bounded, equivalently when \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}\). If \(P\) is pointed and \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\ne\{0\}\), an exact finite generator representation requires recession-ray columns in addition to point columns. If the lineality space \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap-\operatorname{rec}(P)\) is nontrivial, \(P\) need not possess extreme points; a representation using only extreme points and extreme rays is then insufficient unless lineality directions are included or the lineality is removed by reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded blocks need only points; pointed unbounded blocks need rays; blocks with lineality require explicit lineality handling or reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ bounded}\iff\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}\); nonzero recession or lineality determines the additional generators required.
review_flags: A directly relevant polyhedral-theory locator is absent from the supplied source hints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the regime-boundary leaf. A specific polyhedral-theory source is required for the boundedness equivalence and the distinctions among pointed recession rays, lineality directions, and existence of extreme points.

children.title: Blockwise Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull representations developed separately for decomposable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of separable blocks while retaining common linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty sets whose convex hulls are polyhedra, and let the only cross-block constraints be \(\sum_{i=1}^q A_i x_i=b\). The blockwise convexification is
\[\left\{x:\sum_{i=1}^qA_ix_i=b,\ x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,q\right\}.\]
It is a relaxation of the original feasible set. Moreover, its value for every linear objective equals the value obtained by replacing each block with any exact finite generator representation of \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexify each separable block independently and retain the linking equations; generator substitution gives the same linear optimization value.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty for every \(i\).
\(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\) admits a finite polyhedral generator representation.
All cross-block restrictions are expressed by \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\subseteq\{x:x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i),\ \sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\).

notation.meaning: Block contribution to the linking constraints

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly addresses blockwise convexification in Dantzig–Wolfe reformulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and blockwise relaxation statement fit the leaf, but no cited locator supports the Dantzig–Wolfe convexification claim or generator-value equivalence.

children.title: Blockwise Extended Formulations
children.top_down_role: Lifted block representations using auxiliary variables or expanded spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator-variable extension of independently convexified polyhedral blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose each block hull has the pointed representation
\[\operatorname{conv}(X_i)=\left\{\sum_{j\in J_i}\lambda_{ij}v^{ij}+\sum_{\ell\in R_i}\mu_{i\ell}r^{i\ell}:\lambda_i,\mu_i\ge0,\ \sum_{j\in J_i}\lambda_{ij}=1\right\}.\]
Substituting this expression for every \(x_i\) into \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\) yields a blockwise extended formulation in variables \((\lambda,\mu)\). Its projection under \(x_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}v^{ij}+\sum_\ell\mu_{i\ell}r^{i\ell}\) is precisely the blockwise-convexified feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce point and ray weights for every block; the resulting master formulation projects exactly onto the blockwise convexification.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\) is a nonempty pointed polyhedron.
The listed points and rays generate \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=\{x:\sum_iA_ix_i=b,\ x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\}\), where \(E\) is the displayed generator extension with the linking equations.

notation.meaning: Point and ray index sets for block i
Point and ray generators of block i

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports this Dantzig–Wolfe extended formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extended-formulation representation fits the leaf and is internally coherent under exact pointed block generators, but it has no supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Convexification–Extension Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Navigation between block convexification choices and their lifted formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification–Extension Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection equivalence between blockwise convexification and its generator extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x:\sum_iA_ix_i=b,\ x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\}\), and let \(E\) be the exact point–ray generator extension of the same blocks. Then
\[C=\operatorname{proj}_x(E).\]
Hence, for every linear objective \(\sum_i c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\), optimization over \(C\) and over \(E\) has the same optimal value whenever that value is well-defined. A feasible generator vector maps to a feasible convexified point, and every feasible convexified point admits at least one feasible generator vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact block generators create an extended formulation whose projection and every linear optimal value coincide with blockwise convexification.
assumptions_latex: Each block generator system represents \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\) exactly.
The linking equations in \(C\) and \(E\) are identical after substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\operatorname{proj}_x(E)\) and \(\inf_{x\in C}\sum_ic_i^{\mathsf T}x_i=\inf_{(x,\lambda,\mu)\in E}\sum_ic_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly documents the convexification–extension projection correspondence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection correspondence is plausible, but no source is supplied. Moreover, this is an extended-formulation projection equivalence, not mathematical duality; representation or property would better describe its role.

children.title: Single Pricing Block
children.top_down_role: Pricing architectures centered on one local block or one oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Pricing Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master pricing when all columns arise from one block generator set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a restricted-master dual vector \(\pi\) for the linking equations and dual scalar \(\sigma\) for the block convexity equation, solve
\[z=\min_{x\in X}\{(c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x-\sigma\}.\]
If an optimizer \(x^*\) satisfies \(z< -\tau\), append its column to the restricted master. If the problem is solved globally and \(z\ge-\tau\), no omitted point column has reduced cost below \(-\tau\). For an unbounded block, recession-column pricing separately minimizes \((c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}r\) over normalized recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One oracle prices the common block; a negative reduced-cost generator enters, while a global nonnegative result certifies no improving point column.
assumptions_latex: All omitted point columns are generated by one set \(X\).
\(\pi\) and \(\sigma\) are dual-optimal for the current restricted master.
\(\tau\ge0\) is the pricing tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z< -\tau\) produces an entering column; exact \(z\ge-\tau\) excludes every point column with reduced cost below \(-\tau\).

notation.meaning: Minimum reduced cost returned by pricing

review_flags: A column-generation source is required for the pricing and recession-column conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits single-block pricing, but a column-generation source is required. The admissible normalization for recession-direction pricing is also unspecified, so that subproblem is not fully defined.

children.title: Multiple Pricing Blocks
children.top_down_role: Pricing architectures distributing column search across several blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Pricing Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent reduced-cost pricing for a separable collection of Dantzig–Wolfe blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For blocks \(i=1,\ldots,q\), given restricted-master duals \(\pi\) and \(\sigma_i\), solve independently
\[z_i=\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{(c_i-A_i^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_i-\sigma_i\}.\]
Append an optimizer from any block with \(z_i< -\tau_i\), possibly appending several columns in one iteration. If every pricing problem is solved globally and \(z_i\ge-\tau_i\) for all \(i\), no omitted point column from any block violates its reduced-cost tolerance. Ray pricing, when required, is performed blockwise without the term \(\sigma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Price each separable block with shared linking duals and its own convexity dual; global nonnegative block minima jointly certify completeness.
assumptions_latex: The generator domain is the Cartesian product \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_q\).
Each block has its own convexity equation and multiplier \(\sigma_i\).
All \(q\) pricing problems are globally solved for certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_i\ge-\tau_i\) for every \(i\) excludes any omitted point column violating its block tolerance.

notation.meaning: Minimum reduced cost for block i
Dual multiplier of block i's convexity equation

review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers multiple-block Dantzig–Wolfe pricing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiple-block pricing algorithm fits the leaf and separates consistently under the stated assumptions, but no Dantzig–Wolfe or column-generation source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Block-Coordination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Coordination issues created by independent or coupled pricing blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coordination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separability criterion for independent pricing and its failure under cross-block generator restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Independent block pricing is exact when the admissible generator domain is \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_q\) and reduced cost separates as
\[\bar c(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q\bar c_i(x_i),\qquad \min_x\bar c(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q\min_{x_i\in X_i}\bar c_i(x_i).\]
If omitted-column feasibility includes a constraint coupling two or more block choices, or if the reduced cost contains a nonseparable term, separate minimizers need not form an admissible or globally minimum column. Joint pricing, an additional coordination master, or a reformulation restoring separability is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate pricing is exact only for a Cartesian generator domain and additive reduced cost; cross-block restrictions require coordination or joint pricing.
assumptions_latex: Each block set \(X_i\) is nonempty.
The pricing objective has a finite minimum whenever the displayed equality is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cartesian feasibility and additive reduced cost justify independent pricing; failure of either condition invalidates that certification in general.
review_flags: The precise coordination boundary needs a decomposition-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits. The Cartesian-domain and additive-objective criterion is plausible, but the asserted coordination consequences require a decomposition-specific citation.

children.title: Exact Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes requiring complete resolution of the relevant column-search problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global reduced-cost minimization as an optimality certificate for a restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) index all admissible columns and let \(J_k\subseteq J\) be the restricted-master columns. At a restricted-master dual solution \(y_k\), exact pricing computes
\[\rho_k=\inf_{j\in J}\bar c_j(y_k).\]
If an attaining column has \(\rho_k<0\), it is eligible to enter. If \(\rho_k\ge0\), then \(y_k\) satisfies every dual constraint of the full master; together with restricted-master primal feasibility and equality of restricted primal and dual values, this certifies optimality for the full linear master. With tolerance \(\tau\), \(\rho_k\ge-\tau\) gives only the corresponding tolerance-dependent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global pricing either finds a negative reduced-cost column or proves full-master dual feasibility and hence LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The full and restricted masters are linear programs with the same existing constraints.
The restricted master has primal and dual optimal solutions.
Pricing globally minimizes reduced cost over every admissible column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\ge0\) implies full-master dual feasibility and certifies full-master optimality of the restricted-master solution.

notation.meaning: Restricted and complete column index sets
Reduced cost of column j at the restricted dual solution

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly establishes the column-generation optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits exact pricing, and the zero-tolerance LP certificate is standard. No supporting locator is supplied, and the quantitative meaning of the tolerance-dependent certificate is not stated precisely.

children.title: Heuristic Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes using incomplete search to discover improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncertifying search for negative reduced-cost columns before exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given restricted-master dual solution \(y_k\), a heuristic pricing oracle searches a subset \(H_k\subseteq J\) and returns some \(j_k\in H_k\) with \(\bar c_{j_k}(y_k)<-\tau\), if it finds one. The returned column may be appended and the restricted master reoptimized. Failure to find such a column establishes only
\[\bar c_j(y_k)\ge-\tau\quad\text{for every examined }j\in H_k;\]
it does not imply the inequality for \(J\setminus H_k\). Therefore heuristic pricing alone cannot certify full-master optimality unless an independently valid coverage or lower-bound certificate is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic pricing may quickly find improving columns, but an unsuccessful search does not certify that no improving column exists.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k\subseteq J\) is the set of columns actually examined.
Every returned column is admissible for the full master.
\(\tau\ge0\) is the reduced-cost tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A found column with \(\bar c_{j_k}(y_k)<-\tau\) is valid for entry; failure on \(H_k\) is not a certificate over \(J\).

notation.meaning: Columns examined by the heuristic oracle

review_flags: The supplied heuristic-method locator is not specific to column-generation pricing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits heuristic pricing, and the noncertification boundary is stated clearly. The available generic heuristic-method inventory does not support this column-generation-specific claim.

children.title: Partial Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes searching only a selected subset of blocks or candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional minimization-form column generation with blockwise partial pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\pi^t\), choose a nonempty subset \(S_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\) and solve the pricing problems only for \(k\in S_t\): \[z_k^t=\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_j(\pi^t).\] Add any discovered column satisfying \(\bar c_j(\pi^t)<-\varepsilon\), reoptimize the restricted master, and repeat. The iteration is exhaustive only on \(\bigcup_{k\in S_t}J_k\). At a terminal dual vector \(\pi^T\), termination is certified only if every block is priced exactly at \(\pi^T\), or a valid blockwise lower bound proves \(\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_j(\pi^T)\ge-\varepsilon\) for every block \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial pricing searches selected blocks for negative reduced-cost columns. Termination is certified only when every block is exactly priced or validly bounded at the terminal dual vector.
assumptions_latex: The full column set \(J\) is partitioned into pricing blocks \(J_1,\ldots,J_K\).
At iteration \(t\), the restricted master supplies a dual vector \(\pi^t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration may add improving columns, but searches performed at earlier or different dual vectors do not certify full-master optimality at the terminal dual vector.

notation.meaning: set of pricing blocks inspected at iteration t
reduced cost of column j at dual vector pi

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard partial-pricing regime for block-structured column generation

children.title: Pricing-Certification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on what each pricing regime can certify about missing columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Certification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates search success from a valid full-master optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^R\) be optimal for the restricted master over \(R\subseteq J\), with dual solution \(\pi\). The exact pricing certificate is \[\min_{j\in J\setminus R}\bar c_j(\pi)\ge0.\] Under this condition, \(\lambda^R\), extended by zeros outside \(R\), is optimal for the full master. For \(\varepsilon>0\), the condition \[\min_{j\in J\setminus R}\bar c_j(\pi)\ge-\varepsilon\] excludes columns whose reduced cost is below \(-\varepsilon\), but it yields a quantified objective-gap certificate only when accompanied by a valid bound on admissible aggregate column weight. If pricing is heuristic, partial, or returns only an incumbent without a valid lower bound, failure to find a column with reduced cost below the threshold is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact exhaustive pricing or valid global bounds transfer restricted-master optimality to the full master. Tolerant bounds require an aggregate column-weight bound to quantify suboptimality, and incomplete search failure is not a certificate.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair \((\lambda^R,\pi)\).
The full master is a minimization LP with column set \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact restricted-master optimality transfers when every omitted column has nonnegative reduced cost; tolerant reduced-cost bounds require additional problem-specific information to quantify an objective gap.

notation.meaning: columns currently present in the restricted master

children.title: Restricted-Master Structure
children.top_down_role: Structural organization of the current generated-column master problem.

assumptions_latex: The full master is \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda\ge0\}\).
A finite subset \(R\subseteq J\) yields a feasible restricted problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite active set \(R\subseteq J\), the restricted master is \[\min_{\lambda_R\ge0}\left\{\sum_{j\in R}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in R}a_j\lambda_j=b\right\}.\] Its dual is \[\max_{\pi}\left\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi:a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_j\ \text{for every }j\in R\right\}.\] Thus an optimal restricted-master dual vector \(\pi^R\) induces the full-column reduced-cost function \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^R\). Columns outside \(R\) violate full dual feasibility exactly when \(\bar c_j<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master retains a finite active column set. Its dual solution prices every possible column and identifies omitted dual-constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a feasible finite set \(R_0\). At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master over \(R_t\), obtaining primal solution \(\lambda^t\) and dual prices \(\pi^t\). Solve \[j_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in J}\{c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^t\}.\] If \(c_{j_t}-a_{j_t}^{\mathsf T}\pi^t<-\varepsilon\), set \(R_{t+1}=R_t\cup\{j_t\}\) and continue. Otherwise stop and output \(\lambda^t\), together with the pricing bound establishing that no omitted column has reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted master, price omitted columns using its dual solution, add an improving column, and stop only with a valid pricing bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the pricing vector \[\tilde\pi^t=(1-\alpha_t)\hat\pi^t+\alpha_t\pi^t,\qquad \alpha_t\in[0,1],\] and price columns using \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\tilde\pi^t\). After accepting new columns and resolving the restricted master, update \(\hat\pi^t\) according to the stabilization policy and relax stabilization as certification approaches. A stopping test based only on \(\tilde\pi^t\) is valid for the original full master only if \(\tilde\pi^t\) is dual feasible there; otherwise exact pricing at an appropriate original-master dual vector is required.

children.title: Primal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization organized around primal master representations or primal movement.

assumptions_latex: The restricted-master feasible set \(F_R\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A reference primal point \(\hat\lambda^t\in F_R\) and parameter \(\rho_t>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized master selects a feasible primal solution near the reference point; certification remains tied to the unregularized master.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quadratic primal regularization of a restricted master
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization directly in restricted-master primal column weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), replace the unregularized restricted-master selection by \[\lambda^{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda\in F_R}\left\{c_R^{\mathsf T}\lambda+\frac{\rho_t}{2}\lVert\lambda-\hat\lambda^t\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Use the associated coupling multipliers for pricing, update \(\hat\lambda^t\), and reduce or remove the regularization before declaring full-master optimality. Because the quadratic term changes the master objective, optimality of this stabilized subproblem alone is not an optimality certificate for the original linear master unless the regularization contribution is eliminated or explicitly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal stabilization regularizes restricted-master column weights around a reference point. The altered objective must be removed or bounded before certifying the original LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Stabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic primal regularization is mathematically plausible, but its use as a column-generation stabilization method, the pricing multipliers it supplies, and the stated certification conditions require a dedicated source.

children.title: Proximal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization organized around proximity controls in the coordination space.

assumptions_latex: The dual master objective is represented by a proper closed convex function \(g\).
A reference price \(\hat\pi^t\) and parameter \(\tau_t>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal step produces a uniquely controlled dual iterate when the squared norm is strongly convex, without changing the target once the proximal residual vanishes.

notation.meaning: convex objective whose minimization represents the dual master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal-point stabilization applied to the dual master objective.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Proximal point method p. 44

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \[\pi^{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi}\left\{g(\pi)+\frac{1}{2\tau_t}\lVert\pi-\hat\pi^t\rVert_2^2\right\},\] using generated columns or cuts to represent the relevant portions of \(g\), and then update the center, commonly by setting \(\hat\pi^{t+1}=\pi^{t+1}\). The optimality condition is \[0\in\partial g(\pi^{t+1})+\tau_t^{-1}(\pi^{t+1}-\hat\pi^t).\] Hence a vanishing proximal residual together with complete pricing recovers stationarity for the unstabilized dual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal stabilization penalizes movement of dual prices from a center. Vanishing proximal residual plus complete pricing restores the unstabilized dual optimality condition.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Certificates

assumptions_latex: The full master is a minimization LP and \(\pi\) is feasible for its equality-row dual variables.
Reduced costs are computed for every column or bounded globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonnegative reduced costs certify full-master optimality of a feasible restricted-master solution; tolerance bounds quantify approximate optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for an equality-form minimization master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((\lambda,\pi)\) is an exact reduced-cost certificate when \(\lambda\ge0\), \(A\lambda=b\), and \[\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\ge0\quad\text{for all }j\in J,\qquad \lambda_j\bar c_j=0\quad\text{for all }j\in J.\] These conditions certify primal and dual optimality. More generally, if \(\bar c_j\ge-\varepsilon\) for all \(j\) and a problem-specific bound controls the total admissible column weight, then the same reduced-cost data yield a corresponding additive objective-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, nonnegative reduced costs, and complementary slackness certify master optimality. Tolerant reduced-cost bounds require a bound on total column weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact LP certificate and the qualified tolerance statement are standard and internally consistent, and certificate is the correct content kind, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Pricing Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates produced by pricing-oracle outcomes across relevant blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-separable pricing certificate with exact optima or rigorous lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(k=1,\ldots,K\), a pricing certificate supplies a verifiable value satisfying \[L_k(\pi)\le\min_{j\in J_k}\{c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\}.\] If \(L_k(\pi)\ge-\varepsilon\) for every block, then every column satisfies \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\ge-\varepsilon\), so no column improves the restricted master beyond the declared tolerance. An incumbent returned by a minimization oracle is an upper bound on the pricing optimum and therefore cannot, without an accompanying lower bound or exactness guarantee, serve as this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing certificate gives a rigorous lower bound for each block's minimum reduced cost. Mere failure to find an improving column is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Each pricing block is solved exactly or returns a rigorous lower bound.
The candidate dual vector \(\pi\) is the vector being tested for full-master dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Blockwise lower bounds certify the absence of columns with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\) when every block meets that threshold.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on the minimum reduced cost in block k

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Transfer Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface transferring blockwise pricing evidence to a full-master LP certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\lambda^R,\pi^R)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for the restricted master. Extend \(\lambda^R\) by zeros on \(J\setminus R\), and let each pricing block certify \[L_k(\pi^R)\le\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_j(\pi^R).\] If \(L_k(\pi^R)\ge0\) for every \(k\), then \(\pi^R\) is feasible for every full-master dual constraint and \(\lambda^R\) is full-master optimal. If only \(L_k(\pi^R)\ge-\varepsilon\), transfer to an objective-gap certificate additionally requires a valid bound on admissible aggregate column weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blockwise pricing bounds become a full-master certificate by establishing every omitted dual constraint; approximate transfer also needs a column-weight bound.
assumptions_latex: The restricted-master primal solution is feasible for the full master after assigning zero weight to omitted columns.
Pricing supplies valid lower bounds for all omitted-column reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing bounds transfer restricted-master primal-dual information into an exact certificate, or into a quantified approximate certificate when an aggregate column-weight bound is also available.

notation.meaning: global lower bound on blockwise reduced costs

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: LP basis degeneracy specialized to the restricted master
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal basis degeneracy in an equality-form restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimal basic feasible restricted-master solution is degenerate when at least one basic column variable equals zero; equivalently, fewer than \(m\) basic variables are strictly positive when the basis has \(m\) positions. In column generation, such degeneracy can allow a newly generated negative-reduced-cost column to enter through a zero-length pivot, leaving the primal solution and objective unchanged. Multiple optimal or nearly optimal bases may then yield substantially different dual vectors, so successive pricing problems can oscillate even though the restricted-master objective exhibits little or no progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master degeneracy occurs when an optimal basis contains zero basic variables. It enables zero-progress pivots and can cause unstable pricing duals.
knowledge_statements.title: Master Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basis-degeneracy definition is correct for an equality-form LP, but the column-generation consequences concerning zero-length pivots, dual instability, and oscillatory pricing require an inspectable source.

children.title: Column-Generation Tail-Off
children.top_down_role: Late-stage regimes characterized by weak incremental progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Tail-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary for slow objective progress in exact LP column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization restricted-master sequence with values \(z_k\), dual vectors \(\pi_k\), and exact pricing minima \(r_k^{\min}\). The run exhibits column-generation tail-off on iterations \(k\in K\) at tolerances \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\) when \(r_k^{\min}< -\varepsilon\) while \(0\le z_k-z_{k+1}\le\delta\) for every \(k\in K\). Thus pricing repeatedly certifies meaningful dual infeasibility, yet adding the priced columns produces only small master-objective improvements. Tail-off alone neither certifies optimality nor implies that pricing has failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tail-off occurs when pricing repeatedly finds materially negative reduced-cost columns but successive restricted-master objectives improve only slightly; it is not an optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) is the exact restricted-master optimum at iteration \(k\).
\(r_k^{\min}\) is obtained by exact pricing under \(\pi_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k^{\min}< -\varepsilon\) together with \(0\le z_k-z_{k+1}\le\delta\) characterizes tail-off, not termination.

notation.meaning: minimum reduced cost returned by pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf and the mathematics is internally coherent, but the proposed threshold-based characterization is a local convention without cited support.

children.title: Column Proliferation
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which excessive generated columns burden the master representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Proliferation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary for excessive restricted-master growth relative to useful progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k\) be the columns present after iteration \(k\), let \(B_k\subseteq C_k\) be an optimal basic column set, and let \(z_k\) be the minimization master value. Column proliferation over \(k=0,\ldots,N\) occurs when \(\lvert C_N\rvert-\lvert C_0\rvert\) is large while many generated columns remain nonbasic or duplicate existing master coefficient vectors, and the aggregate improvement \(z_0-z_N\) is small relative to that growth. The condition identifies master-size pathology; it does not invalidate the reduced-cost optimality test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column proliferation is rapid master growth dominated by unused or duplicate columns while objective progress remains small; exact reduced-cost termination remains valid.
assumptions_latex: Each restricted master is solved to optimality.
Columns with identical master coefficients and costs are treated as duplicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Excessive growth of \(\lvert C_k\rvert\) relative to \(z_0-z_N\) is a computational pathology, not a failure of LP optimality theory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but “large” growth and “small” improvement do not define an inspectable boundary, and no source supports this operational characterization.

children.title: Pathology Interaction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where degeneracy, tail-off, or column growth reinforce one another.

knowledge_statements.title: Pathology Interaction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates computational interactions among degeneracy, tail-off, and column proliferation from correctness failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In exact LP column generation, master degeneracy, tail-off, and column proliferation may coexist: alternative optimal bases can change \(\pi_k\), pricing can generate distinct negative-reduced-cost columns, and those columns can yield negligible objective improvement while enlarging the master. Their interaction crosses the correctness boundary only if an inexact procedure declares termination without establishing \(r_k^{\min}\ge -\varepsilon\), or discards columns in a way that removes all representations needed for the restricted-master optimum. Otherwise these phenomena affect computational progress but not the reduced-cost certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy, tail-off, and proliferation may reinforce one another, but correctness fails only when termination or column management destroys the reduced-cost certificate.
assumptions_latex: The full master is an LP with a valid reduced-cost pricing oracle.
Restricted masters are feasible and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With exact pricing, termination requires \(r_k^{\min}\ge -\varepsilon\); observed stagnation or master growth cannot replace this test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction-boundary role fits, but the assertion that correctness can fail only in the two stated ways is too broad to retain without a formal source. The effect of column deletion also requires more precise conditions.

children.title: Lagrangian Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation choices based on moving selected coupling restrictions into the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization form obtained by dualizing coupling equalities in a separable finite-dimensional convex program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\). For each \(i\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^p\) be linear, and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). For \[p^\star=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\right\},\] the Lagrangian relaxation at \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) is \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\left\langle\lambda,\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i-b\right\rangle\right\}.\] It has the block representation \[q(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda,x_i\rangle\right\},\] and weak duality gives \(q(\lambda)\le p^\star\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional separable convex minimization problem, dualizing the coupling equality produces independent block minimizations, and every multiplier gives a valid lower bound on the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and convex.
Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, with nonempty effective domain intersecting \(X_i\).
The primal constraint is the equality \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), \(q(\lambda)\le p^\star\), and \(q(\lambda)\) admits the displayed block-separable representation.

notation.meaning: linear coupling operator for block i

children.title: Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Blockwise coordination through a dual representation of linking structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supergradient dual decomposition for equality-coupled separable convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^p\), positive step sizes \(\alpha_k\), and an iteration limit \(N\), for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\) each block computes in parallel \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda^k,x_i\rangle\right\}.\] Form \(g^k=\sum_i A_i x_i^k-b\) and update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k\). For every \(\mu\in\mathbb R^p\), \[q(\mu)\le q(\lambda^k)+\langle g^k,\mu-\lambda^k\rangle,\] so \(g^k\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function at \(\lambda^k\). Output the best computed dual bound \(\max_{0\le j\le N}q(\lambda^j)\) and any primal point produced by a separately specified recovery procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block minimizes independently at the current equality multiplier. The coordinator forms the coupling residual, which is a dual supergradient, performs an ascent update, and retains the best dual bound.
assumptions_latex: The coupling constraint is \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\), with multiplier domain \(\mathbb R^p\).
Every block subproblem attains its minimum.
Each step size satisfies \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(g^k\) is a supergradient of \(q\) at \(\lambda^k\), and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k\) is a supergradient-ascent update.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative restricted-master method; the extract supplies no stopping criterion or convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose any \(\lambda^0\). For every \(j=1,\ldots,J\), compute
\[
x_j(\lambda^0)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_j\in X_j}\{f_j(x_j)+(\lambda^0)'A_jx_j\}.
\]
At iteration \(k\geq1\), solve the restricted master formed from the columns indexed by \(i=0,\ldots,k-1\), and let \(\lambda^k\) be a Lagrange multiplier for its linking equality
\[
\sum_{j=1}^J A_j\left(\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\xi^i x_j(\lambda^i)\right)=b.
\]
Then, for every \(j\), compute
\[
x_j(\lambda^k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_j\in X_j}\{f_j(x_j)+(\lambda^k)'A_jx_j\}.
\]
Augment the master with a variable \(\xi^k\) having cost
\[
c_k=\sum_{j=1}^J f_j(x_j(\lambda^k))
\]
and column
\[
a_k=\begin{pmatrix}1\\ \sum_{j=1}^J A_jx_j(\lambda^k)\end{pmatrix},
\]
and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from any multiplier and solve every block Lagrangian subproblem. At each iteration, solve the current restricted master and use a multiplier of its linking equality to resolve all block subproblems. Add one aggregate column whose cost is the sum of the resulting block objective values and whose entries are one together with the aggregate linking vector, then repeat.
assumptions_latex: J\in\mathbb{N}
x_j(\lambda^k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_j\in X_j}\{f_j(x_j)+(\lambda^k)'A_jx_j\}\text{ can be obtained for every generated }\lambda^k
\text{Each restricted master can be solved and supplies a multiplier }\lambda^k\text{ for its linking equality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The restricted master is recursively enlarged by }(c_k,a_k)=\left(\sum_{j=1}^J f_j(x_j(\lambda^k)),\begin{pmatrix}1\\ \sum_{j=1}^J A_jx_j(\lambda^k)\end{pmatrix}\right).

children.title: Relaxation–Decomposition Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Navigation between relaxed constraints and the resulting dual block structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation–Decomposition Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic correspondence between dualized coupling constraints and blockwise dual evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separable objective \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\), product domain \(X=\prod_i X_i\), and coupling equality \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\), relaxing that equality with \(\lambda\) gives \[q(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_i q_i(\lambda),\qquad q_i(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda,x_i\rangle\bigr).\] Conversely, the block functions \(q_i\) and common multiplier reconstruct the Lagrangian dual \(\sup_\lambda q(\lambda)\). Hence relaxation creates decomposition precisely when all cross-block dependence lies in the dualized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the only cross-block constraints makes dual evaluation separable; summing the block value functions reconstructs the Lagrangian dual.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_i X_i\) and \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\).
All cross-block dependence occurs through \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is decomposable exactly through the displayed additive representation of \(q(\lambda)\).

children.title: Augmented Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition regimes using augmented penalties for coupling coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-of-multipliers decomposition with a quadratic equality-coupling residual penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=\sum_i A_i x_i-b\), choose \(\rho>0\), \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^p\), and an iteration limit \(N\). For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda^k,r(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r(x)\rVert^2\right\}\] by an exact coordinated or decomposed inner solution, and set \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho r(x^{k+1}).\] Output \(x^N\), \(\lambda^N\), and the residual \(r(x^N)\). The quadratic term generally couples the blocks, so implementing the primal step by decomposition requires splitting, coordination, or auxiliary consensus variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method exactly minimizes an augmented Lagrangian and updates the multiplier by the coupling residual. Its quadratic penalty generally couples blocks, so the inner minimization requires a coordinated decomposition mechanism.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The coupling constraint is \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\).
Each displayed augmented-Lagrangian minimization attains a solution and is solved exactly.
The penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal minimization and multiplier update define the equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian iteration, whose primal step is generally not directly block-separable.

children.title: Proximal Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition regimes using proximal controls in primal or dual spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximally stabilized maximization of a concave Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a concave dual function \(q\), center \(\lambda^k\), and parameter \(t_k>0\), compute \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda}\left\{q(\lambda)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert\lambda-\lambda^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Evaluate \(q(\lambda)\) through its independent Lagrangian block subproblems. Stop when \(\lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert/t_k\le\varepsilon\), and output \(\lambda^{k+1}\), its dual bound, and any recovered feasible primal point. The proximal term regularizes multiplier movement while preserving separable evaluation of \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method maximizes a proximally regularized dual model, stabilizing multiplier movement while evaluating the dual through independent block problems.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave.
The proximal maximization attains a solution for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{k+1}\) is the proximal-point update for maximizing \(q\).

children.title: Augmentation–Proximal Hybrid Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes combining augmented coupling penalties with proximal stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmentation–Proximal Hybrid Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid primal-residual augmentation and proximal multiplier stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\rho_k>0\), \(t_k>0\), and \((x^k,\lambda^k)\). A hybrid iteration computes \(x^{k+1}\) by minimizing a decomposed or split model of \(\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda^k,r(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert r(x)\rVert^2\), then chooses \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda}\left\{\widehat q_k(\lambda)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert\lambda-\lambda^k\rVert^2\right\},\] where \(\widehat q_k\) is the dual model induced by the augmented primal step. Stop when coupling and multiplier residuals meet prescribed tolerances. Positive \(\rho_k\) and finite \(t_k\) distinguish the hybrid regime from either pure method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid combines a quadratic primal feasibility penalty with a proximal restriction on multiplier movement and stops using primal and dual residuals.
assumptions_latex: The block functions and domains are closed and convex.
Each primal and multiplier subproblem is solved to its declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k>0\) and \(t_k<\infty\) jointly define an augmentation–proximal hybrid iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Dual Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal or bundle stabilization for concave, generally nondifferentiable decomposition duals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be a concave dual function available through values and supergradients. Maintain a center \(\bar\lambda^k\) and a concave cutting-plane model \(m_k(\lambda)\ge q(\lambda)\). For \(t_k>0\), compute \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda}\left\{m_k(\lambda)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Evaluate \(q(\lambda^{k+1})\), add its supergradient cut, and accept it as the new center only when actual dual improvement is a prescribed fraction of predicted improvement. Stop when the model-predicted improvement is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle model limits unstable multiplier motion, adds supergradient cuts, and changes the center only after sufficient actual dual improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave.
Exact values and one supergradient of \(q\) are available at trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal term and serious-step test stabilize maximization of the nonsmooth dual function \(q\).

notation.meaning: polyhedral upper model of the concave dual function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bundle-stabilization outline is mathematically plausible and the algorithm role fits, but the serious-step and predicted-improvement conventions require an authoritative bundle-method source and precise locator.

children.title: Lagrangian Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Bound information obtained from Lagrangian or dual-decomposition representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable lower-bound certificate for a minimization problem with relaxed coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For multiplier \(\lambda\), provide block minimizers \(x_i(\lambda)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda,x_i\rangle\}\) and the value \[L(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_i\left(f_i(x_i(\lambda))+\langle A_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda,x_i(\lambda)\rangle\right).\] Independent verification of block feasibility, block optimality, and arithmetic establishes \(L(\lambda)=q(\lambda)\le p^\star\). With a feasible primal point \(\hat x\), the pair additionally certifies \(0\le F(\hat x)-p^\star\le F(\hat x)-L(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier and verifiably optimal block solutions certify a global lower bound; adding a feasible primal point certifies an optimality-gap upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization problem with coupling equality \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\).
Each supplied block solution is globally optimal for its Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\lambda)\le p^\star\), and feasible \(\hat x\) yields gap certificate \(F(\hat x)-L(\lambda)\).

children.title: Primal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Routes from decomposed or dual solutions to primal candidate solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ergodic recovery of a coupling-feasible primal candidate from Lagrangian block solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given block solutions \(x_i^k\in X_i\) from dual iterations and weights \(w_k>0\), define \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^N w_k\) and \(\bar x_i^N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^N w_k x_i^k\). If each \(X_i\) is convex, then \(\bar x_i^N\in X_i\), while its coupling residual is \[r(\bar x^N)=\sum_i A_i\bar x_i^N-b=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^N w_k\left(\sum_i A_i x_i^k-b\right).\] Stop when this residual and a primal-dual gap meet their tolerances; output \(\bar x^N\), or project or repair it when exact coupling feasibility is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted averages of dual subproblem solutions preserve block feasibility and average coupling residuals; projection or repair may still be needed for exact feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every \(X_i\) is convex and each \(x_i^k\in X_i\).
All weights satisfy \(w_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_i^N\in X_i\) and \(r(\bar x^N)\) equals the weighted average of iteration residuals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging identities are correct and do not overclaim convergence, but the algorithmic recovery and stopping prescription lacks a source; the primal-dual gap is also not defined for a generally infeasible averaged point.

children.title: Bound–Recovery Gap
children.top_down_role: Structural causes of separation between strong dual bounds and usable primal candidates.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with primal feasible set \(F\).
A Lagrangian procedure supplies a valid lower bound \(L\), and recovery supplies either \(\hat x\in F\) or no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound–recovery gap is \(G=U-L\), where \(U=f(\hat x)\) when \(\hat x\in F\), and \(U=+\infty\) when recovery produces no feasible point. Weak duality gives \(G\ge 0\). A finite \(G\le \varepsilon\) certifies that \(\hat x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal relative to the Lagrangian bound; \(G=0\) certifies optimality whenever both values are attained.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard minimization bound-gap convention for Lagrangian relaxation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the minimization convention; maximization reverses the roles of upper and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with objective \(f\), let \(L\) be a valid Lagrangian lower bound. If primal recovery returns \(\hat x\in F\), set \(U=f(\hat x)\); otherwise set \(U=+\infty\). The bound–recovery gap is \[G:=U-L.\] By weak duality, \(G\ge 0\). If \(G\le \varepsilon<+\infty\), then \(f(\hat x)-f^\star\le \varepsilon\); thus the recovered point and bound jointly form an \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, subtract the Lagrangian lower bound from the recovered feasible value. A finite gap bounds the recovered point’s suboptimality; zero gap certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Recovery Gap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization gap definition and epsilon-optimality implication are mathematically consistent and fit the Bound–Recovery Gap leaf, but the record cites no inspectable source. The inventory does not identify a section specifically supporting this Lagrangian bound-recovery certificate.

assumptions_latex: The block-structured primal and its dual are feasible finite-dimensional linear programs with finite optimal values.
All subproblem polyhedra admit finite extreme-point and extreme-ray representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the coefficient pairing induced by LP duality, every Benders feasibility or optimality cut generated from a dual subproblem extreme ray or point is the dual constraint associated with the corresponding Dantzig–Wolfe ray or column. Conversely, every generated Dantzig–Wolfe column induces the paired Benders inequality. Hence full cut generation and full column generation describe dual master LPs with equal optimal values.
review_flags: exact primal-dual orientation depends on the chosen block-LP convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP correspondence, including feasibility rays and optimality columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a block-structured LP and form Benders decomposition by projecting designated subproblem variables from the primal. Form Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition of the dual LP using the corresponding block polyhedra. Under the primal–dual coefficient pairing, a subproblem extreme point producing a Benders optimality cut indexes the paired Dantzig–Wolfe column constraint, while an extreme ray producing a Benders feasibility cut indexes the paired recession column. Consequently, after all required points and rays are included, \(M_B\) and \(M_{DW}\) are LP duals and satisfy \[\operatorname{val}(M_B)=\operatorname{val}(M_{DW}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a block LP, primal Benders cuts correspond to columns in a Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition of the dual; the completed master problems are LP duals with equal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders–Dantzig–Wolfe Primal–Dual Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind fits the correspondence leaf, but the exact pairing among Benders optimality cuts, feasibility rays, Dantzig–Wolfe columns, and recession columns depends on the block-LP formulation and sign convention. No cited decomposition source establishes the stated bidirectional correspondence or the claim that the completed masters are LP duals.

assumptions_latex: The polytope \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
The system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\), is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual bound equals the optimal value of the Dantzig–Wolfe convexification master. If \(X=\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\) denotes the relevant generating points, the master is \(\min\{\sum_j c^\top v^j\theta_j:\sum_j Av^j\theta_j=b,\sum_j\theta_j=1,\theta\ge0\}\), and its LP dual is the Lagrangian maximization with the corresponding normalization multiplier.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: LP duality between Lagrangian relaxation and the Dantzig–Wolfe convexification master
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality for a feasible bounded finite-dimensional polyhedral convexification master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\), define \(q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(b-Ax)\}\). If \(X\) is compact and its convex hull is polyhedral, then LP strong duality yields \[\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q(\lambda)=\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\}.\] Writing \(x=\sum_j v^j\theta_j\), with \(\theta\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\theta_j=1\), gives the Dantzig–Wolfe master; therefore its value is exactly the Lagrangian dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best Lagrangian bound for the linking equations equals the Dantzig–Wolfe master value obtained by replacing the subproblem set with its convex hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–Dantzig–Wolfe Bound Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated equality between the Lagrangian bound and the Dantzig–Wolfe convexification value is standard and the duality kind fits the leaf. However, no inspectable source is cited for the precise compact-polyhedral hypotheses and formulation.

assumptions_latex: A primal–dual LP pair is represented by mutually paired rows and columns.
Restricted problems retain primal and dual feasibility conventions consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated dual inequality found by separation is equivalent, under LP duality, to a primal column having improving reduced cost. Dually, an improving dual column corresponds to a violated primal inequality. Thus adding a cutting plane on one side and generating its paired column on the other are transpose operations, although their intermediate restricted-master iterates need not have identical objective values.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of the candidate column

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: row-column symmetry under finite-dimensional LP duality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic symmetry of LP row and column generation, not identity of algorithmic trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) solve a restricted dual master and let a missing primal column have coefficients \(a_j\) and cost \(c_j\). Its reduced cost is \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^\top y\). For minimization, pricing finds \(\bar c_j<0\), equivalently a violation of the omitted dual inequality \(a_j^\top y\le c_j\). Hence inserting the improving primal column is dual to inserting that violated inequality as a cutting plane. Applying the same argument to the dual exchanges rows and columns, establishing cutting-plane–column-generation symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-reduced-cost column is exactly a violated constraint in the paired dual. Column generation and cutting-plane generation are therefore row-column dual operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Plane–Column-Generation Symmetry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost identity correctly expresses the row-column dual symmetry for a minimization LP, and duality is an appropriate content kind. The record nevertheless lacks a cited source with a section or theorem locator supporting the cutting-plane/column-generation correspondence.

children.title: Optimization Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces returning optimizing solutions over an implicit feasible region.

assumptions_latex: The query set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
The linear objective vector \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) is supplied with each query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns an optimizer and optimal value when the infimum is attained and finite; it returns an infeasibility or unboundedness status otherwise. An approximate oracle with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) may return \(x_\varepsilon\in K\) satisfying \(c^\top x_\varepsilon\le\inf_{x\in K}c^\top x+\varepsilon\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization oracle over a fixed finite-dimensional set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimization oracle for \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) accepts \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and solves \[\inf_{x\in K}c^\top x.\] If the value is finite and attained, it returns \(x^\star\in\arg\min_{x\in K}c^\top x\) and \(c^\top x^\star\). It otherwise reports emptiness or unboundedness when the oracle model supports those statuses. An \(\varepsilon\)-optimization oracle may instead return \(x_\varepsilon\in K\) whose objective is at most \(\varepsilon\) above the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a linear objective, an optimization oracle minimizes it over a fixed set and returns an optimizer, or an appropriate infeasible or unbounded status.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this leaf, and the exact and additive-approximation formulations are coherent. An authoritative oracle-model source is still required, particularly for the optional emptiness and unboundedness status conventions.

children.title: Separation Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces identifying violated inequalities or certifying their absence.

assumptions_latex: The query point is \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), and the target set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle either confirms \(z\in K\) or returns \((a,\beta)\) with \(a\ne0\) such that \(a^\top x\le\beta<a^\top z\) for every \(x\in K\). This inequality is a directly checkable separating cut. A weak oracle replaces strict separation by a prescribed rational tolerance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard strong separation oracle for closed convex sets
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation oracle; weak separation requires an explicit tolerance and encoding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strong separation oracle for a closed convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) accepts \(z\in\mathbb R^n\). It either certifies \(z\in K\) or returns \(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \[a^\top x\le\beta<a^\top z\qquad\text{for every }x\in K.\] The returned inequality is valid for \(K\) and violated by \(z\), so it can be inserted as a cutting plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation oracle either confirms membership in a closed convex set or returns a valid linear inequality that the query point violates.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong-separation definition is mathematically standard for a closed convex set and fits the terminal container. No source reference with a definition, theorem, section, or page locator is attached.

children.title: Pricing Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces searching for columns with improving master contributions.

assumptions_latex: A minimization restricted master supplies a dual multiplier vector \(y\).
Each admissible column \(j\in J\) has cost \(c_j\) and master coefficient vector \(a_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing oracle computes \(j^\star\in\arg\min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^\top y)\). If its minimum reduced cost is negative, the returned column can improve the current restricted master; if the minimum is nonnegative, no omitted column violates the paired dual inequalities, certifying optimality for the full LP whenever the restricted master is feasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard reduced-cost pricing oracle for LP column generation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pricing for a minimization LP; signs reverse under a maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given restricted-master dual multipliers \(y\), a pricing oracle solves \[\min_{j\in J}\bar c_j,\qquad \bar c_j:=c_j-a_j^\top y.\] If the minimum is negative, it returns an index \(j^\star\) and the associated improving column \(a_{j^\star}\). If the minimum is nonnegative, every omitted dual inequality \(a_j^\top y\le c_j\) is satisfied. Provided the restricted master is feasible, this nonnegativity certificate establishes optimality for the full master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over all admissible columns. A negative result supplies an improving column; a nonnegative minimum certifies that no omitted column can improve the LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost pricing definition and the full-master optimality conclusion are consistent under the stated minimization convention. The claim still requires a column-generation source specifying the feasibility and duality conditions; none is cited.

children.title: Oracle-Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation conditions under which oracle capabilities can be transferred.

assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured in the bit model for rational finite-dimensional convex data.
The target convex body has known inner and outer radius bounds and admits tolerance-controlled oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial-time reductions between weak optimization and weak separation require convexity, rational accuracy control, polynomially bounded encoding length, and geometric well-boundedness. These reductions do not by themselves equate exact oracles, nonconvex-set oracles, unrestricted integer optimization, or models lacking radius and precision bounds; in those regimes an oracle may reveal strictly less information or require superpolynomial encoding.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bit-complexity boundary for optimization-separation equivalence
precise weak-oracle theorem and source locator required
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of polynomial oracle equivalence, not a claim that all exact oracle models coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational convex body \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(B(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(a,R)\), weak optimization and weak separation are polynomial-time interreducible when \(\log(R/r)\), input encoding, and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) are polynomially bounded. The equivalence boundary is crossed if convexity, geometric well-boundedness, or controlled rational tolerance is removed. In particular, this theorem does not imply polynomial equivalence for exact real-arithmetic answers, arbitrary nonconvex sets, unrestricted discrete sets, or outputs requiring exponentially many bits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimization and separation are polynomially equivalent only in controlled convex bit models. Exact, nonconvex, badly scaled, or uncontrolled-precision oracle models fall outside that equivalence theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct role for this leaf, but weak optimization/separation equivalence depends on precise oracle definitions, rational encodings, radius data, and accuracy transformations. No theorem-level source is cited, so the stated boundary and exclusions cannot be reliably validated.

children.title: Adapted Decisions
children.top_down_role: Decision representations organized by available information at each stage.

assumptions_latex: A filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) describes information revealed through time.
For each stage \(t\), decisions take values in a measurable space \((X_t,\mathcal X_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A decision process is adapted precisely when every \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t/\mathcal X_t\)-measurable.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports adapted stochastic decisions.
A stochastic-process or multistage stochastic-programming source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time decisions adapted to the model's information filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decision process \(x=(x_t)_{t=0}^T\) is adapted to \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) if, for every \(t\), the random element \(x_t:\Omega\to X_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t/\mathcal X_t\)-measurable; equivalently, \[x_t^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F_t\qquad\text{for every }B\in\mathcal X_t.\] Hence the stage-\(t\) decision may depend on information available by stage \(t\), but not on distinctions between outcomes that \(\mathcal F_t\) does not reveal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision process is adapted when each stage decision is measurable with respect to the information available at that stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Adapted Decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of adaptedness is standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Implementable Decisions
children.top_down_role: Decision representations compatible with realizable information access.

assumptions_latex: A filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) specifies the information available to the decision maker.
Each feasible decision set \(D_t(\omega)\subseteq X_t\) is prescribed at stage \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Implementability requires both information compatibility and pointwise feasibility: \(x_t\in\mathcal F_t\) measurably and \(x_t(\omega)\in D_t(\omega)\) almost surely.
review_flags: Implementability terminology varies across stochastic-programming sources.
No supplied locator establishes the selected information-and-feasibility convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementability means observable-information dependence plus feasibility, not merely measurability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decision process \(x=(x_t)_{t=0}^T\) is implementable for the stated model if, for every stage \(t\), (i) \(x_t:\Omega\to X_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable with respect to the specified decision-space sigma-algebra, and (ii) \[x_t(\omega)\in D_t(\omega)\quad\text{for }\mathbb P\text{-almost every }\omega.\] Thus an implementable rule is adapted and satisfies the stagewise feasibility restrictions. A rule using future information, or an adapted rule violating \(D_t(\omega)\), is not implementable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implementable decision uses only currently available information and belongs to the applicable feasible set almost surely at every stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Implementable Decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is coherent, but “implementable” is convention-dependent and no source supports the chosen combination of adaptedness and almost-sure feasibility.

children.title: History-Measurable Decisions
children.top_down_role: Decision representations indexed by distinguishable observed histories.

assumptions_latex: The observed history at stage \(t\) is a measurable map \(H_t:\Omega\to\mathcal H_t\).
The available information is \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H_t)\), and \(X_t\) is a standard Borel space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stage decision is history-measurable exactly when it factors measurably through \(H_t\).

notation.meaning: Decision rule as a function of history

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the history-factorization statement.
The standard-Borel factorization version requires an appropriate probability reference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-based realization of adapted decisions in standard Borel decision spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stage-\(t\) decision \(x_t:\Omega\to X_t\) is history-measurable if there exists a measurable map \(\phi_t:\mathcal H_t\to X_t\) such that \[x_t(\omega)=\phi_t(H_t(\omega))\quad\text{for }\mathbb P\text{-almost every }\omega.\] Under \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H_t)\) and the standard Borel assumption on \(X_t\), this factorization is equivalent, up to almost-sure equality, to \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurability of \(x_t\). Therefore decisions with identical observed histories receive identical values, modulo null sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision is history-measurable when it can be written as a measurable function of the observations available by that stage.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Measurable Decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The history-factorization formulation fits the leaf, but the almost-sure factorization equivalence and its measurable-space hypotheses require a specific source locator.

children.title: Information-Compatibility Crosswalk

assumptions_latex: At stage \(t\), information is represented by \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H_t)\).
In a finite scenario tree, two scenarios share a stage-\(t\) node exactly when their histories \(H_t\) agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptedness, history factorization, and nodewise constancy are equivalent descriptions of information compatibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crosswalk among filtration, observed-history, and finite scenario-tree formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stage-\(t\) decision, the following descriptions are equivalent under the stated assumptions: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable; there is a measurable \(\phi_t\) with \(x_t=\phi_t\circ H_t\) almost surely; and, in the finite scenario representation, \[n_t(\omega)=n_t(\omega')\;\Longrightarrow\;x_t^\omega=x_t^{\omega'}.\] The first is filtration language, the second is history language, and the third is nonanticipativity or node-consensus language.
