knowledge_statements.title: Parameterization Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient algebraic compatibility condition linking scenario metrics, consensus aggregation, dual balance, and multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite and let \(W_s=p_sM_s\succ0\) act on a common finite-dimensional decision space. One compatible metric parameterization uses \[z^+=\left(\sum_{s\in S}W_s\right)^{-1}\sum_{s\in S}W_sx_s^+,\qquad y_s^+=y_s+W_s(x_s^+-z^+),\] with initial balance \(\sum_{s\in S}y_s^0=0\). The projection identity gives \(\sum_{s\in S}W_s(x_s^+-z^+)=0\), and hence \(\sum_{s\in S}y_s^+=0\). Thus these coupled choices preserve dual balance and derive the scenario metric, aggregation, and multiplier steps from the same weighted consensus parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient compatibility convention is to use the same scenario weights in the metric consensus average and multiplier increments; this preserves balanced dual variables.

\(W_s=p_sM_s\) is positive definite for every \(s\in S\).
All variables lie in a common finite-dimensional decision space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{s\in S}y_s^k=0\) is invariant under the displayed compatible updates.

children.title: Scenario Bundling
children.top_down_role: Aggregation of scenarios into coordinated computational blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Bundling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition obtained by partitioning scenarios and solving each bundle jointly before global consensus aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B\) be a partition of the finite scenario set \(S\). A scenario-bundled decomposition replaces individual scenario blocks by bundle blocks. For \(B\in\mathcal B\), define \(p_B=\sum_{s\in B}p_s\) and the normalized bundle objective \[F_B(x_B)=\sum_{s\in B}\frac{p_s}{p_B}f_s(x_s)+\delta_{\mathcal N_B}(x_B),\] where \(\mathcal N_B\) imposes the nonanticipativity relations represented inside bundle \(B\). Progressive hedging then solves one penalized subproblem per bundle and enforces the remaining cross-bundle consensus relations through aggregation and multipliers. Singleton bundles recover scenario-wise decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario bundling partitions scenarios into jointly solved blocks, enforces nonanticipativity inside each block, and leaves remaining agreement constraints to global consensus updates.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) is a disjoint partition of \(S\).
Every bundle has \(p_B>0\).
\(\mathcal N_B\) contains exactly the internal nonanticipativity constraints assigned to bundle \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B=\{\{s\}:s\in S\}\) recovers scenario-wise decomposition.

notation.meaning: partition of scenarios into computational bundles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible, but no citation supports the specialized bundle objective or the division between internal and cross-bundle nonanticipativity constraints. Those conventions materially determine the formulation, so a scenario-bundling source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Scenario Grouping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural or statistical bases for forming scenario groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Grouping Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition and history-compatibility conditions for mathematically valid scenario grouping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A grouping map \(b:S\to\mathcal B\) is admissible when its nonempty fibers form a partition and every equality imposed within a bundle respects information histories. Specifically, if the bundled formulation identifies stage-\(t\) decisions of scenarios \(s\) and \(s'\), then it must satisfy \[h_t(s)=h_t(s').\] Scenarios with different histories may share a computational bundle, but their stage decisions must remain distinct unless the original model imposes their equality. Similarity scores based on data, probability, or solution behavior may select the partition, but they cannot override this history-compatibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grouping may use similarity or workload criteria, but any decision equality created within a bundle must coincide with an equality required by scenario histories.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite scenario set with history maps \(h_t\).
The original nonanticipativity relation equates decisions exactly at common histories.
Every scenario is assigned to one nonempty bundle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An imposed equality \(x_{s,t}=x_{s',t}\) is valid only if \(h_t(s)=h_t(s')\).

notation.meaning: information history of scenario s at stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated restriction is plausible for equality constraints introduced by a bundled formulation, but no source is supplied. A precise scenario-tree or bundling reference is required to verify the claimed admissibility condition and its scope.

children.title: Dynamic Bundle Reconfiguration
children.top_down_role: Changes to scenario partitions during computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Bundle Reconfiguration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive repartitioning of scenarios during bundled progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\), and let \(\mathcal B^k\) partition \(S\). Initialize scenario decisions and multipliers, and choose a deterministic reconfiguration rule \(R\). At iteration \(k\), solve each bundle subproblem using the current penalties and multipliers; recover decisions \(x_s^{k+1}\); and compute \(\bar x^{k+1}=\sum_{s\in S}p_sx_s^{k+1}\). Set \(\mathcal B^{k+1}=R(\mathcal B^k,\{x_s^{k+1}\}_{s\in S},\{w_s^k\}_{s\in S})\), preserving every scenario and its multiplier when bundles change. Then update \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Stop when the prescribed primal and multiplier criteria hold; output \(\bar x^{k+1}\) and the final partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly repartition scenarios from current disagreement data, while preserving scenario probabilities and multipliers, then continue progressive-hedging updates until the chosen stopping tests hold.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(\rho>0\), and every \(\mathcal B^k\) is a partition of \(S\).
Bundle solves return scenario-level decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B^{k+1}\) remains a scenario partition and the progressive-hedging state remains well defined across reconfiguration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no evidence supports this dynamic bundled-PH procedure. The rule R must explicitly map each valid partition and state to a valid partition; bundle subproblems and scenario-level recovery also require authoritative specification.

children.title: Parallel Progressive Hedging
children.top_down_role: Concurrent scenario-subproblem execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Progressive Hedging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous scenario-parallel implementation of one progressive-hedging iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(S\), probabilities \(p_s>0\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and initial \(\bar x^0,w_s^0\), iteration \(k\) dispatches independently, for every \(s\in S\), \[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] After all workers synchronize, compute \(\bar x^{k+1}=\sum_{s\in S}p_sx_s^{k+1}\) and update in parallel \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Stop when all required scenario solves have returned and the prescribed residual test holds; output \(\bar x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve all scenario subproblems concurrently, synchronize their decisions, form the probability-weighted consensus, update scenario multipliers concurrently, and stop on a specified residual test.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each displayed scenario subproblem attains a minimizer.
Workers use the same iteration state before synchronization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parallel step produces the same iterate as the corresponding synchronous serial scenario loop, up to solver tie-breaking.

The formula also represents a common-consensus, effectively two-stage setting rather than general multistage nonanticipativity.

children.title: Randomized Progressive Hedging
children.top_down_role: Randomized scenario, block, or coordination selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Progressive Hedging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random block activation applied to scenario-wise progressive-hedging updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite and let \(A_k\subseteq S\) be sampled at iteration \(k\), with every scenario having positive conditional activation probability. Given \(\bar x^k,w^k\), solve the progressive-hedging subproblem for each \(s\in A_k\): \[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right\};\] set \(x_s^{k+1}=x_s^k\) for \(s\notin A_k\). Compute \(\bar x^{k+1}=\sum_sp_sx_s^{k+1}\), and update \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Stop using a residual test evaluated on a state containing current values for every scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly activate scenario blocks, retain inactive decisions, recompute consensus from the complete current state, and update multipliers; every scenario must remain eligible for activation.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(\Pr(s\in A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)>0\) for every scenario.
Activated scenario subproblems attain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration defines a randomized full-state progressive-hedging update; convergence requires additional sampling and convexity hypotheses.

notation.meaning: history available before iteration k sampling

children.title: Asynchronous Progressive Hedging
children.top_down_role: Coordination with delayed or unsynchronized scenario information.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Progressive Hedging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed, worker-driven scenario updates with bounded-staleness state reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker event \(k\) activate scenario \(s_k\) and read a delayed consensus \(\bar x^{\tau_k}\), where \(0\le k-\tau_k\le D\). It computes \[x_{s_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_{s_k}}\left\{f_{s_k}(x)+\langle w_{s_k}^{\tau_k},x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^{\tau_k}\rVert^2\right\},\] while other scenario decisions retain their latest values. An atomic coordinator recomputes \(\bar x^{k+1}=\sum_sp_sx_s^{k+1}\) and updates the activated multiplier using the accepted decision. Each scenario must be activated infinitely often. Stop only from a consistent snapshot satisfying the prescribed residual test; output its consensus decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve scenario subproblems from boundedly stale states, while a coordinator atomically incorporates decisions; termination must use a consistent global snapshot.
assumptions_latex: Delays satisfy \(0\le k-\tau_k\le D<\infty\).
Every scenario is activated infinitely often.
Coordinator writes are atomic and accepted updates are not lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The event sequence defines an asynchronous progressive-hedging execution; convergence is not implied without further analytic conditions.

notation.meaning: scenario activated at worker event k
iteration index of the delayed state read

children.title: Execution-Regime Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Boundaries for combining parallelism, randomization, or asynchrony.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution-Regime Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-consistency conditions separating synchronous, randomized, and asynchronous executions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution regime is compatible with a scenario-wise progressive-hedging state \(z^k=(x^k,\bar x^k,w^k)\) if: \(\bar x^k=\sum_sp_sx_s^k\) whenever a residual is evaluated; each accepted scenario result is paired with the state version used to compute it; multiplier updates use that accepted decision and a declared consensus version; no accepted update is silently lost; and every scenario required by the regime is eventually processed. Synchronous parallel execution additionally requires a barrier before consensus formation. Randomized execution requires positive persistent activation probabilities. Asynchronous execution requires a stated delay model and atomic state incorporation. These conditions establish semantic compatibility, not convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible executions preserve complete, versioned scenario state, form consensus consistently, avoid lost updates, and ensure scenario coverage; each execution regime adds its own synchronization or activation requirements.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_sp_s=1\).
Every scenario result carries an identifiable state version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residuals and multiplier updates have an unambiguous progressive-hedging interpretation under the stated execution regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Integer Progressive Hedging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive hedging applied to mixed-integer scenario subproblems without a global-convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenario feasible sets \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) containing designated integer coordinates, initialize \(w_s^0\) with \(\sum_sp_sw_s^0=0\), choose \(\rho>0\), and set \(\bar x^0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert^2\right\},\] form \(\bar x^{k+1}=\sum_sp_sx_s^{k+1}\), and set \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Stop on consensus, an iteration limit, or stagnation. Return a feasible nonanticipative integer incumbent only after a separate repair or fixing step verifies membership in every relevant \(X_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply progressive-hedging subproblems to mixed-integer scenarios, but treat the result as heuristic and return an incumbent only after explicit nonanticipativity and feasibility checks.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(\sum_sp_s=1\).
Each \(X_s\) enforces its declared integrality restrictions.
Scenario subproblems are solved to the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure supplies candidate integer decisions but, without additional global search, supplies no certificate of global optimality.

notation.meaning: mixed-integer feasible set for scenario s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the heuristic-integer-PH leaf and the absence of a global-optimality claim is appropriate. An authoritative integer-PH source is nevertheless required, especially for the stopping, repair, and incumbent-validation boundary.

children.title: Progressive-Hedging Search Guidance
children.top_down_role: Use of hedging information to guide discrete search.

knowledge_statements.title: Progressive-Hedging Search Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Using scenario disagreement as branching guidance rather than as a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node, let \(x_{s,j}\) be the progressive-hedging value of integer coordinate \(j\) in scenario \(s\), and define \(d_j=\sum_sp_s\lvert x_{s,j}-\bar x_j\rvert\), where \(\bar x_j=\sum_sp_sx_{s,j}\). A search-guidance rule may select an unfixed coordinate from \(\operatorname*{argmax}_j d_j\), optionally breaking ties by objective impact, and branch on admissible integer disjunctions for that coordinate. The score \(d_j\) measures scenario disagreement only: it is neither a node lower bound nor a proof that the selected branch improves the search tree. All pruning decisions must therefore use independently valid bounds or infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario disagreement can rank integer branching candidates, but it cannot justify pruning; valid bounds or infeasibility certificates must control all eliminations.
assumptions_latex: Candidate coordinates are integer and not fixed at the current search node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_j\) is admissible as a branching score but not as a global-bound certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Principle fits the search-guidance leaf, and the distinction between a score and a bound is sound. No source supports this particular disagreement score or its use in PH-guided branching, and admissible disjunction construction is left unspecified.

children.title: Branch-Bound Tree Integration
children.top_down_role: Placement of scenario coordination within a search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Bound Tree Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding heuristic progressive hedging within globally valid branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a branch-and-bound queue with the original mixed-integer stochastic program and incumbent value \(U=+\infty\). At each node \(N\), compute a valid relaxation lower bound \(L_N\). Prune only if the relaxation is infeasible or \(L_N\ge U\). Otherwise run a bounded progressive-hedging heuristic under the node fixings; if repair yields a feasible nonanticipative integer point \(x^N\), set \(U=\min\{U,F(x^N)\}\). Choose a valid integer disjunction, possibly using progressive-hedging disagreement, and enqueue the children. Stop when the queue is empty or the certified gap meets tolerance. Output the incumbent and the minimum active-node lower bound; progressive-hedging values never replace relaxation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use progressive hedging to find incumbents and guide branching, while ordinary valid relaxations provide node bounds and all pruning certificates.
assumptions_latex: Every branching disjunction covers the node's integer-feasible set.
Each \(L_N\) is a valid lower bound for node \(N\).
Incumbents are accepted only after full feasibility verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the queue is exhausted, the returned incumbent is globally optimal; with early stopping, its certified gap uses only valid node lower bounds.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the PH/branch-and-bound integration and certification claim have no cited evidence. Global optimality on queue exhaustion additionally requires exact coverage, valid fathoming, and correct treatment of integral nodes and infeasibility.

children.title: Hybrid Bound Certification
children.top_down_role: Validity of bounds produced by the integrated hybrid.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Bound Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid optimality-gap certificate for a progressive-hedging and branch-and-bound hybrid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(x^I\) be a verified feasible nonanticipative integer solution with \(U=F(x^I)<+\infty\). Let \(\mathcal Q\) be the active branch-and-bound nodes, and for each \(N\in\mathcal Q\) let \(L_N\) be a proved lower bound on every feasible completion in \(N\). If fathomed nodes have valid infeasibility, integrality, or bound certificates, then \(L=\min_{N\in\mathcal Q}L_N\) is a global lower bound, with \(L=U\) when \(\mathcal Q=\varnothing\). Consequently \(0\le U-F^\star\le U-L\). Progressive-hedging augmented objective values may contribute only when separately proved to be valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and independently valid bounds for every remaining search node certify the global gap; raw progressive-hedging objectives do not.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimum \(F^\star\).
The active and fathomed nodes cover the original feasible set.
Every reported incumbent and node bound has been independently verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\) is a valid absolute global-optimality-gap certificate.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for active node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is the correct kind and the gap inequality is standard under valid coverage and bounds. No source is supplied, and the special convention L=U for an empty active set is valid only after all nodes have been soundly fathomed and the incumbent accounting is complete.

children.title: Nonconvex Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated nonconvergent behavior in nonconvex scenario coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-scenario binary example exhibiting a period-two progressive-hedging orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two scenarios have probabilities \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), feasible sets \(X_1=X_2=\{0,1\}\), zero objectives, and penalty \(\rho>0\). Use the update \(x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}}\{w_s^kx+\frac{\rho}{2}(x-\bar x^k)^2\}\), followed by averaging and multiplier updating. Initialize \((x_1^0,x_2^0)=(0,1)\), \(\bar x^0=1/2\), and \((w_1^0,w_2^0)=(-\rho/4,\rho/4)\). Then the next scenario vector is \((1,0)\), the multipliers become \((\rho/4,-\rho/4)\), and the following update returns exactly to the initial full state. Thus the iterates form a nonconsensual period-two cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-cost two-scenario binary problem cycles forever between opposite scenario decisions, showing that nonconvex progressive hedging need not converge.
assumptions_latex: Scenario subproblem ties, if any, follow the displayed strict minimizers.
The consensus and multiplier updates are performed synchronously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,\bar x^k,w^k)\) has period two and never reaches scenario consensus.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Counterexample is the exact appropriate kind. The displayed arithmetic does produce the claimed strict period-two orbit, but the record has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale satisfying the evidence contract.

children.title: Missing Global Certificates
children.top_down_role: Absence of globally valid optimality evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Global Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why heuristic integer progressive hedging alone does not certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonconvex or mixed-integer stochastic minimization problem, a progressive-hedging state consisting of scenario minimizers, multipliers, a consensus vector, and small residuals does not by itself certify global optimality. Consensus and feasibility can verify an incumbent and hence an upper bound \(U\), but the penalized scenario objectives depend on algorithmic multipliers and quadratic penalties and are not automatically a global lower bound. A global gap certificate requires an independently valid \(L\le F^\star\), obtained, for example, from a relaxation or exhaustive search. Without such an \(L\), neither termination, stagnation, cycling detection, nor zero consensus residual establishes \(U=F^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer progressive hedging may verify a feasible incumbent, but its residuals and penalized objectives do not supply the lower bound needed for global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region or objective is nonconvex.
No independent globally valid lower bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite progressive-hedging run cannot certify a global optimality gap solely from its heuristic state.

notation.meaning: objective value of a verified feasible incumbent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct kind and the separation between an incumbent upper bound and an independently valid lower bound is appropriate. The nontrivial claim about what integer PH states cannot certify lacks authoritative evidence.

children.title: Cycling Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable signatures distinguishing cycling from slow progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycling Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact repeated-state certificate for deterministic progressive-hedging cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a deterministic progressive-hedging implementation define a state transition \(z^{k+1}=T(z^k)\), where \(z^k\) contains all scenario decisions, multipliers, consensus values, penalty parameters, bundle assignments, and deterministic solver tie-breaking state. If stored iterates satisfy \(z^j=z^k\) for some \(j<k\), then determinism gives \(z^{j+r}=z^{k+r}\) for every \(r\ge0\); hence the subsequent orbit is periodic with period dividing \(k-j\). If some state in this cycle has nonzero consensus residual, the execution cannot converge to consensus while it remains under the same transition map. Approximate recurrence within a tolerance is only a diagnostic warning, not an exact cycling certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a deterministic implementation, exact repetition of the complete state certifies a periodic orbit; approximate repetition is only a warning.
assumptions_latex: The transition map \(T\) is deterministic and unchanged between iterations \(j\) and \(k\).
The recorded state includes every variable affecting future updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^j=z^k\) certifies periodicity with a period dividing \(k-j\).

notation.meaning: complete algorithmic state at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate fits the exact-recurrence leaf, and deterministic repetition of a genuinely complete state implies periodicity. No source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied, while completeness of the recorded state is implementation-sensitive.

children.title: Heuristic-Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Separation between practical stopping evidence or global certification.

assumptions_latex: The scenario subproblems may contain integer variables, so their feasible sets need not be convex.
Progressive hedging is stopped by a user-specified iteration, time, residual, or stagnation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination under such a rule yields only a heuristic incumbent unless an independent valid bound closes the optimality gap.

notation.meaning: primal residual measuring disagreement of scenario decisions
best feasible incumbent value at iteration k
valid global lower bound, when available

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes practical stopping from globally certified termination in integer progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer or otherwise nonconvex progressive-hedging iteration, a stopping test such as \(k\geq K\), \(r^k\leq\varepsilon\), elapsed time exceeding \(T\), or insufficient incumbent improvement may terminate the computation. These tests certify only that the prescribed heuristic rule has fired. In particular, \(r^k=0\) establishes scenario agreement of the current decisions but does not establish global optimality. A valid \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate requires an independently justified global bound \(L^k\) satisfying \(U^k-L^k\leq\varepsilon\). Without such a bound, termination reports an incumbent and diagnostics, not a globally certified solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integer progressive hedging, iteration, time, residual, or stagnation stopping rules produce heuristic incumbents; global optimality requires a separate valid bound closing the gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-Termination Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical distinction are appropriate, but no source supports the integer/nonconvex progressive-hedging stopping and certification claims. A specialized source must confirm that residual agreement is not an optimality certificate and specify the conditions under which the stated incumbent-bound gap is valid.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Introduction to Stochastic Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Introduction to Stochastic Programming

assumptions_latex: The multistage stochastic linear program is represented by a finite scenario tree.
Every node subproblem has relatively complete recourse and finite optimal value.
Linear-programming dual solutions are available for descendant subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting root decision and recursively generated cuts constitute a stagewise nested Benders approximation of the multistage problem.

notation.meaning: stagewise recourse value at node n
polyhedral lower approximation of the recourse value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree linear nested Benders method with backward cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each nonterminal approximation \(\underline Q_n^0\) by a valid affine lower bound. At iteration \(k\), solve the root problem and recursively solve child problems using the current descendant approximations. For each visited nonterminal node \(n\), obtain optimal dual multipliers from the problems indexed by \(m\in C(n)\); aggregate their affine value-function minorants with the conditional child probabilities to form a cut \(\ell_n^k\leq Q_n\). Update \(\underline Q_n^{k+1}=\max\{\underline Q_n^k,\ell_n^k\}\) in backward stage order. Stop when the root upper and lower bounds satisfy the prescribed gap tolerance, and return the associated nonanticipative policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested Benders alternates forward node solves with backward, probability-weighted dual cuts that refine stagewise recourse approximations until the root bound gap is acceptable.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Nested Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the precise finite-tree nested-Benders procedure, probability-weighted cuts, root bounds, and policy-return claim have no citation. A source must identify the selected variant and its termination guarantees.

children.title: Quadratic Nested Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Nested decomposition with quadratic stage structure.

assumptions_latex: Each node model is convex and its recourse function admits valid affine lower cuts.
The stabilization matrix is positive semidefinite and the proximal parameter is positive.
Stabilization is applied only to trial-point selection, not to cut validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each trial point is obtained from a quadratically stabilized nested master while all retained affine cuts remain valid lower bounds.

notation.meaning: current stability center at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex nested Benders with nodewise proximal quadratic trial-point regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(n\) and iteration \(k\), compute a trial decision by minimizing the local stage cost plus \(\underline Q_n^k(x_n)\) and the term \(\tfrac12\|x_n-\bar x_n^k\|_{H_n}^2\) over the node-feasible set. Solve descendant problems at that trial decision, generate valid affine cuts, and append them to the corresponding stagewise approximations. Accept the trial decision as the new center when the realized improvement meets the prescribed serious-step test; otherwise retain \(\bar x_n^k\). Reduce, increase, or retain the stabilization weight according to the stated update rule. Terminate using valid root bounds, and output the incumbent policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic nested decomposition selects trial decisions with nodewise proximal terms, adds ordinary valid Benders cuts, and updates stability centers through serious and null steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Nested Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Quadratic Nested Decomposition, but the serious-step mechanism, nodewise proximal master, stabilization-weight updates, and valid-bound termination require a specialized source. The phrase “according to the stated update rule” does not actually specify a rule.

children.title: Stabilized Nested Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Stabilization mechanisms for nested master approximations.

assumptions_latex: The nested master problems are convex and possess valid lower models of downstream value functions.
Each stabilization term vanishes at its current center and is nonnegative elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stabilization changes the sequence of trial points but not the validity of the nested lower models or the original problem being solved.

notation.meaning: lower model of the node value function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic stabilization principle for convex stagewise nested decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stabilized nested-decomposition iteration chooses each node trial point by minimizing \(m_n^k(x)+S_n^k(x;\bar x_n^k)\), where \(S_n^k(x;\bar x_n^k)\geq0\) and \(S_n^k(\bar x_n^k;\bar x_n^k)=0\). Descendant solves are evaluated for the unstabilized stochastic program, and their dual information generates cuts for \(m_n^{k+1}\). Thus stabilization controls trial-point movement and may distinguish serious from null steps, but it must not be incorporated into cuts as though it were part of the original recourse function. Valid termination is based on bounds for the unstabilized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilization term regulates nested-decomposition trial points, while descendant evaluations, cuts, bounds, and termination must continue to refer to the original unstabilized problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Nested Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind is locally suitable, but nonnegativity and vanishing at the center alone do not characterize all stabilization properties needed by a convergent nested-decomposition method. A source must support the serious/null-step interpretation and the separation of stabilization from valid recourse cuts and bounds.

children.title: Quadratic Stabilization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of quadratic structure with stabilization choices.

assumptions_latex: The node decision space is finite-dimensional.
The stabilization matrix is symmetric positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic interface is a convex proximal regularizer with the stated value and gradient at the stability center.

notation.meaning: quadratic stabilization term at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nodewise metric and scaling conditions for quadratic stabilization.

source_refs.locator: 2.8 Variable metric methods p. 54
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic stabilization interface at node \(n\) has the form \[S_n^k(x;\bar x_n^k)=\frac{1}{2\tau_n^k}(x-\bar x_n^k)^{\mathsf T}H_n^k(x-\bar x_n^k),\] with \(\tau_n^k>0\) and \(H_n^k=(H_n^k)^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Consequently, \(S_n^k\) is convex, \(S_n^k(\bar x_n^k;\bar x_n^k)=0\), and \(\nabla_xS_n^k(\bar x_n^k;\bar x_n^k)=0\). If uniform control of trial displacement is required, impose \(0<\mu I\preceq H_n^k\preceq MI\) and keep \(\tau_n^k\) within stated positive bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic stabilization uses a positive scaling and positive-semidefinite metric; uniform positive-definite metric bounds provide controlled nodewise trial displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Stabilization Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8 Variable metric methods p. 54
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited variable-metric section plausibly supports the generic quadratic regularizer but does not establish its claimed interface with nested decomposition. The plain statement also omits the center value, zero-gradient conclusion, and bounded-metric conditions expressed in LaTeX. A directly relevant stabilization source is required.

assumptions_latex: A finite scenario-tree formulation has convex node feasible sets and integrable convex costs.
Copies of history-equivalent decisions are coupled by linear nonanticipativity equations.
A constraint qualification sufficient for strong convex duality holds when equality is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing nonanticipativity separates the scenario problems; the Lagrangian dual gives a lower bound, and under strong duality its supremum equals the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex finite-tree formulation obtained by dualizing nonanticipativity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the scenario-expanded multistage problem as \(v^*=\inf\{F(x):x\in X,\ Ax=0\}\), where \(X\) contains the scenario-local dynamics and feasibility constraints and \(Ax=0\) enforces nonanticipativity. Its Lagrangian dual function is \[g(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{F(x)+\langle\lambda,Ax\rangle\}.\] Because scenario copies are uncoupled after removing \(Ax=0\), this infimum decomposes by scenarios or scenario-tree branches. Weak duality gives \(g(\lambda)\leq v^*\) for every \(\lambda\). Under the stated convexity, closedness, and qualification assumptions, \(\sup_{\lambda}g(\lambda)=v^*\); otherwise the supremum remains a valid lower bound but may have a duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing nonanticipativity separates multistage scenario problems. The resulting dual always supplies lower bounds and equals the primal value under an appropriate convex constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Lagrangian Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Duality is the correct content kind, and weak duality is stated correctly for minimization. However, the exact closedness and constraint-qualification hypotheses needed for equality, and whether the chosen scenario-expanded formulation fully decomposes by scenarios or branches, require a specific source.

assumptions_latex: The multistage problem is convex with stagewise state transitions and finite conditional expectations.
At sampled states, child subproblems admit dual solutions producing valid affine lower bounds.
The chosen sampling law covers the relevant realizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface maintains cut-based lower approximations of Bellman functions and uses them in forward simulation and backward cut generation.

notation.meaning: Bellman cost-to-go function at stage t
cut-based lower approximation after iteration k
affine cut generated at stage t and iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex cut-based interface between nested decomposition and stochastic dual dynamic programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each downstream Bellman function by \(\underline V_t^k(s)=\max_{j\leq k}\ell_t^j(s)\leq V_t(s)\). A forward pass samples a realization path and selects feasible decisions using these approximations. A backward pass solves the stage subproblems at the visited predecessor states; dual multipliers define affine minorants for each sampled or enumerated realization, and conditional expectation produces a new cut \(\ell_t^{k+1}\). Updating by \(\underline V_t^{k+1}=\max\{\underline V_t^k,\ell_t^{k+1}\}\) preserves the lower-bound property. The current approximations provide a policy for simulation and a root lower bound, while independent forward simulation supplies statistical upper estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SDDP represents Bellman functions by maxima of affine lower cuts, using sampled forward decisions and backward dual information to refine those approximations.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits this interface, but the record selects a particular convex SDDP formulation without citing it. A source must support cut construction under conditional expectation, sampling coverage, preservation of lower bounds, and the interpretation of forward simulation as an upper estimate.

children.title: Recombining Scenario Trees
children.top_down_role: Scenario representations that merge equivalent histories.

assumptions_latex: A finite directed acyclic scenario structure is layered by stages.
Nodes carry information states, and arcs carry conditional transition probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structure is recombining exactly when distinct histories can enter a common later node whose future model depends only on that node's information state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-stage recombination defined through merging histories and Markov-sufficient node states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A recombining scenario tree is a stage-layered directed acyclic graph \(G=(N,E)\), with \(N=\bigcup_{t=0}^T N_t\), root \(N_0=\{r\}\), arcs only from \(N_t\) to \(N_{t+1}\), and probabilities \(p_{ij}\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}p_{ij}=1\). It is recombining when some node \(j\) has at least two distinct predecessors and all histories reaching \(j\) share the same information state, feasible continuation model, and conditional law of future uncertainty. Decisions assigned to \(j\) therefore depend on that common information state rather than on which predecessor history reached it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recombining scenario structure merges distinct histories at a node whenever they share the same decision-relevant state, continuation model, and conditional future law.
knowledge_statements.title: Recombining Scenario Trees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the object described is a recombining directed acyclic scenario graph rather than a tree in the strict graph-theoretic sense. A terminology source must establish the intended usage and the sufficiency conditions for merging histories.

children.title: Policy-Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph-based representations of recurring multistage states.

assumptions_latex: The stochastic control model has a finite horizon or an explicitly specified cyclic continuation rule.
Each graph node identifies a decision-information state and each outgoing arc identifies a possible transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible policy is represented by node decision rules satisfying local constraints and arcwise state transitions.

notation.meaning: decision rule attached to node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-and-arc representation of policies for multistage stochastic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A policy-graph representation consists of a directed graph \(G=(N,E)\), node labels specifying information states and local optimization models, arc labels specifying realizations or transition laws, and probabilities \(p_{nm}\) with \(\sum_{m:(n,m)\in E}p_{nm}=1\). A policy assigns to each node \(n\) a measurable decision rule \(\pi_n\) on that node's admissible state space. Along every reachable arc \((n,m)\), the decision \(\pi_n\) must satisfy the local constraints and induce an admissible successor state for \(m\). Nodes may have multiple predecessors, so histories with the same decision-relevant state can share one continuation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy graph stores decision-information states at nodes, stochastic transitions on arcs, and feasible node decision rules, allowing multiple histories to share a continuation policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Graph Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and local scope are appropriate, but the formal node, arc, probability, measurability, and shared-continuation requirements have no supporting citation. A policy-graph source is needed to fix the exact formalism.

children.title: Tree-to-Policy-Graph Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between recombining trees or policy graphs.

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite scenario tree with node data, conditional arc probabilities, and nonanticipative node decisions.
Two nodes are merged only when their information states and complete continuation subtrees are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient policy graph preserves feasible policies and their probability-weighted objective values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless quotient construction using decision-relevant continuation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(u\sim v\) for same-stage tree nodes when they have identical decision-information states, local feasible models and costs, and probability-preserving equivalent labeled continuations. Compute the equivalence classes backward from the leaves. Create one policy-graph node \([u]\) for each class and an arc \(([u],[v])\) for every tree arc \((u,v)\); combine duplicate arcs by summing their conditional probabilities. Attach the common node model to each class and identify the corresponding decision rules. Stop after processing the root stage. The translation is lossless under the equivalence predicate: every tree policy induces a graph policy, every graph policy lifts to a nonanticipative tree policy, and corresponding expected objective values agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward quotienting merges tree nodes with identical information, local models, and probability-preserving continuations, producing a policy graph that preserves policies and expected values.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-to-Policy-Graph Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the lossless quotient theorem requires a precise continuation-equivalence definition and source. Summing all duplicate quotient arcs can incorrectly multiply conditional probabilities when multiple equivalent parent representatives exist; probabilities must instead be defined per parent class and successor class under a lumpability or equivalent consistency condition.

assumptions_latex: The two-stage stochastic linear program has relatively complete recourse and finite expected cost.
An independent identically distributed sample of finite size is fixed before optimization.
Each sampled recourse problem admits a linear-programming dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L-shaped decomposition solves the fixed sample-average problem by adding valid sample-aggregated feasibility and optimality cuts.

notation.meaning: recourse value for sampled realization i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-sample two-stage linear SAA solved by the classical L-shaped method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given samples \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\), form \(\widehat F_N(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Q(x,\xi^i)\). Initialize a master problem in \((x,\theta)\) with first-stage constraints and a valid lower bound on \(\theta\). At a master solution \(x^k\), solve every sampled recourse problem. If one is infeasible, add a feasibility cut obtained from a dual ray. Otherwise, aggregate the dual optimal solutions into an affine cut \(\theta\geq\alpha_k+\beta_k^{\mathsf T}x\). Re-solve the master until its lower bound and the evaluated sample-average objective satisfy the prescribed gap tolerance; return the SAA optimizer and value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix an iid sample, solve its scenario recourse problems, and iteratively add aggregated L-shaped feasibility or optimality cuts until the SAA bound gap closes.
knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Average Approximation with L-Shaped Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but relatively complete recourse makes sampled recourse infeasibility—and hence feasibility cuts—unnecessary. A sourced version should either retain relatively complete recourse and describe only optimality cuts or relax that assumption and state the feasibility-cut conditions.

assumptions_latex: The objective is a convex two-stage expectation with unbiased sampled recourse information.
The master maintains valid cutting-plane lower models and a bounded sequence of trial decisions.
Sampling and step-size rules satisfy the method's stated consistency conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stochastic-decomposition iteration updates a sampled lower model and returns an incumbent selected by its prescribed statistical or model-based stopping rule.

notation.meaning: current lower model of expected recourse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic convex sampling-and-cut template; a named variant requires a more specific source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a feasible first-stage point \(x^0\) and a valid lower model \(m_0\) of expected recourse. At iteration \(k\), draw \(\xi^k\), solve the corresponding recourse problem at \(x^k\), and obtain sampled dual information defining an affine recourse cut. Incorporate that cut into \(m_{k+1}\) using the method's prescribed averaging, rescaling, or cut-retention rule. Choose \(x^{k+1}\) by minimizing the first-stage cost plus \(m_{k+1}\), possibly with stabilization, over the first-stage feasible set. Update an incumbent using sampled objective estimates. Stop only under the specified statistical or model-based criterion, and report the incumbent together with the sampling and bound diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic decomposition samples recourse information sequentially, updates a cut-based expected-recourse model, solves a master for new trials, and tracks a statistically assessed incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Decomposition Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is plausible, but the statement blends averaging, rescaling, cut retention, stabilization, and several stopping regimes from potentially different stochastic-decomposition variants. A named method and authoritative source are required before its update and termination claims can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Sequential Sampling
children.top_down_role: Progressive enlargement or refinement of sampled information.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential enlargement of an independent scenario sample for a two-stage stochastic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given batch sizes \(1\le N_1<N_2<\cdots\), draw nested i.i.d. samples \(S_k=\{\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^{N_k}\}\). At stage \(k\), solve the sample-average decomposition problem \[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\frac{1}{N_k}\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}Q(x,\xi^i)\right\}.\] Using an independent validation sample, compute an estimated optimality gap \(\widehat g_k\) and a valid error radius \(r_k\). Stop and return \(x_k\) when \(\widehat g_k+r_k\le\varepsilon\); otherwise increase the sample to \(S_{k+1}\) and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly enlarge an i.i.d. scenario sample, solve its decomposed sample-average problem, and stop when an independently validated optimality-gap upper bound meets the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and each displayed sample-average problem attains a minimizer.
The validation sample is independent of the sample used to compute \(x_k\).
The radius \(r_k\) has the stated confidence coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned decision satisfies the algorithmic stopping certificate \(\widehat g_k+r_k\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: nested scenario sample at stage k

children.title: Adaptive Scenario Sets
children.top_down_role: Data-dependent selection or revision of active scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Scenario Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive retention and augmentation of scenarios during decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite scenario set \(S_0\) and iteration counter \(k=0\). Solve the restricted decomposition problem on \(S_k\) to obtain \(x_k\). From a candidate pool \(C_k\), evaluate scores \(v(x_k,\xi)\ge0\), retain a prescribed subset \(R_k\subseteq S_k\), and select \(A_k\subseteq C_k\) containing scenarios with largest scores or scores above threshold \(\tau_k\). Set \(S_{k+1}=R_k\cup A_k\). Stop when \(A_k=\varnothing\) and the restricted problem meets its optimization tolerance; otherwise increment \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve on a finite scenario set, score candidate scenarios, retain useful existing scenarios, add influential candidates, and stop when none qualifies for addition.
assumptions_latex: Every \(S_k\) is finite and the restricted problem is solvable.
The score \(v(x,\xi)\) is computable for every candidate scenario.
The retention and addition rules are fixed before each update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update produces the explicitly determined finite set \(S_{k+1}=R_k\cup A_k\).

children.title: Sampling-to-Scenario Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Coupling between sequential evidence or scenario-set revision.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-to-Scenario Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts sampled diagnostic information into an active scenario-set update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\) solve the current restricted problem on \(S_k\), and draw a diagnostic sample \(D_k\) independently of the optimization sample conditional on the past. Given a measurable score \(v(x_k,\xi)\), define \[A_k=\{\xi\in D_k:v(x_k,\xi)>\tau_k\},\qquad S_{k+1}=R_k\cup A_k,\] where \(R_k\subseteq S_k\) is the retained set. Thus sampling information affects the next decomposition problem only through the measurable selection rule producing \(A_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnostic sample is converted into new active scenarios by a measurable score-and-threshold rule, then combined with retained scenarios.
assumptions_latex: The diagnostic sample \(D_k\) is conditionally independent of the optimization sample.
The score map \(\xi\mapsto v(x_k,\xi)\) is measurable.
The threshold \(\tau_k\) is determined from information available before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adapted set \(S_{k+1}\) is a measurable function of \(S_k\), \(D_k\), and the current decision \(x_k\).

children.title: Importance Sampling
children.top_down_role: Biased sampling designs paired with statistical correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Importance Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Change-of-measure representation for scenario expectations and decomposition estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the target scenario law and \(Q\) a proposal law satisfying \(P\ll Q\). For any measurable integrand \(h\) with \(\mathbb E_Q[|h(\xi)|w(\xi)]<\infty\), where \(w=dP/dQ\), \[\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]=\mathbb E_Q[w(\xi)h(\xi)].\] Hence, for i.i.d. draws \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\sim Q\), the estimator \(\widehat\mu_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^Nw(\xi^i)h(\xi^i)\) is unbiased for \(\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expectations under the target law equal weighted expectations under a dominating proposal law, yielding an unbiased weighted scenario estimator.
assumptions_latex: \(P\ll Q\).
The integrand is measurable and \(\mathbb E_Q[|h|w]<\infty\).
The sampled scenarios are i.i.d. under \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_Q[\widehat\mu_N]=\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\).

children.title: Variance-Reduction Devices
children.top_down_role: Devices for reducing estimator variability.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduction Devices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance comparison for unbiased scenario estimators under a common sampling budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be an unbiased square-integrable estimator of \(\mu\), and let \(Z\) be a square-integrable control variate with known mean \(m\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Z)>0\). For \(Y_\beta=Y-\beta(Z-m)\), \(\mathbb E[Y_\beta]=\mu\), and the choice \(\beta^*=\operatorname{Cov}(Y,Z)/\operatorname{Var}(Z)\) gives \[\operatorname{Var}(Y_{\beta^*})=\operatorname{Var}(Y)-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(Y,Z)^2}{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}\le\operatorname{Var}(Y).\] This supplies a variance-reduced scenario estimator without changing its expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimally weighted control variate preserves unbiasedness and reduces variance by the squared covariance divided by the control's variance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[Y]=\mu\) and \(\mathbb E[Z]=m\) is known.
\(\operatorname{Var}(Z)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator \(Y_{\beta^*}\) is unbiased and has variance no greater than \(Y\).

children.title: Rare-Scenario Emphasis
children.top_down_role: Sampling emphasis for low-probability influential scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Rare-Scenario Emphasis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposal-law condition ensuring rare target scenarios receive increased sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the target law, \(Q\) an importance-sampling proposal, and \(R\) a measurable rare-scenario set with \(0<P(R)<1\). The proposal emphasizes \(R\) by factor \(\kappa>1\) when \[Q(R)\ge\kappa P(R),\qquad P\ll Q.\] For an unbiased estimator, every sampled contribution is multiplied by \(w=dP/dQ\). If densities \(p\) and \(q\) exist, the stronger pointwise condition \(q(\xi)\ge\kappa p(\xi)\) for \(P\)-almost every \(\xi\in R\) implies \(w(\xi)\le1/\kappa\) on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposal emphasizes a rare set when it assigns that set at least a fixed multiple of its target probability while retaining likelihood-ratio correction.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is measurable and \(0<P(R)<1\).
\(P\ll Q\).
For the pointwise conclusion, \(P\) and \(Q\) possess densities under a common dominating measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rare scenarios occur more frequently under \(Q\), while weighting by \(dP/dQ\) preserves target expectations.

children.title: Statistical Optimality Bounds
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based bounds on solution quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Optimality Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-sample confidence bound for the optimality gap of a candidate decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\), and let \(\widehat U\) and \(\widehat L\) be statistics computed from validation data independent of the candidate decision \(\widehat x\). Suppose \(\mathbb P\{F(\widehat x)\le\widehat U\}\ge1-\alpha_U\) and \(\mathbb P\{z^*\ge\widehat L\}\ge1-\alpha_L\). Then the observable quantity \(B=\max\{0,\widehat U-\widehat L\}\) certifies \[\mathbb P\{F(\widehat x)-z^*\le B\}\ge1-\alpha_U-\alpha_L.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid upper bound on candidate performance minus a valid lower bound on the optimum yields a confidence bound on the optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: The candidate \(\widehat x\) is fixed relative to the validation data.
The stated one-sided coverage inequalities hold.
\(\alpha_U,\alpha_L\ge0\) and \(\alpha_U+\alpha_L<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is a \((1-\alpha_U-\alpha_L)\)-confidence upper certificate for the optimality gap.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: union-bound construction from one-sided statistical bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Out-of-Sample Validation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Independent evidence for performance beyond the construction sample.

knowledge_statements.title: Out-of-Sample Validation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample performance certificate using validation observations independent of model fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat x\) be chosen without using validation observations \(Y_i=f(\widehat x,\xi^i)\), where \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m\) are i.i.d. and \(Y_i\in[a,b]\) almost surely. Define \(\overline Y_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_i\). For any \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), Hoeffding's inequality gives \[\mathbb P\left\{F(\widehat x)\le\overline Y_m+(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\alpha)}{2m}}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The displayed upper endpoint is therefore an out-of-sample performance certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bounded validation losses provide a Hoeffding upper confidence certificate for the true expected performance of a fitted decision.
assumptions_latex: The validation scenarios are i.i.d. and independent of the construction of \(\widehat x\).
\(f(\widehat x,\xi)\in[a,b]\) almost surely.
\(F(\widehat x)=\mathbb E[f(\widehat x,\xi)]\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed upper endpoint covers \(F(\widehat x)\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided Hoeffding certificate is mathematically appropriate for independent bounded validation losses and fits the certificate leaf, but no citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Confidence Calibration
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of statistical confidence across reported certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous confidence allocation across repeated validation certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certificates indexed by \(k=1,\ldots,K\), choose error probabilities \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\) satisfying \[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\alpha_k\le\alpha.\] If event \(E_k\) denotes validity of certificate \(k\) and \(\mathbb P(E_k)\ge1-\alpha_k\), then \[\mathbb P\left(\bigcap_{k=1}^{K}E_k\right)\ge1-\sum_{k=1}^{K}\alpha_k\ge1-\alpha.\] For indefinitely many sequential checks, the same conclusion holds when \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k\le\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate per-check error probabilities with total at most the desired global error to obtain simultaneous coverage by the union bound.
assumptions_latex: Every individual certificate has coverage at least \(1-\alpha_k\).
The error allocation satisfies the displayed summability condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All certificates are simultaneously valid with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), without requiring independence.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposable Polyhedral Risk Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario polyhedral risk representation exposing scenario-separable inner terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenario losses \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\in\mathbb R^N\), let \(U=\{q\in\mathbb R^N:Aq\le b,\ q\ge0,\ \mathbf1^\top q=1\}\) be a nonempty polytope. The functional \[\rho(z)=\max_{q\in U}\sum_{i=1}^{N}q_i z_i\] is convex, monotone, translation equivariant, and positively homogeneous. For fixed \(q\), the objective is a sum of scenario-local terms \(q_i z_i\); consequently, decomposition may separate scenario evaluations while a finite-dimensional master problem enforces the coupling constraints defining \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral risk measure is the maximum expected loss over a polytope of scenario weights, exposing separable scenario terms and finite coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite.
The envelope \(U\) is a nonempty polytope contained in the probability simplex.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Dynamic-Risk Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-consistent nested risk evaluation on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a finite scenario tree with filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\), let \(Z_t\) be an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable stage cost and let \(\rho_t\) map integrable \(\mathcal F_{t+1}\)-measurable random variables to \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable ones. Define recursively \(V_T=Z_T\) and \[V_t=Z_t+\rho_t(V_{t+1}),\qquad t=T-1,\ldots,0.\] Then the dynamic evaluation is \(V_0=Z_0+\rho_0(Z_1+\rho_1(\cdots+\rho_{T-1}(Z_T)\cdots))\), and each recursion step couples a node only to its children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-consistent dynamic risk evaluation nests one-step conditional risk mappings backward through a scenario tree, creating node-local parent–child interfaces.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and horizon \(T\) are finite.
Each \(Z_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and lies in the domain of the recursion.
Each \(\rho_t\) is a monotone conditional risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nested risk value is obtained by backward nodewise recursion through the one-step interfaces \(\rho_t\).
