knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguity Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional inner maximization for a fixed decision in robust stochastic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) be fixed, let \(Q(x,\xi)\) be a measurable scenario loss, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty set of probability measures for which the expectations are well defined. The ambiguity subproblem at \(x\) is \[\Phi(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)].\] Any attaining distribution \(P_x^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\) is a worst-case distribution. If the supremum is unattained, an \(\varepsilon\)-maximizer satisfies \(\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\ge\Phi(x)-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed decision, an ambiguity subproblem maximizes expected loss over an admissible family of probability distributions and returns a worst-case value or distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty set of probability measures.
\(Q(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and has a well-defined expectation under every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(x)\) is the worst-case expected scenario loss associated with decision \(x\).

notation.meaning: scenario loss at fixed decision x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining inner problem of distributionally robust optimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes the distributional inner maximization and fits the ambiguity-subproblem leaf, but it has no authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Scenario Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Scenario-indexed subproblem structure retained under decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario linear recourse subproblems for a fixed first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), let \(p_s>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), and let \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be fixed. For each \(s\in S\), let \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_s}\), \(q_s\in\mathbb R^{m_s}\), \(W_s\in\mathbb R^{r_s\times m_s}\), \(h_s\in\mathbb R^{r_s}\), and \(T_s\in\mathbb R^{r_s\times n}\). The scenario subproblem is \[Q_s(x)=\inf_{y_s\in Y_s}\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\}.\] If every \(Q_s(x)\) is finite and there are no constraints coupling distinct \(y_s\), then the risk-neutral recourse value is \(Q(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\), and the scenario subproblems can be solved independently conditional on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed first-stage decision, uncoupled finite-scenario linear recourse yields one independently solvable subproblem per scenario, and the risk-neutral recourse value is their probability-weighted sum.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\{1,\ldots,N\}\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is fixed.
\(Q_s(x)\in\mathbb R\) for every \(s\in S\).
No constraint couples recourse variables belonging to distinct scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\), and the \(Q_s(x)\) are independently computable conditional on \(x\).

notation.meaning: optimal recourse value in scenario s

children.title: Adversarial Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Worst-case subproblem structure within distributional decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case recourse subproblems under an explicitly specified uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) be fixed, let \(\mathcal U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set, and let \(Q(x,u)\) be the optimal recourse cost under realization \(u\in\mathcal U\). The adversarial subproblem associated with \(x\) is \[A(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x,u).\] If the supremum is attained, any \(u^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x,u)\) is an adversarial realization. It either supplies a worst-case scenario for constraint or column generation or certifies that a proposed bound \(\eta\) is valid when \(A(x)\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed candidate decision, an adversarial subproblem selects the uncertainty realization having the largest optimal recourse cost.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
\(Q(x,u)\) is well-defined in the extended real line for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x,u)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the adversarial-subproblem leaf, but no robust or distributionally robust optimization source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Subproblem-Nesting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination consequences when these subproblem roles are nested.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem-Nesting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-level, nested, and flattened arrangements of distributional and recourse optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x\), let \(Q_s(x)=\inf_{y_s\in Y_s(x)}c_s(y_s)\), and let \(\mathcal P\) be a set of scenario probability vectors. The distributionally robust value has the nested representation \[V(x)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{s=1}^{N}p_sQ_s(x)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{s=1}^{N}p_s\inf_{y_s\in Y_s(x)}c_s(y_s).\] A regime is scenario-parallel when the inner recourse problems are solved separately for a proposed \(p\); it is fully nested when an outer ambiguity solve repeatedly invokes them; and it is flattened when valid duality replaces one or more inner value functions by a single-level formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributional decomposition may solve recourse problems separately, invoke them inside an ambiguity problem, or flatten the nesting through valid dual reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\subseteq\{p\in\mathbb R_+^N:\sum_sp_s=1\}\) is nonempty.
Each \(Q_s(x)\) is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{s=1}^{N}p_s\inf_{y_s\in Y_s(x)}c_s(y_s)\).

notation.meaning: feasible recourse set in scenario s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested representation fits the container and appropriately conditions flattening on valid duality, but the representation and the asserted regime taxonomy have no supporting citation.

children.title: Nonseparable Risk Structure
children.top_down_role: Risk structures that resist scenario-wise separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Risk Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A functional criterion for failure of additive scenario separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) be nonempty, let \(Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N)\in D\) collect scenario losses, and let \(\rho:D\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a risk functional. The risk structure is scenario-separable on \(D\) if functions \(\rho_s:\mathbb R\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) exist such that \(\rho(Z)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\rho_s(Z_s)\) for every \(Z\in D\). It is nonseparable on \(D\) when no such collection exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk is nonseparable on a loss domain when it cannot be represented throughout that domain as a sum of functions of the individual scenario losses.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) is nonempty.
\(\rho:D\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\) is nonseparable on \(D\) if and only if \(\nexists(\rho_s)_{s=1}^N\;\forall Z\in D:\rho(Z)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\rho_s(Z_s)\).

children.title: Cross-Scenario Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies linking decisions or certificates across scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Scenario Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-based criterion for coupling otherwise scenario-indexed recourse decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\) be scenario-indexed recourse decisions with nonempty local feasible sets \(Y_s(x)\), and let \(G:\prod_{s=1}^NY_s(x)\to\mathbb R^r\). Define \[\mathcal Y(x)=\{y:y_s\in Y_s(x)\ \text{for all }s,\ G(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\leq 0\},\] where the inequality is componentwise. Cross-scenario coupling is present when this joint constraint is nonredundant, namely when \(\mathcal Y(x)\subsetneq\prod_{s=1}^{N}Y_s(x)\). In that case, fixing \(x\) does not yield independent scenario-feasible choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-scenario coupling is present when a well-defined, nonredundant joint constraint makes the feasible recourse set strictly smaller than the product of the scenario-local feasible sets.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_s(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(s\in\{1,ldots,N\}\).
\(G:\prod_{s=1}^NY_s(x)\to\mathbb R^r\) is well-defined.
The inequality \(G(y)\leq0\) is interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Y(x)\subsetneq\prod_{s=1}^{N}Y_s(x)\), so scenario-wise feasibility is not independent.

children.title: Separability Loss
children.top_down_role: Decomposition consequences caused by global risk coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Separability Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of the structural guarantee for independent scenario minimization under objective or constraint coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_s:Y_s(x)\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be scenario-local objectives. If \(F(y)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}F_s(y_s)\) and \(\mathcal Y(x)=\prod_{s=1}^{N}Y_s(x)\), then \[\inf_{y\in\mathcal Y(x)}F(y)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\inf_{y_s\in Y_s(x)}F_s(y_s),\] whenever both sides are well-defined. If the objective is not additively separable or the feasible set is not a Cartesian product, this identity is no longer structurally guaranteed and uncoordinated scenario minimization may fail to recover the joint optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive objectives and a Cartesian-product feasible set guarantee exact independent scenario minimization; losing either structure removes that guarantee and can make uncoordinated scenario solves inexact.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed infimum is well-defined in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\).
The functions \(F_s\) are the objectives used by the proposed scenario-wise decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of objective additivity or product feasibility removes the general separability guarantee, although equality may still occur in special instances.

children.title: Coordination-Burden Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of master or coordination structure under coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination-Burden Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration communication burden induced by a general scenario-coupling graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent cross-scenario dependencies by an undirected graph \(G=(S,E)\), where edge \(\{s,t\}\) requires exchange of a vector of dimension \(d_{st}\) during each exact coordination iteration. Any edge-local implementation that updates every coupling once per iteration communicates at least \[C_{\mathrm{iter}}\geq\sum_{\{s,t\}\in E}d_{st}\] scalar values, and a direct two-way exchange communicates at most \(2\sum_{\{s,t\}\in E}d_{st}\). Hence dense uniform coupling with \(d_{st}=d\) has per-iteration communication order \(\Theta(dN^2)\), whereas bounded-degree coupling has order \(O(dN)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination traffic scales with coupling edges: dense all-to-all scenario coupling is quadratic, while bounded-degree coupling is linear in the scenario count.
assumptions_latex: Every coupling edge is updated once per coordination iteration.
Messages transmit explicit scalar coordinates without compression.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{iter}}=\Theta(dN^2)\) for complete uniform coupling and \(C_{\mathrm{iter}}=O(dN)\) for uniformly bounded degree.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the burden-growth leaf, but the edge-message counting model and its lower and upper bounds require a specific distributed-optimization or communication-complexity source.

children.title: Scenario Explosion
children.top_down_role: Growth in scenario count across multistage representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial growth of a full multistage scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a horizon of \(T\) uncertainty stages. If every history at stage \(t-1\) has exactly \(b_t\geq1\) children, then the number of stage-\(t\) nodes is \(n_t=\prod_{j=1}^{t}b_j\), and the total number of nonroot nodes is \[N_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\prod_{j=1}^{t}b_j.\] For constant branching \(b_t=b>1\), \(N_T=(b^{T+1}-b)/(b-1)=\Theta(b^T)\). Any deterministic-equivalent formulation storing at least one scalar per node therefore requires \(\Omega(N_T)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full scenario tree grows exponentially with the number of stages when each node has a fixed branching factor greater than one.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\).
Every stage-\(t-1\) history has exactly \(b_t\) children.
At least one scalar datum or variable is stored per node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\prod_{j=1}^{t}b_j\), and \(N_T=\Theta(b^T)\) when \(b_t=b>1\).

notation.meaning: number of nodes at stage t
total number of nonroot scenario-tree nodes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario-tree counts and asymptotic conclusion are mathematically standard and the complexity-bound kind fits, but no multistage stochastic-programming source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Uneven branching or computational burden across a scenario tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work imbalance across parallel scenario-tree subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite nonempty set of scenario-tree subproblems, let \(w_s>0\) be their work estimates, and let \(P\in\mathbb N\) be the number of workers. For an assignment \(\pi:S\to\{1,\ldots,P\}\), define \(L_k=\sum_{s:\pi(s)=k}w_s\) and \[I(\pi)=\frac{P\max_{1\leq k\leq P}L_k}{\sum_{s\in S}w_s}.\] Then \(I(\pi)\geq1\), with equality exactly when all worker loads are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario-tree imbalance is the heaviest worker load divided by the average load; it is at least one and equals one exactly under perfect load balance.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
\(w_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
\(P\in\mathbb N\), and each subproblem is assigned to exactly one worker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(\pi)\geq1\), with \(I(\pi)=1\) if and only if \(L_1=\cdots=L_P\).

children.title: Explosion-Imbalance Interaction
children.top_down_role: Compounding effects of scenario growth or uneven tree structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Explosion-Imbalance Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel makespan lower bounds combining total scenario work and load imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_T\) scenario-tree subproblems with works \(w_s>0\) be assigned to \(P\) workers by \(\pi\), and let \(L_k\) and \(I(\pi)\) be the resulting loads and imbalance factor. Ignoring communication, every nonpreemptive execution has makespan \[M(\pi)=\max_kL_k=I(\pi)\frac{\sum_{s=1}^{N_T}w_s}{P}.\] If \(w_s\geq w_{\min}>0\), then \(M(\pi)\geq I(\pi)N_Tw_{\min}/P\). Thus exponential node growth remains exponential for fixed \(P\), while imbalance multiplies the average-work bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario explosion raises total work, and imbalance multiplies the average-load makespan; fixed parallelism cannot remove exponential tree growth.
assumptions_latex: \(w_s\geq w_{\min}>0\).
Subproblems are nonpreemptively assigned to \(P\) workers.
Communication and coordination overhead are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(\pi)\geq I(\pi)N_Tw_{\min}/P\); if \(N_T=\Theta(b^T)\) and \(P\) is fixed, then \(M(\pi)=\Omega(I(\pi)b^T)\).

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on subproblem work

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound is algebraically consistent under the stated static load model, and the complexity-bound kind fits, but the makespan model and interaction claim have no supporting parallel-complexity citation.

children.title: Weak Recourse Approximations
children.top_down_role: Low-fidelity approximations of recourse value structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Recourse Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative weakness of a lower approximation to a convex recourse function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\) be a convex recourse function and let \(\underline Q_k(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}\{\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\}\) satisfy \(\underline Q_k(x)\leq Q(x)\) on \(X\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) and a region \(R\subseteq X\), the approximation is \(\varepsilon\)-weak on \(R\) when \[\sup_{x\in R}\bigl(Q(x)-\underline Q_k(x)\bigr)>\varepsilon.\] A master solution lying in such a region may have a recourse lower bound whose error exceeds \(\varepsilon\), despite every constituent cut being valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cutting-plane recourse model is weak on a region when its worst-case underestimation there exceeds the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is finite and convex on \(X\).
Every affine cut underestimates \(Q\) on \(X\).
\(R\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in R}(Q(x)-\underline Q_k(x))>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: polyhedral lower approximation after k cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition precisely defines regional weakness of a valid lower approximation and fits the leaf, but no Benders or cutting-plane source with a specific locator supports this terminology and formulation.

children.title: Cut Tail-Off
children.top_down_role: Diminishing improvement from additional certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Tail-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing improvement of valid recourse cuts while the target gap remains unmet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((L_k)_{k\geq0}\) be master-problem lower bounds and \((U_k)_{k\geq0}\) incumbent upper bounds, with \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\) and \(U_k\geq L_k\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), cut tail-off occurs along an infinite index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) when \[U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }k\in K,\qquad \lim_{\substack{k\to\infty\\k\in K}}(L_{k+1}-L_k)=0.\] Thus valid cuts can yield vanishing lower-bound improvement while the reported optimality gap remains above tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut tail-off occurs along an infinite subsequence when valid cuts produce lower-bound improvements tending to zero while the incumbent gap stays above the target tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All added cuts are valid lower estimators.
\(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\) and \(U_k\geq L_k\) for every \(k\).
\(\varepsilon>0\), and \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) is infinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\) for every \(k\in K\), while \(L_{k+1}-L_k\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\) through \(K\).

notation.meaning: master lower bound after k cuts
incumbent upper bound at iteration k

children.title: Approximation-Strength Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence distinguishing weak modeling from exhausted cut progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Strength Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic for tail-off caused by weak lower approximations of expected recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the true recourse function and let \(\underline Q_k=\max_{j\le k}\ell_j\le Q\) be the current cutting-plane approximation. For a finite diagnostic set \(D_k\subset X\), define \[\Delta_k:=\max_{x\in D_k}\bigl(Q(x)-\underline Q_k(x)\bigr),\qquad \rho_k:=\frac{Q(x_k)-\underline Q_k(x_k)}{\max\{1,|Q(x_k)|\}}.\] The approximation is \((\varepsilon,\eta)\)-strong on \(D_k\) at \(x_k\) exactly when \(\Delta_k\le\varepsilon\) and \(\rho_k\le\eta\). Persistent violation while master progress tends to zero diagnoses approximation-driven tail-off.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare true and cutting-plane recourse on diagnostic points. Large persistent absolute or relative underestimation, despite vanishing master progress, diagnoses weak-approximation tail-off.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_j(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(j\le k\).
\(Q\) is evaluable on the finite set \(D_k\cup\{x_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_k\le\varepsilon\) and \(\rho_k\le\eta\) characterize the stated diagnostic strength.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct error diagnostics for cutting-plane recourse approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The error measures are well defined, but the causal tail-off diagnosis is decomposition-specific, “master progress” is undefined, and no inspectable source supports the proposed diagnostic thresholds or conclusion.

children.title: Rare Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility confined to low-probability or sparsely sampled scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Rare Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-based definition for infrequent second-stage infeasibility under a fixed first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) be fixed, let \(\xi\sim P\), and let \(Y(x,\xi)\) denote the second-stage feasible set. Define the infeasibility event and its probability by \[I_x:=\{\xi:Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\},\qquad p(x):=P(I_x).\] Relative to a prescribed rarity threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\), recourse infeasibility at \(x\) is rare when \(0<p(x)\le\tau\). It is absent when \(p(x)=0\), and it is not rare under this convention when \(p(x)>\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse infeasibility is rare when its scenario probability is positive but no greater than a specified rarity threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(I_x\) is measurable under \(P\).
\(\tau\in(0,1)\) is fixed before detection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<p(x)\le\tau\) is the rare-infeasibility predicate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: measurable-event definition of probabilistic recourse infeasibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability-based predicate is internally precise and the definition kind fits the leaf, but the threshold convention has no cited stochastic-programming source.

children.title: Unstable Infeasibility Detection
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of infeasibility evidence to sampling or numerical variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Infeasibility Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection instability when rare infeasibility is inferred from finite independent scenario batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x\), let \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{Y(x,\xi_i)=\varnothing\}\) for independent \(\xi_i\sim P\), and let \(\widehat p_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i\). Then \[\operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_N)=\frac{p(x)(1-p(x))}{N},\qquad \frac{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_N)}}{p(x)}=\sqrt{\frac{1-p(x)}{Np(x)}}.\] Thus relative detection error is large when \(Np(x)\) is small. In particular, as \(p(x)\downarrow0\) with bounded \(Np(x)\), relative precision does not stabilize, so classifications based on whether \(\widehat p_N\) crosses a fixed threshold remain sample-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rare infeasibility detection is unstable when the expected number of infeasible sampled scenarios is small; relative estimation error then remains large.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) are independent with common distribution \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded \(Np(x)\) prevents vanishing relative standard error.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Bernoulli variance calculation identifies the rare-event detection boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli variance and relative-standard-error formulas are correct under the stated independence assumptions, and the failure-boundary kind fits. An inspectable rare-event or stochastic-programming source is still required.

children.title: Missed-Infeasibility Risk
children.top_down_role: Consequences of failing to expose rare infeasible scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed-Infeasibility Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-sample probability that an independent scenario batch contains no infeasible realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) with infeasibility probability \(p(x)=P\{Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\}\). For \(N\) independent sampled scenarios, the probability that every sampled subproblem is feasible, despite \(p(x)>0\), is \[P\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^{N}\{Y(x,\xi_i)\ne\varnothing\}\right)=(1-p(x))^N.\] Consequently, to make this missed-infeasibility probability at most \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), it is necessary and sufficient that \[N\ge \frac{\log\alpha}{\log(1-p(x))},\] with the integer sample size rounded upward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch of independent scenarios misses all infeasible outcomes with probability \((1-p)^N\); the displayed logarithmic bound gives the required sample size.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) are independent with common distribution \(P\).
\(N\in\mathbb{N}\), \(0<p(x)<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The missed-infeasibility risk equals \((1-p(x))^N\).

notation.meaning: true infeasibility probability at the fixed decision

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: complement probability for independent Bernoulli trials

children.title: Sampling Bias
children.top_down_role: Systematic distortion from scenario-generation or selection choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias of a sampled optimal-value or optimality-gap estimator relative to its target quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\in\mathbb{R}\) be a deterministic target, such as the true optimal value or optimality gap, and let \(\widehat T_N\) be an integrable statistic constructed from \(N\) sampled scenarios. Its sampling bias is \[b_N:=\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]-T.\] The statistic is unbiased at sample size \(N\) when \(b_N=0\), asymptotically unbiased when \(b_N\to0\) as \(N\to\infty\), upward biased when \(b_N>0\), and downward biased when \(b_N<0\). Bias concerns repeated-sampling expectation, not the error of a single realized sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling bias is the repeated-sampling mean of an estimator minus its target; it may vanish exactly, asymptotically, or neither.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite and nonrandom.
\(\mathbb{E}|\widehat T_N|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_N=\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]-T\) defines sampling bias.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional statistical definition specialized to scenario sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate for the leaf, but no authoritative statistics or stochastic-programming citation with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Sampling Variance
children.top_down_role: Replication-to-replication instability in reported performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated-sampling dispersion of a scenario-based estimator around its own expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat T_N\) be a square-integrable statistic computed from \(N\) sampled scenarios. Its sampling variance and standard error are \[v_N:=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat T_N)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\bigl(\widehat T_N-\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]\bigr)^2\right],\qquad \operatorname{se}(\widehat T_N):=\sqrt{v_N}.\] These quantities measure dispersion across independent repetitions of the entire sampling procedure. They do not include the squared displacement between \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]\) and the target and therefore do not, by themselves, measure total estimation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling variance measures repeated-sample dispersion around the estimator’s own mean; it excludes systematic bias from the target.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N^2]<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_N=\mathbb{E}[(\widehat T_N-\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N])^2]\) defines sampling variance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional variance definition specialized to scenario sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variance definition and its distinction from bias are correct, and the content kind fits, but the record has no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: False Gap Confidence
children.top_down_role: Overstated confidence in estimated optimality gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: False Gap Confidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nominal gap coverage can fail when confidence intervals account for variance but omit bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a true optimality gap and let \(\widehat G_N\) have bias \(b_N\) and reported standard error \(s_N>0\). Consider the nominal interval \(I_N=[\widehat G_N-zs_N,\widehat G_N+zs_N]\), where \(z>0\) is calibrated for the centered error. If \((\widehat G_N-G-b_N)/s_N\) is standard normal, then its actual coverage is \[P(G\in I_N)=\Phi\!\left(z-\frac{b_N}{s_N}\right)-\Phi\!\left(-z-\frac{b_N}{s_N}\right).\] Hence nominal confidence is valid only after controlling standardized bias; as \(|b_N|/s_N\to\infty\), actual coverage tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variance-only gap interval can have near-zero actual coverage when estimator bias is large relative to its reported standard error.
assumptions_latex: \(s_N>0\) is treated as fixed under the stated calibration.
\((\widehat G_N-G-b_N)/s_N\) has the standard normal distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncontrolled \(|b_N|/s_N\) invalidates nominal gap coverage.

notation.meaning: true gap and sampled gap estimator
estimator bias and reported standard error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shifted-normal coverage formula is correct under the stated fixed-standard-error model, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A gap-estimation source is needed to support this model-specific failure interpretation.

children.title: Bias-Variance Confounding
children.top_down_role: Difficulty separating systematic distortion from sampling noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias-Variance Confounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square decomposition showing why replicate dispersion alone cannot reveal systematic sampling error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\in\mathbb{R}\) and let \(\widehat T_N\) be square-integrable, with bias \(b_N=\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]-T\) and variance \(v_N=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat T_N)\). Then \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[(\widehat T_N-T)^2\right]=v_N+b_N^2.\] Thus repeated samples identify dispersion around \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N]\), while displacement of that expectation from an unknown \(T\) is not separated without external information, independent validation, or structural assumptions. Consequently, a small empirical variance cannot by itself certify a small mean-square error or a reliable optimality-gap estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean-square error equals variance plus squared bias. Low replicate dispersion therefore cannot distinguish accuracy from stable systematic error.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite and nonrandom.
\(\mathbb{E}[\widehat T_N^2]<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MSE}(\widehat T_N;T)=v_N+b_N^2\).

children.title: Mixed-Integer Decomposition Contexts
children.top_down_role: Interfaces created when integrality enters the master, local subproblems, recourse model, or generated-column representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Master with Continuous Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-angular mixed-integer regime with discrete linking variables and continuous scenario recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integer-master, continuous-subproblem decomposition has the form \[\min_{x\in X\cap(\mathbb{Z}^{p}\times\mathbb{R}^{n-p})}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s Q_s(x)\right\},\qquad Q_s(x):=\inf_{y_s\in\mathbb{R}^{m_s}}\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\}.\] The variables \(x\) are shared master variables and contain at least one integer component; each scenario variable \(y_s\) is continuous. When every feasible subproblem has a finite optimum, linear-programming duality yields convex polyhedral recourse functions and valid Benders optimality cuts, while the master remains a mixed-integer optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete linking decisions remain in the master, while each scenario recourse problem is continuous and can generate linear-programming dual cuts.
assumptions_latex: Every subproblem used for an optimality cut is feasible with finite value.
At least one component of \(x\) is integer and every \(y_s\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(Q_s\) is convex polyhedral on its finite domain, but the master feasible set is mixed-integer.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard block-angular Benders formulation with master-side integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly places integrality in the master and continuous variables in the subproblems. Its Benders-duality and polyhedral-value-function claims require a specific mixed-integer decomposition source.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Master with Integer Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-angular regime with continuous linking decisions and discrete scenario-recourse variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous-master, integer-subproblem decomposition has the form \[\min_{x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s Q_s(x)\right\},\qquad Q_s(x):=\inf_{y_s\in Y_s\cap(\mathbb{Z}^{r_s}\times\mathbb{R}^{m_s-r_s})}\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\},\] with \(r_s\ge1\) for at least one scenario. Although the explicit master variables are continuous, integer recourse generally makes \(Q_s\) nonconvex and discontinuous. Consequently, ordinary linear-programming dual multipliers do not in general provide an exact global representation of \(Q_s\); integer-valid cuts or alternative value-function approximations are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linking decision is continuous, but integer recourse generally destroys convexity, so ordinary linear-programming Benders cuts are not globally exact.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\) contains no imposed integrality restrictions.
At least one scenario has \(r_s\ge1\).
Each stated recourse infimum is interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integer subproblem variables generally prevent an exact convex polyhedral recourse representation by linear-programming dual cuts.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard block-angular formulation with subproblem-side integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the integrality-placement regime, but the general claims about nonconvexity, discontinuity, and the insufficiency of ordinary LP-dual cuts require an authoritative integer-recourse source.

children.title: Master-Problem Integrality
children.top_down_role: Discrete structure located in the decomposition master.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Problem Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality placement on variables retained in the decomposition master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a decomposed model \[\min\{F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_S):(x,y_1,\ldots,y_S)\in\mathcal F\},\] in which \(x\) is retained in the master and the blocks \(y_s\) are assigned to subproblems. Master-problem integrality is present when the master domain imposes \[x\in X\cap(\mathbb{Z}^{p}\times\mathbb{R}^{n-p})\quad\text{for some }p\ge1.\] This classification depends on variable placement, not merely on whether the original model contains integer variables. It makes the master nonconvex even when all subproblems are continuous and their value functions are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master-problem integrality means that at least one variable retained in the master is constrained to be integer.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition specifies a master block \(x\) and subproblem blocks \(y_s\).
Coordinates are ordered so the first \(p\) master components are integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\ge1\) in the master domain is the master-integrality predicate.

notation.meaning: variables assigned to subproblem block s
number of explicitly integer master coordinates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integrality classified by decomposition block membership

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly classifies integrality by variables retained in the master, and its content kind fits. No decomposition source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Subproblem Integrality
children.top_down_role: Discrete structure located in decomposed subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality placement on variables assigned to one or more decomposition subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a decomposition with master variable \(x\) and subproblem block \(s\) having domain \[Y_s(x):=\{y_s\in\mathbb{Z}^{r_s}\times\mathbb{R}^{m_s-r_s}:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\}.\] Subproblem integrality is present when \(r_s\ge1\) for at least one block \(s\). The classification is independent of whether \(x\) is continuous or integer. Because the associated value function \(Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:y_s\in Y_s(x)\}\) is then an integer-programming value function, linear-programming duality alone does not generally yield its exact global epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblem integrality means that at least one variable assigned to a subproblem is constrained to be integer.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition specifies master variable \(x\) and subproblem variables \(y_s\).
Each subproblem domain is interpreted as empty when its displayed constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of a block \(s\) with \(r_s\ge1\) is the subproblem-integrality predicate.

notation.meaning: feasible domain of subproblem block s
number of integer coordinates in block s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integrality classified by decomposition block membership

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integrality predicate is precise and appropriate for the leaf. The accompanying claim about failure of an exact LP-dual epigraph representation needs an inspectable integer-decomposition source.

children.title: Joint Master-Subproblem Integrality
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous discrete structure across both decomposition levels.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set has block form \(F=\{(x,y):x\in X\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}),\ y\in Y\cap(\mathbb Z^q\times\mathbb R^{m-q}),\ A x+B y\ge b\}\).
Both \(p\ge 1\) and \(q\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) has joint master-subproblem integrality because integer restrictions occur in both blocks.
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically treats integrality in both decomposition blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the placement regime, independently of any particular decomposition algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a block-structured optimization problem with master variables \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and subproblem variables \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), joint master-subproblem integrality is the regime
\[
x\in X\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}),\qquad y\in Y\cap(\mathbb Z^q\times\mathbb R^{m-q}),
\]
where \(p,q\ge 1\), after fixed coordinate permutations. Thus neither block is wholly continuous, and feasibility of a master assignment may require solving an integer optimization problem in the subproblem block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint integrality means that at least one master coordinate and at least one subproblem coordinate are constrained to be integer.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Master-Subproblem Integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source with a specific locator supports this decomposition-specific integrality terminology or scope.

children.title: Integrality-Placement Consequences
children.top_down_role: Certificate or coordination consequences of integrality placement.

assumptions_latex: The problem is decomposed into master variables \(x\) and subproblem variables \(y\).
The recourse value is \(Q(x)=\inf\{q(y):y\in Y(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integer restrictions on \(x\) determine master search, while integer restrictions on \(y\) can invalidate an exact LP-dual-cut representation of \(Q\).

notation.meaning: subproblem feasible set at a master decision

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports these decomposition consequences.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates consequences of integer master decisions from consequences of integer subproblem decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the value function \(Q(x)=\inf\{q(y):y\in Y(x)\}\), integrality in the master block makes optimization over \(x\) a discrete search problem. If \(Y(x)\) is continuous and convex and strong duality holds, supporting inequalities obtained from subproblem dual solutions can represent \(Q\) over the master domain. If \(Y(x)\) contains integer restrictions, its LP dual generally represents only a relaxation, so ordinary dual Benders cuts need not describe \(Q\) exactly; valid integer, combinatorial, or logic-derived certificates are then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master integrality creates discrete search; subproblem integrality can destroy the exactness of ordinary LP-dual Benders cuts and require stronger certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Placement Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the consequences leaf, but the claims about exact value-function representation and the certificates required under subproblem integrality need an authoritative source specifying the relevant convexity, duality, and integer-recourse conditions.

children.title: First-Stage Integrality
children.top_down_role: Discrete decisions before uncertainty is revealed.

assumptions_latex: A two-stage model has first-stage decision \(x\) and scenario recourse decisions \(y_s\).
At least one coordinate of \(x\) is integer-restricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is in the first-stage-integrality regime when recourse integrality is not required by this classification.
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically treats two-stage integrality placement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies integrality imposed on decisions selected before uncertainty is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a deterministic equivalent
\[
\min\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s q_s^\top y_s:x\in X,\ W_s y_s\ge h_s-T_sx,\ y_s\in Y_s\ \text{for all }s\in S\right\}.
\]
First-stage integrality means that, after a coordinate permutation, \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}\) for some \(p\ge1\). The term specifies integrality of decisions chosen before the scenario is revealed and, by itself, imposes no integer restriction on any \(Y_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-stage integrality constrains some pre-uncertainty decisions to integers without, by itself, constraining recourse decisions to integers.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Stage Integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but no source with an inspectable locator supports the precise convention that first-stage integrality imposes no classification requirement on recourse sets.

children.title: Recourse Integrality
children.top_down_role: Discrete decisions after uncertainty is revealed.

assumptions_latex: A two-stage model has first-stage decision \(x\) and scenario recourse decisions \(y_s\).
At least one coordinate of some \(y_s\) is integer-restricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model has integer recourse whenever \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb Z^{q_s}\times\mathbb R^{m_s-q_s}\) for some \(s\) and \(q_s\ge1\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically treats integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines integrality in decisions selected after scenario information becomes available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenario \(s\), let
\[
Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx,\ y_s\in Y_s\}.
\]
Recourse integrality is present when, after a coordinate permutation, \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb Z^{q_s}\times\mathbb R^{m_s-q_s}\) for at least one scenario \(s\) and some \(q_s\ge1\). This designation concerns the post-observation variables \(y_s\) and does not imply that the first-stage set for \(x\) is integer-restricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse integrality constrains some post-observation scenario decisions to integers, independently of whether first-stage decisions are integer.
knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but a source is needed to confirm whether “recourse integrality” is intended to require integer restrictions in at least one scenario, every scenario, or a specified scenario class.

children.title: Two-Stage Integrality Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between first-stage or recourse discreteness.

assumptions_latex: The deterministic equivalent has linking constraints \(W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\).
Both \(x\) and at least one \(y_s\) contain integer-restricted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integrality is coupled across stages because feasible integer recourse and its value depend parametrically on the integer first-stage decision.
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports the stated coupling property.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers simultaneous first-stage and recourse integrality linked through scenario constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x\in X\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p})\) and \(y_s\in Y_s\cap(\mathbb Z^{q_s}\times\mathbb R^{m_s-q_s})\), with \(p\ge1\) and \(q_s\ge1\) for some \(s\). Under linking constraints \(W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\), the feasible integer-recourse set
\[
R_s(x)=\{y_s:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx,\ y_s\in Y_s\cap(\mathbb Z^{q_s}\times\mathbb R^{m_s-q_s})\}
\]
and its value \(Q_s(x)\) depend on the integer first-stage assignment. This dependence constitutes two-stage integrality coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both stages contain integer decisions, and linking constraints make feasible integer recourse and its value depend on the first-stage assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Integrality Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the coupling leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the proposed definition of two-stage integrality coupling and its scenario quantification lack cited support.

children.title: Benders Decomposition with an Integer Master

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(X\) may contain integer restrictions.
For fixed \(x\), the subproblem is a linear program with strong duality whenever feasible and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with coincident bounds returns an optimal integer-master solution; otherwise generated cuts provide valid master relaxations.

notation.meaning: master approximation of the subproblem value

review_flags: No supplied locator covers Benders decomposition with an integer master.
An authoritative algorithm source and convergence conditions are required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Benders separation for a discrete master and a continuous linear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\min\{c^\top x+Q(x):x\in X\}\), initialize a master containing \(x\in X\), a variable \(\theta\), and any valid lower bound on \(\theta\). At iteration \(k\), solve the mixed-integer master to obtain \((x^k,\theta^k)\). Solve the linear subproblem defining \(Q(x^k)\). If it is infeasible, add a feasibility cut obtained from a dual ray; if feasible and \(\theta^k<Q(x^k)\), add the dual optimality cut supporting \(Q\) at \(x^k\). Stop when the incumbent upper bound and master lower bound agree within the prescribed tolerance, and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve an integer master, evaluate its continuous LP subproblem, and add dual feasibility or optimality cuts until the bounds meet.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Decomposition with an Integer Master

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but finite or tolerance termination for an integer master requires sourced assumptions concerning cut validity, master solution, subproblem duality, bounds, and the represented master domain.

assumptions_latex: For each fixed \(x\in X\), the subproblem is a convex program satisfying a constraint qualification.
The resulting value function has valid generalized Benders cuts derived from primal and dual subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the master lower bound meets the incumbent upper bound, the incumbent solves the stated convex-subproblem decomposition to the chosen tolerance.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers generalized Benders decomposition.
An authoritative source is needed to certify the precise convexity and constraint-qualification version.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex nonlinear subproblem version with complicating variables retained in the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):g(x,y)\le0,\ y\in Y\}\), initialize a relaxation in \((x,\theta)\) over \(x\in X\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \((x^k,\theta^k)\), then solve the convex subproblem at \(x^k\). From an optimal primal-dual pair, add a generalized optimality cut giving a valid lower bound on \(Q(x)\); from an infeasibility certificate, add a generalized feasibility cut excluding certified infeasible master decisions. Update lower and incumbent upper bounds. Stop at the prescribed bound gap and return the best feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized Benders alternates a master problem with convex nonlinear subproblems and adds cuts derived from optimal dual solutions or infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Benders Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but generalized Benders cut construction and convergence depend on precise convexity, duality, constraint-qualification, feasibility-certificate, and master-domain assumptions that are not sourced here.

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(X\) is discrete or mixed-integer.
For every tested \(x^k\), subproblem reasoning can produce a valid lower-bound or infeasibility inference over a specified subset of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is exact upon finite termination if every cut is valid, incumbents are correctly evaluated, and the final master lower bound equals the incumbent value.

notation.meaning: subproblem value or infinity when infeasible

review_flags: No supplied locator covers logic-based Benders decomposition.
An authoritative source is needed for the formal inference-dual framework.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inference-based Benders scheme permitting discrete or combinatorial subproblems without LP duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\min\{c(x)+Q(x):x\in X\}\), solve a master relaxation in \((x,\theta)\) to obtain \((x^k,\theta^k)\). Evaluate the subproblem at \(x^k\). If infeasible, derive a valid logical inference excluding a set of master assignments containing \(x^k\). If feasible, derive a valid inequality \(\theta\ge L_k(x)\) satisfying \(L_k(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(X\) and \(L_k(x^k)=Q(x^k)\), when such an exact-at-incumbent inference is available. Add the inference, update bounds, and stop when the master bound matches the best feasible value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logic-based Benders replaces LP dual cuts with valid deductions from a discrete or combinatorial subproblem and iterates to bound agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but the validity and exactness conditions for logic-based optimality and feasibility inferences require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Combinatorial Benders Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates exploiting discrete combinatorial structure.

assumptions_latex: Master assignments are binary vectors \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
The subproblem at \(\bar x\) proves that every assignment matching \(\bar x\) on an index set \(C\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\) is a verifiable infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: index set sufficient for the infeasibility inference

review_flags: No supplied locator covers combinatorial Benders certificates.
A source is required for the minimal-conflict interpretation and terminology.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-master infeasibility certificate derived from a sufficient conflicting partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\) have an infeasible subproblem, and suppose a verified conflict set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) proves that every \(x\) satisfying \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for all \(i\in C\) is also infeasible. Then
\[
\sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1
\]
is a combinatorial Benders certificate: every feasible master assignment must differ from \(\bar x\) on at least one index in \(C\). Its validity is checked by verifying the stated conflict inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict subset of binary master decisions yields a cut requiring every feasible assignment to differ on at least one conflicting coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Benders Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed conflict inequality is conditionally valid and certificate is an appropriate content kind, but its classification as a combinatorial Benders certificate and the required verification standard for the conflict inference need a cited source.

children.title: No-Good Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates excluding previously identified discrete assignments.

assumptions_latex: The master assignment \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\) has an infeasible subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality excludes exactly \(\bar x\) among binary master assignments and is therefore a valid no-good certificate.

notation.meaning: indices fixed to zero or one in the tested assignment

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports no-good certificates in Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical binary no-good cut excluding one certified infeasible master assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an infeasible binary master assignment \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\), define \(I_0=\{i:\bar x_i=0\}\) and \(I_1=\{i:\bar x_i=1\}\). The no-good inequality
\[
\sum_{i\in I_0}x_i+\sum_{i\in I_1}(1-x_i)\ge1
\]
is satisfied by every binary assignment except \(\bar x\). Consequently, once infeasibility of the subproblem at \(\bar x\) has been verified, this inequality is a directly checkable certificate that removes that assignment without removing any other binary master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary no-good cut excludes one certified infeasible master assignment and leaves every other binary assignment feasible with respect to the cut.
knowledge_statements.title: No-Good Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary no-good inequality is precise and certificate fits the leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator supports its use and terminology in this Benders certificate hierarchy.

children.title: Certificate-Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Relative exclusion scope across combinatorial or no-good certificates.

assumptions_latex: Certificates \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are valid for the same master domain \(X\).
Each certificate defines a retained set \(R(C)=\{x\in X:x\text{ satisfies }C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\) is at least as strong as \(C_2\) exactly when \(R(C_1)\subseteq R(C_2)\).

notation.meaning: retained master assignments under certificate C

review_flags: No supplied locator covers a Benders certificate-strength ordering.
Terminology and intended hierarchy require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders valid certificates by inclusion of the master assignments they retain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid certificate \(C\), let \(R(C)=\{x\in X:x\text{ satisfies }C\}\). Define \(C_1\) to be at least as strong as \(C_2\) when \(R(C_1)\subseteq R(C_2)\); equivalently, every assignment excluded by \(C_2\) is also excluded by \(C_1\). Strict strength holds when the inclusion is proper. Thus a conflict cut based on \(C\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is strictly stronger than the full-assignment no-good cut whenever it validly excludes additional binary assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate strength is ordered by retained-set inclusion: a stronger certificate removes every assignment removed by a weaker one, and possibly more.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Strength Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Retained-set inclusion gives a coherent strength ordering, although the central statement is definitional rather than merely a property. A source is needed to confirm the intended Benders certificate ordering and terminology before choosing or revising the content kind.

children.title: Branching Framework
children.top_down_role: Tree-search structure surrounding Benders separation.

assumptions_latex: Every generated Benders cut is globally valid for the original master domain or explicitly local to its branch-and-bound node.
Node relaxations provide valid lower bounds, and feasible evaluated assignments provide upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhausting the search tree with a final global gap within tolerance certifies an optimal integer-master solution to that tolerance.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers branch-and-Benders-cut integration.
An authoritative source is needed for convergence and local-cut management conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound framework with Benders separation embedded at search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a branch-and-bound tree for the integer master in variables \((x,\theta)\). At an active node \(v\), solve its current relaxation. Prune \(v\) if infeasible or if its lower bound cannot improve the incumbent. Otherwise, evaluate the subproblem at the candidate \(x^v\); add every violated globally valid Benders cut to all applicable nodes, and add a locally valid cut only within its certified subtree. Reoptimize after separation. If no cut is violated and \(x^v\) is integral, update the incumbent; if \(x^v\) is fractional, branch on a valid master disjunction. Stop when no active node can close the prescribed global gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-Benders-cut embeds subproblem cut separation within branch-and-bound, pruning by bounds and branching when a cut-complete master candidate remains fractional.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the branching-framework leaf, but the claims about global versus local cut applicability, cut-complete node processing, pruning, and global-gap certification require a sourced branch-and-Benders-cut framework with explicit convergence conditions.

children.title: Benders-Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Generation of Benders certificates within the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node separation for a branch-and-Benders-cut method with linear recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), solve the recourse linear program defining \(Q(\bar x)\). If it is feasible and bounded, obtain an optimal dual solution \(\bar\pi\) and add the violated optimality cut \[\theta\ge \bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\] whenever \(\bar\theta<\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)-\varepsilon\). If the recourse problem is infeasible, obtain an extreme ray \(\bar r\) of its dual recession cone and add the feasibility cut \[\bar r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le 0\] whenever \(\bar r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>\varepsilon\). Otherwise, separation terminates without a cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve recourse at the current node solution; return a violated dual optimality cut, a dual-ray feasibility cut, or certify that neither is violated beyond tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\).
Strong linear-programming duality applies whenever the recourse problem is feasible and bounded.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a globally valid violated Benders cut or certifies absence of such a cut from the solved recourse dual.

notation.meaning: dual feasible point and dual recession ray

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and the primal-dual separation statement fit Benders-Cut Separation, but no source reference or inspectable locator supports the dual-point and dual-ray cases. The supplied local inventory is off topic, so the precise separation procedure cannot be accepted as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Node-Level Cut Management
children.top_down_role: Placement, reuse, or locality of certificates across nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Cut Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and retention rules for Benders cuts inside branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\) with domain \(X_v\), partition generated inequalities into global cuts, valid for the original master domain \(X\), and local cuts, proved valid only on \(X_v\). Install every global cut at the root or a shared global pool. Install a local cut only at \(v\) and its descendants whose domains are contained in \(X_v\). A cut may be deleted from an active relaxation after aging, but its validity classification and derivation record are retained; a deleted cut may be reactivated when violated. No local cut may be propagated outside its validity subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify cuts by validity domain, propagate global cuts everywhere and local cuts only down their valid subtree, while permitting inactive cuts to be safely reactivated.
assumptions_latex: Each generated inequality has an established validity domain.
For every descendant \(w\) of \(v\), the node domains satisfy \(X_w\subseteq X_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every active node relaxation contains only inequalities valid on that node domain, so cut management cannot remove feasible solutions of the node subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Node-Level Cut Management, and the stated validity-domain rule is mathematically plausible. However, the global-pool, aging, deletion, retention, and reactivation policies are implementation claims with no supporting branch-and-Benders-cut source or locator.

children.title: Search-Certificate Integration
children.top_down_role: Coordination between branching decisions or Benders information.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Certificate Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate for finite branch-and-Benders-cut search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every open or fathomed leaf \(v\), let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound on all feasible completions in \(X_v\), computed from a relaxation containing only valid branching constraints and Benders cuts. Let \(U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x+Q(\hat x)\) be the verified objective value of an incumbent \(\hat x\). If every leaf is infeasible or satisfies \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon\), then \((\hat x,U,\{L_v\}_v)\), together with the branching partition and cut-validity records, certifies \(U-z^*\le\varepsilon\). For \(\varepsilon=0\), the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An evaluated incumbent plus valid bounds covering every search leaf certifies global optimality, or epsilon-optimality, when no leaf can improve the incumbent sufficiently.
assumptions_latex: The terminal leaves form a disjoint cover of the original master domain.
Each \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound on its leaf domain.
The incumbent \(\hat x\) is feasible and its recourse value is evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-z^*\le\varepsilon\), where \(z^*\) is the global optimum.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for leaf v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits Search-Certificate Integration, and the bound-covering statement is coherent for minimization. No authoritative source or locator is supplied for the branch-and-Benders-cut certificate interpretation, and the local inventory does not address it.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Introduction to Stochastic Programming
