knowledge_statements.title: Integer L-Shaped Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario two-stage stochastic integer optimization with discrete first-stage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a master problem in \((x,\theta)\) with \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) and valid lower bounds on \(\theta\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master to obtain \((x^k,\theta^k)\), evaluate every scenario recourse value \(Q_s(x^k)\), and generate valid feasibility or lower-bounding cuts for \(\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\). Add any cut violated by \((x^k,\theta^k)\), update the incumbent using the evaluated value \(c^{\mathsf T}x^k+\sum_s p_sQ_s(x^k)\), and repeat. Stop when the master lower bound and incumbent upper bound differ by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively solve an integer master, evaluate scenario recourse, add valid recourse cuts, and stop when master and incumbent bounds meet within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Each scenario recourse problem can be solved or validly certified infeasible.
All generated cuts are valid lower bounds or feasibility conditions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the incumbent is feasible and has objective value at most \(\varepsilon\) above the optimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Integer L-Shaped Methods, but the record gives a broad decomposition template without citing a specific integer L-shaped variant or establishing conditions for finite termination. An authoritative method definition and locator are required to determine the intended cut family and sufficient convergence hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary First-Stage Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-excluding recourse certificates for binary first-stage vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), fix \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\), and define \[d_{\bar x}(x)=\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i).\] Then \(d_{\bar x}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x=\bar x\), and \(d_{\bar x}(x)\ge1\) otherwise. Hence \(d_{\bar x}(x)\ge1\) is a verifiable no-good certificate excluding only \(\bar x\). If \(Q(x)\ge L\) for every binary \(x\), then \[\theta\ge Q(\bar x)-(Q(\bar x)-L)d_{\bar x}(x)\] is valid and is exact at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary Hamming distance yields a no-good infeasibility certificate and, with a global recourse lower bound, a point-exact recourse-value cut.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le Q(x)\) for all binary first-stage vectors under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities respectively exclude only \(\bar x\) and provide a globally valid recourse lower bound that equals \(Q(\bar x)\) at \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Hamming distance from the reference vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the terminal container, and the binary no-good inequality and point-exact lower cut are internally consistent under the stated global lower bound. They remain entirely unsourced, with no authoritative binary L-shaped or integer-decomposition locator.

children.title: Disjunctive Recourse Cuts
children.top_down_role: Recourse certificates derived from discrete disjunction structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Recourse Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear cuts obtained from a finite disjunction describing integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the epigraph of an integer-recourse value function over a region \(D\) satisfy \[E=\{(x,\theta):x\in D,\ \theta\ge Q(x)\}\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^m P_j,\] where every \(P_j\) is a polyhedron representing one valid recourse disjunct. Any inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\theta\ge\gamma\) valid for each \(P_j\) is valid for \(E\) and for \(\operatorname{conv}(E)\). Separation over the disjunctive hull seeks coefficients satisfying validity on all disjuncts and violated at a candidate \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\); the resulting inequality is a disjunctive recourse cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive recourse cut is an inequality valid on every polyhedral recourse disjunct and therefore on their union and convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The finite family \(\{P_j\}_{j=1}^m\) covers the integer-recourse epigraph on \(D\).
The candidate point and all disjuncts use the same \((x,\theta)\)-space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity on every \(P_j\) implies validity of \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\theta\ge\gamma\) for the integer-recourse epigraph and its convex hull.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Disjunctive Recourse Cuts, and validity on every covering disjunct does imply validity on the covered epigraph. No source identifies the integer-recourse disjunction, its construction, or a specific theorem or section supporting this representation.

children.title: Tender-Space Cuts
children.top_down_role: Certificates expressed through tender-space representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tender-Space Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recourse inequalities expressed in the right-hand-side image of first-stage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For recourse \[Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\in Y\},\] define the tender variable \(z=h-Tx\) and value function \(\varphi(z)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge z,\ y\in Y\}\). Then \(Q(x)=\varphi(h-Tx)\). Every inequality \(\theta\ge a^{\mathsf T}z+b\) valid for the epigraph of \(\varphi\) on the reachable tender set \(Z=\{h-Tx:x\in X\}\) pulls back to the valid master inequality \[\theta\ge a^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)+b.\] Thus one tender-space cut simultaneously applies to all first-stage points sharing the same tender vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent recourse through its right-hand-side tender vector; any valid epigraph cut there pulls back to a valid first-stage master cut.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the first-stage domain and \(Y\) is the recourse domain.
The recourse problem depends on \(x\) only through \(h-Tx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid tender-space inequality induces a valid inequality in the original master space by substituting \(z=h-Tx\).

notation.meaning: recourse value as a function of the tender vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Tender-Space Cuts, and the affine pullback is internally coherent. The record has no source or locator for tender-space terminology or its use in integer-recourse decomposition; the supplied inventory is unrelated.

children.title: Cut-Space Comparison
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between disjunctive or tender-space representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Space Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison under the affine map from first-stage to tender space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to Z\) be \(F(x)=h-Tx\), and suppose \(Q(x)=\varphi(F(x))\). A tender-space inequality \(\theta\ge a^{\mathsf T}z+b\) and its pullback \(\theta\ge a^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)+b\) have identical violation at every corresponding pair \((x,F(x))\). Consequently, a family of tender-space cuts and its complete pullback define the same relaxation over \(X\). If \(F\) is noninjective, an arbitrary first-stage-space cut need not be representable in tender space because its right-hand side may distinguish points \(x^1,x^2\) satisfying \(F(x^1)=F(x^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tender cuts and their pullbacks are equally strong on reachable points, but noninjective tender mappings prevent some first-stage cuts from having tender-space representations.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=h-Tx\) maps \(X\) onto the reachable tender set \(Z\).
The recourse value factors as \(Q=\varphi\circ F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete pullback preserves relaxation strength; when \(F\) is noninjective, tender-space representability is restricted to inequalities constant on fibers of \(F\).

notation.meaning: fiber of first-stage points with tender vector z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits Cut-Space Comparison, and identical violation under direct substitution is clear. The stronger claims about complete relaxation equivalence and fiberwise representability require a source that fixes the admissible cut classes and domains; none is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Based Recourse Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite search-tree certificates for mixed-integer recourse values or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a first-stage vector \(\bar x\) and consider its mixed-integer recourse problem. A finite branch-and-bound tree is a recourse certificate if its leaves cover the recourse domain, every infeasible leaf carries a valid infeasibility certificate, and every remaining leaf carries a valid lower bound \(L_\ell\). If a feasible recourse solution has value \(U\) and \(L_\ell\ge U\) for every feasible leaf, the tree certifies \(Q(\bar x)=U\). If every leaf is certified infeasible, it certifies \(Q(\bar x)=+\infty\). Tree-derived inequalities may support a master cut only after their validity beyond the fixed point \(\bar x\) is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete recourse branch-and-bound tree certifies the exact recourse value, or infeasibility, through leaf coverage and verifiable leaf bounds.
assumptions_latex: The branching disjunctions produce a finite leaf cover of the recourse domain.
Every leaf bound or infeasibility claim has a valid independently checkable certificate.
The feasible solution attaining \(U\), when present, satisfies all recourse constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tree certifies either \(Q(\bar x)=U\) or \(Q(\bar x)=+\infty\), according to its leaf certificates.

notation.meaning: recourse value at the fixed first-stage vector
value of a feasible recourse solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits Branching-Based Recourse Certificates, and the finite leaf-cover certificate is plausible. No authoritative mixed-integer recourse or branch-and-bound certificate source with a specific locator is provided, so the exact certificate requirements cannot be validated.

children.title: Extensive-Form Components
children.top_down_role: Scenario blocks retained explicitly in a unified formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Extensive-Form Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario blocks retained explicitly in a finite-scenario deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenarios \(s\in S_E\), an extensive-form component retains variables \(y_s\), constraints \(W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx\), domain restrictions \(y_s\in Y_s\), and objective terms \(p_sq_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\) explicitly in the master model. Its contribution is therefore represented by \[\min_{\{y_s\}_{s\in S_E}}\ \sum_{s\in S_E}p_sq_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\quad\text{subject to}\quad W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx,\ y_s\in Y_s\ \text{for all }s\in S_E.\] The shared first-stage vector \(x\) provides the coupling to all retained scenario blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extensive-form component keeps selected scenario variables, constraints, integrality restrictions, and weighted costs explicitly coupled to the common first-stage vector.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite.
Each retained scenario has a specified recourse domain \(Y_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained blocks exactly represent the aggregate recourse contribution of scenarios in \(S_E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Extensive-Form Components, and the selected scenario-block formulation is internally consistent. It lacks an authoritative stochastic-programming extensive-form citation and locator; the local inventory is off topic.

children.title: Decomposition Components
children.top_down_role: Scenario blocks handled through separated coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario blocks represented through recourse-value surrogates and valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenarios \(s\in S_D\), a decomposition component replaces explicit recourse variables by master variables \(\theta_s\) and a collection \(\mathcal C_s\) of inequalities valid for the epigraph of \(Q_s\). The component is \[\theta_s\ge \ell(x)\quad\text{for every }\ell\in\mathcal C_s,\] with master objective contribution \(\sum_{s\in S_D}p_s\theta_s\). If \(\mathcal C_s\) gives an exact epigraph representation on \(X\), then minimizing over \(\theta_s\) yields \(\theta_s=Q_s(x)\); otherwise the component supplies the lower approximation \(\theta_s\ge\sup_{\ell\in\mathcal C_s}\ell(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition component substitutes scenario recourse blocks with value surrogates constrained by valid epigraph cuts, exactly or as a lower approximation.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\ell\in\mathcal C_s\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le Q_s(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
Scenario weights satisfy \(p_s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The component is a valid lower representation of decomposed recourse and is exact when each cut family describes the corresponding epigraph.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Decomposition Components, and valid epigraph lower bounds give the stated lower approximation. No source or locator supports the component formulation or specifies an exact cut family for integer recourse, so the exactness clause cannot be externally checked.

children.title: Partial-Decomposition Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Architectures retaining selected blocks while decomposing others.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Decomposition Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid deterministic equivalent with explicit and cut-represented scenario partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the finite scenario set as \(S=S_E\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_D\). Retain \(y_s\) and the recourse constraints explicitly for \(s\in S_E\), while representing every \(s\in S_D\) by a surrogate \(\theta_s\) and valid epigraph cuts. The hybrid objective is \[c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S_E}p_sq_s^{\mathsf T}y_s+\sum_{s\in S_D}p_s\theta_s.\] If the explicit blocks exactly model their recourse problems and the cut families exactly describe \(\operatorname{epi}Q_s\) on \(X\) for all \(s\in S_D\), then the hybrid and the full extensive form have the same feasible first-stage projections and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition scenarios between explicit recourse blocks and cut-based recourse surrogates; exact components make the hybrid equivalent to the full extensive form.
assumptions_latex: \(S_E\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_D=S\).
Explicit scenario blocks are exact.
For each \(s\in S_D\), the retained cuts exactly describe \(\operatorname{epi}Q_s\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial-decomposition hybrid has the same feasible first-stage projection and optimal value as the full extensive form.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Partial-Decomposition Hybrids, and equivalence is plausible when both explicit and decomposed components are exact. The hybrid construction and equivalence claim have no authoritative source or inspectable locator, while all supplied inventory entries are unrelated.

children.title: Hybrid Partition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing which structure remains explicit or decomposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Partition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines which variables and scenarios remain extensive-form versus decomposed in a stochastic mixed-integer hybrid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set and let \(I\) index variable or constraint blocks. A hybrid partition boundary is a pair \((E,D)\) satisfying \(E\cap D=\varnothing\) and \(E\cup D=I\), together with a nonanticipativity set \(N\subseteq I\). Blocks in \(E\) are represented explicitly for every applicable scenario in the master extensive form; blocks in \(D\) are assigned to scenario or block subproblems and communicated through linking variables, cuts, or columns. Every index in \(N\cap D\) must retain an explicit master linking representation enforcing its required cross-scenario equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid boundary partitions model blocks between explicit extensive-form representation and decomposition while preserving master links for decomposed nonanticipative decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(I\) are finite.
Every decomposed block has a specified master-to-subproblem linking map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((E,D)\) defines a valid partial-decomposition boundary exactly when all decomposed nonanticipative blocks retain master linking constraints.

notation.meaning: blocks retained in the extensive form

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports stochastic extensive-form hybrid partition boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited for this specialized hybrid-decomposition definition. The claimed exact characterization is also too strong: retaining master links for decomposed nonanticipative blocks is necessary but is not by itself sufficient to establish a valid partial decomposition.

children.title: Branching Architecture
children.top_down_role: Tree-search organization for generated-column formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-price tree architecture with column generation at every processed node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a mixed-integer master formulation with a finite or implicitly enumerable column set \(P\). Initialize the root with a restricted set \(P_0\subseteq P\). At each open node \(v\), impose its branching restrictions, solve the restricted master, and repeatedly add a feasible column of negative reduced cost until none exists. The resulting relaxation bound permits pruning by infeasibility or incumbent dominance. If its solution is integral, update the incumbent; otherwise create exhaustive child restrictions and enqueue the children. Stop when no open nodes remain, returning the incumbent or an infeasibility declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-price embeds complete column generation in every search-tree node before pruning, accepting, or branching on that node.
assumptions_latex: Each pricing problem can certify that no improving column exists.
Every branching disjunction is exhaustive for the node-feasible integer solutions.
Node bounds are compared using a fixed minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustion of the tree, the returned incumbent is optimal for the implicitly column-generated integer formulation, provided all node operations are exact.
review_flags: Supplied source hints do not cover branch-and-price architecture.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Branching Architecture leaf, but no source supports the branch-and-price procedure or its global-optimality claim. The required finiteness and exactness conditions also need authoritative formulation.

children.title: Node-Level Pricing
children.top_down_role: Column generation within individual search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pricing loop for one branch-and-price node under its inherited restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let \(P(v)\) be the columns satisfying all inherited branching restrictions. Solve the restricted master over \(R(v)\subseteq P(v)\) and obtain dual multipliers \((\pi,\sigma)\). For minimization, compute \(p^*\in\arg\min_{p\in P(v)}\bar c_p(\pi,\sigma)\), where \(\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sigma\). If \(\bar c_{p^*}<0\), add \(p^*\) to \(R(v)\) and repeat. Otherwise stop and return the restricted-master solution and bound as the optimum of the full node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node-level pricing repeatedly generates branch-feasible negative-reduced-cost columns; absence of such a column certifies the full node relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: The node restricted master is solved exactly.
The pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over \(P(v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\min_{p\in P(v)}\bar c_p\ge 0\), the current restricted-master optimum equals the full node-relaxation optimum.

notation.meaning: columns currently present at the node

review_flags: Supplied source hints do not support node-level branch-and-price pricing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but no citation supports the node-pricing certificate. The reduced-cost formula assumes a particular master structure and dual convention that is not fully specified.

children.title: Branching-Pricing Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Preservation of tractable pricing under branching restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Pricing Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition ensuring branching restrictions remain enforceable inside the pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the original column set and let a branch disjunction at node \(v\) produce children \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\). The disjunction is pricing-compatible when each child admits a set \(P(v_i)=\{p\in P:g_i(p)\le 0\}\) for which the pricing oracle can optimize reduced cost, and when the child sets are exhaustive for integer-feasible parent solutions. Formally, every integer-feasible parent solution belongs to at least one child formulation, while every generated column at child \(v_i\) lies in \(P(v_i)\). Thus pricing neither violates the branch decision nor loses all descendants of a feasible integer solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching rule is pricing-compatible when child restrictions are enforceable by pricing and exhaustively cover the parent’s integer-feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: The parent and child formulations use the same column interpretation.
Each child restriction can be evaluated on an individual column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing under \(P(v_i)\) preserves child validity, and the collection of children preserves exhaustive integer search.
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses branching-pricing compatibility conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately a condition, but no source supports the proposed characterization. Pricing compatibility can involve aggregate master restrictions rather than only columnwise sets of the displayed form, so the asserted generality requires evidence or qualification.

children.title: Tree-Wide Column Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse or localization of generated columns across the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Wide Column Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity criterion for reusing generated columns across branch-and-price nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate every generated column \(p\in P\) with its structural data and retain it in a global pool. A pooled column may be inserted at node \(v\) only if \(p\in P(v)\), where \(P(v)\) incorporates every branching restriction inherited by \(v\). Reusing such a column changes only the restricted representation, not the full node relaxation. Consequently it preserves validity and can improve the initial restricted master. Reuse without the membership test can introduce a branch-infeasible column and invalidate the node bound; failure of membership merely excludes the column from that node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns may be shared across the tree only after checking all inherited branch restrictions; valid reuse preserves the node relaxation and its bound.
assumptions_latex: Stored columns retain sufficient data to test node feasibility.
Node restrictions act on column attributes without altering column costs or coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Insertion of any pooled \(p\in P(v)\) preserves the full relaxation at node \(v\); insertion of \(p\notin P(v)\) is invalid.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports tree-wide column-pool reuse in branch-and-price.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the leaf, but no source supports the tree-wide reuse criterion. Its validity depends on how branching restrictions, local rows, and column coefficients are represented, so the stated universal conclusion needs a specialized reference.

children.title: Branching Architecture
children.top_down_role: Tree-search organization for the generated formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-cut-and-price architecture coordinating exact node pricing with dynamically separated valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a branch-and-bound root with restricted columns and valid base rows. At each node \(v\), impose inherited branch restrictions and alternate restricted-master optimization, pricing of branch-feasible negative-reduced-cost columns, and separation of violated valid inequalities. Continue until neither oracle produces an addition. Then prune by infeasibility or incumbent dominance, accept an integral solution, or create exhaustive children from a fractional solution. Any newly added row invalidates the current dual prices and therefore triggers reoptimization and renewed pricing. Terminate when the open-node set is empty and return the best incumbent.

children.title: Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Valid-inequality generation within search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local separation of valid inequalities within branch-cut-and-price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node relaxation solution \(x^*\) and a valid inequality family \(\mathcal C\), solve the separation problem: find \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal C\) maximizing violation \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x^*-\beta\). If the maximum exceeds tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), add \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) to the restricted master, reoptimize it, and restart pricing because the row changes reduced costs. If no member has violation greater than \(\varepsilon\), return an \(\varepsilon\)-separation certificate for \(\mathcal C\). Every added inequality must remain valid under the node’s branch restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation adds a maximally violated valid inequality, then reoptimizes and reprices; no violation above tolerance certifies closure for the chosen cut family.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal C\) is valid for the relevant integer solutions.
The separation problem is solved globally or returns a valid nonexistence certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination without an added cut certifies \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x^*\le\beta+\varepsilon\) for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal C\).

children.title: Column Pricing

knowledge_statements.title: Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost column generation under the current rows and branching restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), solve the restricted master containing its current cuts and obtain dual multipliers \((\pi,ho)\) for base rows and generated cuts. Over the branch-feasible column set \(P(v)\), solve \(p^*\in\arg\min_{p\in P(v)}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\rho^{\mathsf T}d_p\}\). If the minimum reduced cost is below \(-\varepsilon\), add \(p^*\), reoptimize, and repeat. Otherwise return an \(\varepsilon\)-pricing certificate. Whenever cut separation adds a row, recompute the dual multipliers before accepting any previous pricing certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Price Coordination

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branch Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection principle balancing disjunction quality against preservation of tractable exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fractional node solution, let \(\mathcal B\) be the candidate exhaustive branching disjunctions. Choose \(b^*\in\arg\max_{b\in\mathcal B_{m pc}}S(b)\), where \(S\) is a specified branching score based on predicted bound improvement, balance, or pricing cost. A candidate with a stronger score but no exact pricing interface is inadmissible because its child bounds cannot be certified by the existing decomposition.

assumptions_latex: The node master is a feasible linear minimization problem, and the restricted master supplies an optimal dual vector \(\pi^k\).

children.title: Lagrangian Bound Strength
children.top_down_role: Quality of bounds induced by a selected relaxation.

assumptions_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb Z^n\) be nonempty and finite, and suppose \(\{x\in X:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\).
The primal problem is \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ Ax=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Define \(\theta(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\}\). Then every multiplier gives a valid lower bound, \(\theta(\lambda)\le z_{\mathrm{IP}}\), and the strongest Lagrangian bound satisfies \[\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\theta(\lambda)=\min\{c^\top x:x\in\operatorname{conv}(X),\ Ax=b\}\le z_{\mathrm{IP}}.\] Thus the bound strength is exactly that of imposing the relaxed equations over the convex hull of the retained integer subproblem set.

assumptions_latex: For each multiplier \(\lambda\), the integer subproblem attains \(x(\lambda)\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\}\).

Steps satisfy \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), with bounded subgradients.

assumptions_latex: A Lagrangian subproblem supplies an integer vector \(x^k\in X\), possibly violating linking constraints \(Ax=b\).
A repair operator can modify \(x^k\) while preserving integrality and membership in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Given \(x^k\), compute a repair candidate \(y^k=R(x^k)\in X\) by selecting modifications that reduce a violation measure \(\rho(y)=\lVert Ay-b\rVert\), optionally penalized by objective deterioration. If \(\rho(y^k)>0\), apply local moves within \(X\) until no admissible improving move remains or a resource limit is reached. Accept \(y^k\) as an incumbent only if \(Ay^k=b\) and all original constraints hold; otherwise retain it solely as a recovery seed, never as a primal bound.

children.title: Lagrangian Primal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Construction of feasible primal solutions from relaxation output.

assumptions_latex: Weighted primal iterates satisfy \(x^k\in X\) and weights satisfy \(w_k\ge0\) with \(\sum_{k=0}^K w_k>0\).
The original problem requires integrality and linking equations \(Ax=b\).

Return a point \(\hat x^K\) only after verifying \(\hat x^K\in F\); otherwise report recovery failure. The aggregate itself is not generally integer or feasible and therefore is not automatically a primal solution.

assumptions_latex: A heuristic produces a candidate \(y\) and metadata defining fixed decisions, confidence scores, or a neighborhood.

children.title: Surrogate Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Aggregation-based relaxation of integer constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Surrogate aggregation for a minimization problem with inequality constraints and a mixed-integer domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty mixed-integer set and consider \(z^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). For any nonzero multiplier vector \(u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), the surrogate relaxation replaces all inequalities by their nonnegative aggregate and has value \[S(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ u^{\mathsf T}g(x)\leq0\}.\] Every feasible point of the original problem is feasible for this relaxation; hence \(S(u)\leq z^*\). The surrogate-dual bound is \(S^*=\sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}}S(u)\leq z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate relaxation aggregates several constraints using nonnegative multipliers. Its optimum is a valid lower bound, and optimizing the aggregation gives the surrogate-dual bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and the displayed infima are well defined.
\(u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(u)\leq S^*\leq z^*\).

notation.meaning: Value of the surrogate relaxation with aggregation vector u.

children.title: Volume Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Volume-oriented stabilization of Lagrangian dual search.

knowledge_statements.title: Volume Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian relaxation underlying the volume algorithm in mixed-integer decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), define the Lagrangian value \[L(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\bigr),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m.\] The volume relaxation is this family of Lagrangian subproblems together with a volume-style dual search for \(L^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}L(\lambda)\). Each evaluated \(L(\lambda)\) is a valid lower bound on \(z^*\). Convex combinations of generated minimizers may provide primal estimates, but they do not alter the certified bound unless they are feasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A volume relaxation uses Lagrangian subproblem values as lower bounds while a volume-style procedure searches the multiplier space and averages generated primal solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty.
\(L(\lambda)>-\infty\) for each multiplier used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\lambda)\leq L^*\leq z^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian-dual value targeted by the volume procedure.

children.title: Surrogate-Volume Comparison

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Volume Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound comparison between surrogate aggregation and the Lagrangian relaxation optimized by a volume method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the same minimization problem and sign convention as in the preceding records. For every \(u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) and \(t\geq0\), weak duality for the single surrogate constraint gives \[L(tu)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+t u^{\mathsf T}g(x)\bigr)\leq S(u).\] Because every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) can be written as \(tu\), taking suprema yields \(L^*\leq S^*\leq z^*\). Thus an exact surrogate-dual bound dominates the exact Lagrangian-dual bound targeted by a volume method, although computational costs may differ.

children.title: Nonconvex Value-Function Geometry
children.top_down_role: Structural sources of nonconvex recourse or subproblem value behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Value-Function Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parametric integer recourse value function need not be convex even with linear data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[0,1]\), define the integer value function \[Q(x)=\min\{y:y\in\mathbb{Z}_+,\ y\geq x\}.\] Then \(Q(0)=0\) and \(Q(x)=1\) for every \(x\in(0,1]\). Consequently, with \(x_1=0\), \(x_2=1\), and \(t=1/2\), one has \(Q(tx_1+(1-t)x_2)=1\), whereas \(tQ(x_1)+(1-t)Q(x_2)=1/2\). Thus the mixed-integer value function is nonconvex and discontinuous at zero, despite having a linear objective and a linearly parameterized constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable integer recourse problem produces a step-valued, nonconvex value function, showing why convex supporting-cut arguments can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(y\in\mathbb{Z}_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(1/2)>\tfrac12Q(0)+\tfrac12Q(1)\), so \(Q\) is not convex.

notation.meaning: Optimal integer recourse value at parameter x.

children.title: Global Cut-Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on extending locally derived cuts across the master domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut-Validity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion separating globally valid value-function cuts from merely local affine estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be a recourse value function and let a master variable \(\theta\) represent \(Q(x)\). An affine inequality \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) is globally valid exactly when \[\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\leq Q(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Agreement at one point, descent information, or local validity on a neighborhood does not imply this condition when \(Q\) is nonconvex. Adding a cut that violates the displayed inequality at any feasible parameter can remove a globally optimal solution and invalidate the master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-function cut is globally valid only if its affine right-hand side underestimates the value function everywhere on the master domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) is the complete feasible master domain.
\(Q(x)\) is the exact recourse value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) is globally valid if and only if \(\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\leq Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct definition of global epigraph-cut validity

children.title: Convexification-Based Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Regimes where convexification restores usable master approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification-Based Cut Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globally valid affine cuts obtained from the closed convex envelope of a nonconvex value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\), extend \(Q\) by \(+\infty\) outside \(X\), and let \(Q^{**}\) denote its lower-semicontinuous convex envelope. Then \[Q^{**}(x)=\sup\{\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x:\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}z\leq Q(z)\text{ for every }z\in X\}.\] Hence every affine minorant in this supremum yields a globally valid master cut \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\). The complete family describes the closed convex hull of the epigraph, but it recovers \(Q\) pointwise only where \(Q(x)=Q^{**}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification recovers globally valid cuts as affine minorants of the value function, describing its closed convex envelope rather than necessarily the original function.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and has a proper lower-semicontinuous convex envelope.
\(Q\) is extended by \(+\infty\) outside \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(\operatorname{epi}Q)=\operatorname{epi}Q^{**}\), and every affine minorant of \(Q\) is a globally valid cut.

children.title: Weak Master Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Master Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master weakness measured in a specified objective direction relative to the attainable master set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\) be the attainable set of master pairs \((x,\theta)\), and let \(M_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\) be the master relaxation after \(k\) cuts, with \(P\subseteq M_k\). For the minimization objective \(d^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\), define \[L_k=\inf_{(x,\theta)\in M_k}\bigl(d^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\bigr),\qquad z^*=\inf_{(x,\theta)\in P}\bigl(d^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\bigr).\] Then \(L_k\leq z^*\). In this objective direction, the master relaxation is weak to the extent that the bound gap \(z^*-L_k\) is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master relaxation is weak in a specified objective direction when its optimal lower bound lies far below the optimum over the attainable master set.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq M_k\).
\(L_k\) and \(z^*\) are finite.

children.title: Weak Subproblem Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Subproblem relaxations that yield low-value cuts or columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Subproblem Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of decomposition strength when cuts are generated from a loose subproblem relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\inf\{q(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\) be the exact subproblem value and let \(R(x)\supseteq Y(x)\) define the relaxed value \(\underline Q(x)=\inf\{q(x,y):y\in R(x)\}\). Then \(\underline Q(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every master-feasible \(x\). Cuts supporting or underestimating \(\underline Q\) remain lower-bounding cuts for \(Q\), but their attainable tightness is limited by the relaxation gap \(Q(x)-\underline Q(x)\). If this gap stays positive near relevant master solutions, repeated exact solution of the relaxed subproblem cannot by itself recover the exact recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loose subproblem relaxation yields valid but potentially weak cuts whose missing strength is bounded below by the subproblem relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\subseteq R(x)\) for every master-feasible \(x\).
The value functions are finite at the points compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline Q(x)\leq Q(x)\), and the local loss of tightness equals \(Q(x)-\underline Q(x)\).

children.title: Bound-Stagnation Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Structural causes of prolonged lower-bound or upper-bound plateaus.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Stagnation Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for failure of a newly generated cut to improve the current master bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) be a minimization master with value \(L_k\) and optimal set \(F_k\). Add a valid inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}z\geq b\), obtaining \(M_{k+1}\subseteq M_k\). Then \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\). Moreover, if some \(z^k\in F_k\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}z^k\geq b\), that point remains feasible and \(L_{k+1}=L_k\). Thus bound stagnation occurs whenever each added cut leaves at least one current master optimum feasible; redundancy, degeneracy, and weak subproblem cuts are mechanisms producing this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut cannot worsen a lower bound, but it produces no improvement if at least one current master optimum satisfies the cut.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cap\{z:a^{\mathsf T}z\geq b\}\).
The master minimum \(L_k\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\), and \(F_k\cap M_{k+1}\neq\varnothing\) implies \(L_{k+1}=L_k\).

children.title: Relaxation-Strength Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to distinguish weak formulations from orchestration delays.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Strength Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable gap and violation measures for diagnosing weak decomposition relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an incumbent supplies an upper bound \(U_k\), the master supplies a lower bound \(L_k\), and evaluation at its solution \((x^k,\theta^k)\) gives an exact or certified recourse value \(Q(x^k)\). Define \[\gamma_k=\frac{U_k-L_k}{\max\{1,|U_k|\}},\qquad v_k=\max\{0,Q(x^k)-\theta^k\}.\] The quantity \(\gamma_k\) is a relative global optimality gap, while \(v_k\) is the missing epigraph enforcement at the sampled point. A large \(\gamma_k\) with persistently small \(v_k\) diagnoses that locally generated recourse cuts are not materially strengthening the global master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative bound gap and sampled epigraph violation distinguish unresolved global weakness from a currently missing recourse cut.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\leq z^*\leq U_k\).
\(Q(x^k)\) is exact or accompanied by a valid evaluation certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq(U_k-z^*)/\max\{1,|U_k|\}\leq\gamma_k\), while \(v_k\) measures sampled epigraph violation.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching–Decomposition Interference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and reuse boundary for decomposition information after branch restrictions alter subproblem domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(r\), let the restricted feasible set be \(F_r\subseteq F\). A cut or column generated using \(F_r\) is globally reusable only if its defining validity condition holds for every point of \(F\); validity merely on \(F_r\) permits use only at node \(r\) and its descendants whose feasible sets are contained in \(F_r\). Likewise, branching on variables absent from the master can destroy pricing separability or require node-dependent pricing domains. Unqualified global reuse of node-local information can therefore remove feasible solutions or omit improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch restrictions make some cuts, columns, and pricing formulations node-local; globally reusing them is safe only after proving validity for the original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(F_r\subseteq F\) is the feasible set induced by branching at node \(r\).
Descendant node \(s\) satisfies \(F_s\subseteq F_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node-local information valid only on \(F_r\) is reusable on descendants with feasible sets contained in \(F_r\), but not globally without validity on \(F\).

children.title: Integer Pricing Problems
children.top_down_role: Pricing contexts with discrete feasible sets or integer-generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Pricing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost optimization over an implicitly represented set of integer columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a restricted master with dual vector \(\pi\) for its linking constraints. If each admissible column is indexed by \(y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^q\), has cost \(c(y)\), and contributes \(a(y)\) to those constraints, the integer pricing problem is \[\rho(\pi)=\inf_{y\in Y}\bigl(c(y)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(y)\bigr).\] For a minimization master, a solution with negative reduced cost is an improving column. If the infimum is attained and \(\rho(\pi)\geq0\), no omitted admissible column has negative reduced cost at \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer pricing minimizes reduced cost over an integer column set; a negative optimum produces an improving column, while a nonnegative certified optimum rules one out.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^q\) indexes every admissible omitted column.
The restricted-master dual vector \(\pi\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\pi)<0\) yields an improving column; a certified \(\rho(\pi)\geq0\) excludes all negative-reduced-cost columns.

children.title: Combinatorial Subproblem Hardness
children.top_down_role: Hardness arising from embedded combinatorial optimization tasks.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Subproblem Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for exact integer pricing in column-generation decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a restricted master problem whose columns are indexed by a finite combinatorial set \(P\). Given dual vector \(\pi\), let pricing require computing \(p^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in P}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\}\). If this optimization problem is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions, then an exact column-generation iteration cannot generally be implemented in polynomial time unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), even when solving the current restricted master is polynomial-time tractable. Thus decomposition does not remove the combinatorial hardness; it transfers that hardness to the pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact reduced-cost minimization is NP-hard, column generation has no general polynomial-time implementation unless P equals NP, even when each restricted master is easy.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and represented implicitly by an input of polynomial encoding length.
Costs \(c_p\), columns \(a_p\), and dual vector \(\pi\) are rationally encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact pricing, and hence a general exact column-generation iteration, is not polynomial-time tractable unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).

children.title: Inexact Pricing Consequences
children.top_down_role: Certificate and progress limitations caused by incomplete pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Pricing Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of additive pricing error on reduced-cost optimality tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization master, let \(r^\star=\min_{p\in P} r_p\), and suppose an inexact pricing oracle returns \(\widehat p\) satisfying \(r_{\widehat p}\le r^\star+\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon\ge0\). If the oracle reports \(r_{\widehat p}\ge0\), then \(r^\star\ge-\varepsilon\); therefore termination certifies only absence of a column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\). Conversely, whenever \(r^\star<-\varepsilon\), every oracle satisfying the additive guarantee must return a negative-reduced-cost column. Without a certified error bound, failure to find such a column is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive-error pricing yields only epsilon reduced-cost optimality. Without a certified error bound, failure to find an improving column does not certify optimality.
assumptions_latex: The pricing set \(P\) is nonempty.
The oracle has the additive guarantee \(r_{\widehat p}\le r^\star+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping test \(r_{\widehat p}\ge0\) implies \(r_p\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(p\in P\), but need not imply \(r_p\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct consequence of the additive pricing-oracle inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error implications are correct, but no cited source supports the pricing consequence. Given the enclosing failure-boundary family, failure_boundary may fit better than property.

children.title: Pricing-Oracular Tractability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures supporting effective exact or specialized pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Oracular Tractability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle condition separating tractable exact pricing from decomposition failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of column-generation instances is pricing-oracularly tractable when, for every rational dual vector \(\pi\), an oracle returns either a minimizer of \(c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\) over \(p\in P\), or a correct certificate that all reduced costs are nonnegative, in time polynomial in the encoded instance and \(\pi\). Under this condition, each pricing call and its exact stopping test are polynomial-time operations. This condition alone does not bound the number of column-generation iterations and therefore does not, by itself, establish polynomial total running time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is pricing-oracularly tractable when exact reduced-cost minimization and certification are polynomial-time; this does not ensure polynomially many master iterations.
assumptions_latex: All instance data and queried dual vectors have finite rational encodings.
Oracle running time is measured in the standard bit-complexity model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact pricing is polynomial-time per call, while polynomial total complexity requires an additional bound on the number and cost of master iterations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard oracle-model tractability condition for column generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle condition and its per-call versus total-complexity distinction are precise, and condition fits the leaf, but no authoritative source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Symmetry-Induced Search Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Equivalent decomposed objects that enlarge search without new information.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Search Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant decomposition search caused by objective- and contribution-preserving formulation symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act on a feasible-object set \(X\). Suppose \(c(gx)=c(x)\) and \(a(gx)=a(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(g\in G\). Then, for every dual vector \(\pi\), all objects in the orbit \(Gx=\{gx:g\in G\}\) have the same reduced cost \(c(x)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(x)\). Consequently, an enumeration-based pricing or generation procedure that does not recognize orbit equivalence may inspect multiple representatives that are indistinguishable for the current reduced-cost calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When symmetry preserves both cost and master contribution, every object in an orbit has the same reduced cost. A procedure that ignores this equivalence may redundantly inspect multiple orbit representatives.
assumptions_latex: A finite group \(G\) acts on the feasible-object set \(X\).
For every \(x\in X\) and \(g\in G\), the action preserves both \(c(x)\) and \(a(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), \(g\in G\), and dual vector \(\pi\), \(c(gx)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(gx)=c(x)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(x)\).

notation.meaning: Orbit of x under the symmetry group
Contribution of object x to the master constraints

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariance of cost and master contribution implies reduced-cost invariance

children.title: Degeneracy-Induced Instability
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous pricing, bases, or multipliers caused by degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing variability caused by nonunique optimal restricted-master dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a restricted linear master have two distinct optimal dual solutions \(\pi^1\) and \(\pi^2\) with the same dual objective value. If an absent column \(p\) satisfies \(c_p-(\pi^1)^{\mathsf T}a_p<0\) and \(c_p-(\pi^2)^{\mathsf T}a_p\ge 0\), then whether \(p\) is identified as an improving column depends on the optimal dual solution supplied to pricing. Thus the restricted-master optimal value alone does not determine the set of negative-reduced-cost columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different optimal restricted-master dual vectors can assign different reduced-cost signs to an absent column, so the set of columns identified as improving can depend on dual-solution selection.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a linear program with distinct optimal dual solutions \(\pi^1\) and \(\pi^2\).
An absent column \(p\) has reduced costs of different signs at these dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Column \(p\) is improving under \(\pi^1\) but not under \(\pi^2\), although both dual vectors attain the same restricted-master dual value.

notation.meaning: Master column and its objective coefficient

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reduced costs depend on the selected dual solution

children.title: Duplicate Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Repeated or near-repeated master inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to enlarge a relaxation when separation repeatedly returns equivalent cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let the relaxation contain inequalities \(a_j^{\mathsf T}x\le b_j\) for \(j\in J_k\). A generated cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is duplicate if some \(j\in J_k\) and scalar \(\lambda>0\) satisfy \((a,b)=\lambda(a_j,b_j)\). Adding it leaves the relaxation unchanged. More generally, if the new inequality is implied by the existing relaxation, its addition does not remove any currently feasible point. Repeated generation of duplicate or implied cuts can increase storage and reoptimization cost without strengthening the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive scaling of an existing cut is duplicate and leaves the relaxation unchanged; repeatedly adding duplicate or implied cuts creates overhead without bound improvement.
assumptions_latex: The current relaxation is described by linear inequalities.
Duplicate inequalities are identified up to positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((a,b)=\lambda(a_j,b_j)\) for some \(\lambda>0\), then adjoining \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) does not change the relaxation.

notation.meaning: Indices of cuts present at iteration k
Coefficient and right-hand-side pair of a generated cut

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positively scaled inequalities define the same halfspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-scaling duplicate criterion and unchanged-relaxation conclusion are correct and fit a failure-boundary record, but no authoritative source is cited.

children.title: Duplicate Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Repeated or equivalent generated variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to enlarge a linear restricted master when pricing repeats an existing column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a linear restricted master contain a column variable \(x_p\ge 0\) with no individual upper bound. Suppose pricing generates another variable \(x_q\ge 0\), also without an individual upper bound, such that \((a_q,c_q)=(a_p,c_p)\). For every feasible solution containing \((x_p,x_q)\), replacing these values by \((x_p+x_q,0)\) preserves all master activities and the objective value. Hence the duplicate column adds no attainable master outcome, although retaining it can increase formulation size and degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative, individually unbounded linear master variables, a column with the same coefficients and cost as an existing column adds no master outcome because its value can be aggregated into the existing variable.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is linear.
Variables \(x_p\) and \(x_q\) are nonnegative and have no individual upper bounds.
The columns satisfy \((a_q,c_q)=(a_p,c_p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution \((x_p,x_q)\mapsto(x_p+x_q,0)\) preserves feasibility, master activity, and objective value.

notation.meaning: Existing and newly generated master variables
Master coefficients and objective coefficient of column p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: identical nonnegative unbounded linear columns can be aggregated

knowledge_statements.title: Centralized Global-Consensus Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Star-form consensus representation with one central global variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For agents \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. The centralized consensus model is
\[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for all }i.\]
Its feasible points are exactly \((z,\ldots,z,z)\), so it is equivalent in optimal value and minimizers to \(\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\). The variable \(z\) is the single global consensus variable through which all agents couple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local variables are constrained to equal one central variable, yielding an equivalent formulation of minimizing the sum of all local objectives at a common decision.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The aggregate problem has at least one feasible point with finite objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The consensus formulation and \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\) have the same optimal value, with \(x_i=z\) at every feasible point.

children.title: Shared-Objective Models
children.top_down_role: Separable local terms linked through a shared aggregate objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Objective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable local objectives evaluated at a common decision through consensus copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex local objectives. A shared-objective model has the aggregate form \(F(z)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\) and admits the consensus representation
\[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for all }i.\]
The objective is separable in the local copies, while all coupling is confined to the equalities. Eliminating the copies recovers \(\min_z F(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of local objectives at one shared decision becomes objective-separable after introducing local copies constrained to equal a common variable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
All local objectives share the decision space \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Introducing \(x_i=z\) separates \(\sum_i f_i\) across agents without changing the feasible shared decisions or objective values.

children.title: Resource-Allocation Models
children.top_down_role: Local decisions coupled through common resource limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Allocation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable allocation subject to one shared aggregate resource constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For agents \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), let \(f_i\) be the local cost, and let \(A_i x_i\) denote resource consumption. A convex resource-allocation model is
\[\min_{x_i\in X_i}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b.\]
The objective and local feasible sets are separable; only the aggregate equality couples agents. Replacing equality by \(\sum_i A_i x_i\le b\) gives the corresponding capacity-allocation form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents minimize separable local costs while their resource consumptions must sum to a common supply, so coupling occurs only through the aggregate constraint.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and convex.
Each \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is block-separable except for the shared resource equation \(\sum_i A_i x_i=b\).

children.title: Aggregate-Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Representations centered on sums or other aggregate decision quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling through a linear aggregate of otherwise local decision blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and define the aggregate variable \(s=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\in\mathbb R^q\). An optimization model has aggregate-variable coupling when it can be written as
\[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,s}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad s=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i,\quad x_i\in X_i.\]
All cross-block dependence is mediated by \(s\); after fixing \(s\) and dualizing or splitting the aggregate equality, the local terms remain block-separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model has aggregate-variable coupling when all interaction among local blocks occurs through a variable equal to the sum of their mapped contributions.
assumptions_latex: The maps \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^q\) are linear.
The functions \(f_i\) and \(g\) are extended-real-valued convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sole cross-block relation is \(s=\sum_i A_i x_i\), and eliminating \(s\) yields the coupling term \(g(\sum_i A_i x_i)\).

notation.meaning: Linear map from local decisions to aggregate contributions

children.title: Local-Copy Resource Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Copy Resource Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent consensus-copy representation of a shared aggregate resource variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i)\). Introduce local resource contributions \(y_i=A_i x_i\), local aggregate copies \(s_i\), and a central aggregate \(s\). The equivalent representation is
\[\min\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_i=A_i x_i,\quad s=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i,\quad s_i=s\ \text{for all }i.\]
Eliminating \(y_i\) and the redundant copies \(s_i\) recovers the original formulation exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local resource contributions and consensus copies expose separability while preserving the original aggregate coupling after the auxiliary variables are eliminated.
assumptions_latex: The expressions \(A_i x_i\) lie in a common finite-dimensional resource space.
Auxiliary variables are constrained by the displayed exact equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection onto \((x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) gives precisely the original feasible decisions and preserves every objective value.

notation.meaning: Local copy and central aggregate resource variable

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scenario-consensus model is an optimization problem of the form
\[
\min_{z\in X,\,(x_s)_{s\in S}\in X^{|S|}}\ \sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_s=z\quad(s\in S).
\]
Equivalently, after eliminating the local copies, it is \(\min_{z\in X}\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(z)\). The replicated form exposes scenario separability: for a fixed consensus variable or associated multipliers, each term involving \(x_s\) can be processed independently, while the equalities enforce nonanticipative agreement across all scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-consensus model gives each scenario a local decision copy and forces every copy to equal one shared decision, exposing separable scenario objectives.

children.title: Graph-Consensus Models
children.top_down_role: Consensus representations whose coupling follows a communication graph.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n,d\ge 1\), let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph.
For every \(i\in V\), the function \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
After assigning an arbitrary orientation to every edge, \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times |E|}\) denotes the resulting vertex-edge incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(G\) is connected, then the edge equalities are equivalent to \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\).

notation.meaning: Finite undirected communication graph with vertices indexed from 1 to n
Oriented vertex-edge incidence matrix of G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undirected finite-graph consensus represented by vertex-edge incidence constraints.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The graph-consensus representation is
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d}\ \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=x_j\quad(\{i,j\}\in E).
\]
With \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), the edge equalities have the compact representation
\[
(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_d)x=0.
\]
If \(G\) is connected, then
\[
\ker(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf 1_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb R^d\},
\]
so edgewise agreement is equivalent to global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph consensus replicates a decision at every vertex and imposes equality along edges. For a connected graph, the incidence constraints are equivalent to global agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Consensus Models

children.title: Mixing-Operator Models
children.top_down_role: Network interactions represented through averaging or mixing operators.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n,d\ge 1\), and let \(x^k\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\) denote the stacked states of \(n\) agents at iteration \(k\).
The matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonnegative and row-stochastic.
The sparsity condition \(W_{ij}=0\) holds whenever agent \(j\) cannot send information to agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(W\) is also column-stochastic and \(\ker(I_n-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_n\}\), then the fixed points of \(W\otimes I_d\) are exactly the consensus vectors.

notation.meaning: Stacked agent state at iteration k
Orthogonal projector onto the scalar consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear finite-agent mixing models for decentralized agreement.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mixing-operator model updates the stacked states according to
\[
x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)x^k.
\]
Each block of \(x^{k+1}\) is a convex combination of states available to the corresponding agent. If \(W\) is also column-stochastic and \(\ker(I_n-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_n\}\), then
\[
\operatorname{Fix}(W\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf 1_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb R^d\}.
\]
Thus \((I_n-W)\otimes I_d\) encodes a linear consensus constraint, while \(J\otimes I_d\) is the orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixing operator replaces each agent state by a topology-compatible weighted average. Under the stated fixed-space condition, its fixed points are exactly the consensus states.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Operator Models

children.title: Topology-Dependent Agreement
children.top_down_role: Agreement structure induced by graph connectivity or neighborhood patterns.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge 2\) and \(d\ge 1\), and let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic.
Order the real eigenvalues of \(W\) so that \(\lambda_1(W)=1\), and define \(\beta=\max_{2\le i\le n}|\lambda_i(W)|\).
Assume \(\beta<1\), and let \(x^0\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disagreement contracts geometrically with factor at most \(\beta\), a quantity determined by the topology and the selected mixing weights.

notation.meaning: Largest magnitude among the nonconsensus eigenvalues

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral dependence of linear agreement on a fixed undirected topology.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the iteration \(x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)x^k\), the average component is invariant and, for every integer \(k\ge 0\),
\[
\|x^k-(J\otimes I_d)x^0\|_2
\le \beta^k\|x^0-(J\otimes I_d)x^0\|_2.
\]
Consequently, \(x^k\to(J\otimes I_d)x^0\). The factor \(\beta\) depends jointly on the communication topology and the admissible edge weights; a smaller nonconsensus spectral radius gives faster agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric doubly stochastic mixing, disagreement decays geometrically at a rate bounded by the largest magnitude of a nonconsensus eigenvalue. That rate depends on both the graph and the selected weights.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There is a unique vector \(\pi\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\) satisfying \(\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_n=1\), and primitivity gives
\[
W^k\longrightarrow \mathbf 1_n\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Hence the directed mixing iteration \(x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I_d)x^k\) satisfies
\[
x^k\longrightarrow \mathbf 1_n\otimes\left((\pi^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_d)x^0\right).
\]
The limiting value is generally a stationary-distribution-weighted average rather than the arithmetic average; directed optimization schemes therefore require balanced weights or a normalization mechanism when the arithmetic aggregate is intended.

children.title: ADMM Viewpoint
children.top_down_role: The operator-splitting interpretation centered on alternating primal blocks.

assumptions_latex: Let \(X,Z,Y\) be finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear maps, and let \(c\in Y\).
The functions \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The problem \(\min\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) has a primal-dual saddle point, every displayed subproblem attains a minimizer, and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For an iterate generated by the exact subproblems, simultaneous vanishing of the primal and dual residuals implies the first-order primal-dual optimality conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((z^0,u^0)\in Z\times Y\), scaled ADMM performs, for every integer \(k\ge 0\),
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in Z}\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2\right\},
\qquad
u^{k+1}=u^k+r^{k+1}.
\]
The primal residual is \(r^{k+1}=Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\), and the dual residual is
\[
s^{k+1}=\rho A^{\mathsf T}B(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
A practical implementation stops when these residuals satisfy prescribed tolerances and reports the multiplier \(y^{k+1}=\rho u^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled two-block ADMM alternately minimizes the augmented Lagrangian over the two primal blocks and then updates the multiplier with the current constraint residual.

children.title: Dual-Decomposition Viewpoint
children.top_down_role: The price-based interpretation centered on separable dual subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\). For each \(i\in\{1,ldots,m\}\), let \(X_i\) be a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, let \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) be linear, where \(Y\) is a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space.
Let \(b\in Y\), and assume strong duality for \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\}\).
The dual-ascent step sizes satisfy \(\alpha_k>0\) for every integer \(k\ge 0\), and each displayed block minimization attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At each iteration, the primal minimizations separate by block, while the coupling equality enters through the shared multiplier and aggregate residual.

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the coupling equality at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the concave dual function \(q:Y\to[-\infty,+\infty)\) by
\[
q(y)=-\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle y,A_i x_i\rangle\bigr).
\]
Starting from \(y^0\in Y\), dual decomposition chooses independently, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\),
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle y^k,A_i x_i\rangle\bigr)
\]
and then updates
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k\left(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i^{k+1}-b\right).
\]
The block minimizations are separable at the current multiplier. Practical stopping rules may use feasibility and dual-change tolerances, and primal averaging may be applied when the raw primal iterates do not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual decomposition assigns a multiplier to the coupling equality, solves every primal block independently at that multiplier, and updates the multiplier using the aggregate feasibility residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With the scaled multiplier \(u^k=y^k/\rho\), the ADMM update \(u^{k+1}=u^k+r^{k+1}\) is equivalent to
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho r^{k+1}.
\]
This has the multiplier-residual form of a dual-ascent step. Ordinary dual decomposition obtains its blockwise primal response by minimizing the unaugmented Lagrangian, whereas ADMM alternately minimizes an augmented Lagrangian containing
\[
\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz-c\|^2.
\]
Thus both methods communicate through the coupling multiplier, but their primal response maps generally differ.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=-x^2\) and \(g(z)=0\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(\partial f(x)=\{-2x\}\) is anti-monotone because
\[
(x-y)\bigl((-2x)-(-2y)\bigr)=-2(x-y)^2<0\quad(x\ne y).
\]
Hence \(\partial f\) is not maximal monotone, and its resolvent lacks the firm-nonexpansiveness guarantee used in the convex splitting correspondence. Moreover, the ADMM \(x\)-subproblem has quadratic coefficient \(\rho/2-1\) and is unbounded below when \(0<\rho<2\). Thus neither well-defined ADMM iterations nor the standard operator equivalence follows after convexity is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvexity can destroy both ADMM subproblem solvability and the maximal-monotone structure required for the usual splitting correspondence.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(v^0\in H\), Douglas–Rachford splitting computes
\[
y^k=J_{\gamma B}v^k,\qquad
x^k=J_{\gamma A}(2y^k-v^k),\qquad
v^{k+1}=v^k+x^k-y^k.
\]
It stops when the fixed-point residual \(\|x^k-y^k\|\) is below a prescribed tolerance and returns \(y^k\). At an exact fixed point, the resolvent identities imply the existence of opposite elements in \(A y^k\) and \(B y^k\), so \(0\in A y^k+B y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Douglas–Rachford alternates two resolvents and a correction step; a fixed point produces a solution of the sum inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal consensus problem
\[
\min_{x,z\in H}\ f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x=z
\]
has the dual minimization \(\min_{y\in H}F(y)+G(y)\), where \(F(y)=f^*(-y)\) and \(G(y)=g^*(y)\). Exact two-block ADMM with augmented-Lagrangian penalty \(\rho\), after the standard affine change combining its multiplier with one primal block, generates the Douglas-Rachford fixed-point iteration for
\[
0\in\partial F(y)+\partial G(y)
\]
with resolvent parameter \(\rho\). Thus the alternating augmented-Lagrangian steps of ADMM represent Douglas-Rachford splitting on the dual inclusion under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For canonical convex consensus, exact ADMM with penalty rho is a primal-coordinate representation of Douglas-Rachford splitting with resolvent parameter rho on the dual optimality inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in H\), the proximal-point method computes
\[
x^{k+1}=J_{\gamma_k T}(x^k),
\]
equivalently choosing \(x^{k+1}\) so that
\[
0\in T(x^{k+1})+\gamma_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).
\]
It stops when the resolvent residual \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|/\gamma_k\) is below a prescribed tolerance and returns \(x^{k+1}\). For \(T=\partial h\) with proper closed convex \(h\), the update is \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\{h(x)+\|x-x^k\|^2/(2\gamma_k)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-point method repeatedly evaluates a monotone operator's resolvent; for a convex subdifferential, each step minimizes a quadratically regularized objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex two-block ADMM viewed as Douglas–Rachford splitting on the dual inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(g\) be proper closed convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, and consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). Assume a saddle point exists and that the subproblems are solvable. For any \(\rho>0\), the scaled two-block ADMM iteration induces, after the standard affine identification of its multiplier and shadow variables, Douglas–Rachford splitting for the dual optimality inclusion \(0\in \partial(f^*\circ(-A^*))(y)+\partial(g^*\circ(-B^*)+\langle c,\cdot\rangle)(y)\). Douglas–Rachford is itself a proximal-point iteration for its associated Douglas–Rachford maximal-monotone operator. Thus the three viewpoints generate the same dual fixed points, although their displayed iterates differ.
