children.title: Progressive-Hedging Viewpoint
children.top_down_role: Scenario-decomposed consensus interpretation of progressive hedging.

knowledge_statements.title: Progressive-Hedging Viewpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario convex progressive hedging in a probability-weighted product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let scenarios \(s=1,\ldots,S\) have probabilities \(p_s>0\), let \(F(x)=\sum_s p_s f_s(x_s)\), and let \(N\) be the nonanticipativity subspace. Choose \(\rho>0\), initialize \(z^0\in N\) and \(w^0\in N^\perp\), and iterate scenario-parallel updates \[x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_u\left\{f_s(u)+\langle w_s^k,u\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|u-z_s^k\|^2\right\},\qquad z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1},\qquad w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).\] Stop when both \(\|x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\|\) and \(\rho\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|\) meet prescribed tolerances; output the nonanticipative policy \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressive hedging solves scenario subproblems independently, averages their decisions onto the nonanticipativity subspace, and updates disagreement multipliers until primal and dual residuals are small.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Every scenario subproblem attains a minimizer.
\(N\) is a closed linear nonanticipativity subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration produces scenario decisions, a nonanticipative projection, and multiplier updates suitable for residual-based termination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Progressive-Hedging Viewpoint container, but no source is supplied. A source must confirm the probability-weighted product-space convention, the scaling of the scenario multipliers and quadratic terms, and the stated primal/dual residual termination rule.

children.title: Scenario-Splitting Viewpoint
children.top_down_role: Operator-splitting representation of scenario copies and nonanticipativity.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Splitting Viewpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space representation separating scenario objectives from nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenarios \(s=1,\ldots,S\) with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\), equip \(H=\prod_s H_s\) with \(\langle x,y\rangle_p=\sum_s p_s\langle x_s,y_s\rangle\). If \(f_s:H_s\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is the scenario objective and \(N\subseteq H\) is the nonanticipativity subspace, then the extensive-form stochastic program is \[\min_{x\in H}\;F(x)+\delta_N(x),\qquad F(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s f_s(x_s).\] The resolvent of \(\partial F\) is scenario-separable, \((\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}x)_s=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_s}(x_s)\), while \(\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_N}=P_N\) couples scenarios only through nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form is a sum of scenario objectives plus the indicator of nonanticipativity. Scenario proximal steps separate, while projection onto nonanticipativity supplies the only coupling.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite and all \(p_s>0\).
Each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(N\) is a closed linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F+\delta_N\) admits separate scenario proximal evaluations followed by the coupling projection \(P_N\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-space representation and componentwise proximal formula are mathematically plausible under the stated weighted inner product, and representation is the correct knowledge kind. No citation is supplied, however. The source should also make clear that the separate proximal map and projection are operators used by a splitting method, not that their simple composition is necessarily the proximal map of the sum.

children.title: Nonanticipativity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural role of scenario agreement within the splitting map.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between scenario agreement, projection residuals, and admissible disagreement multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be the closed linear subspace of scenario policies that agree whenever scenarios share the same observed history. Then \(x\) is nonanticipative exactly when \(x=P_Nx\), equivalently \(x-P_Nx=0\). Moreover, \(N_{N}(z)=N^\perp\) for every \(z\in N\), where \(N_N\) is the normal-cone operator. Consequently, the optimality system for \(\min_x F(x)+\delta_N(x)\) is \[0\in\partial F(x)+w,\qquad x\in N,\qquad w\in N^\perp.\] Thus progressive-hedging multipliers lie in the orthogonal disagreement space, and its residual \(x-P_Nx\) measures violation of nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity is membership in a scenario-agreement subspace. Projection residuals measure its violation, while valid multipliers belong to the orthogonal disagreement subspace.
assumptions_latex: The scenario policy space is a Hilbert product space.
\(N\) is the closed linear nonanticipativity subspace.
\(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in N\), \(w\in N^\perp\), and \(-w\in\partial F(x)\) characterize the convex nonanticipative optimum.

notation.meaning: orthogonal complement of the nonanticipativity subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection and orthogonal-complement identities are standard, but the asserted multiplier characterization of every optimum requires a constraint qualification ensuring the relevant subdifferential sum rule or multiplier existence. No source is provided to determine the intended hypotheses, so the mathematical version is not yet reliable.

children.title: Nonconvex Transfer Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of the correspondence for discrete or nonconvex scenario models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Transfer Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why convex progressive-hedging convergence does not transfer automatically to nonconvex scenario models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convex splitting guarantees cease to apply when a scenario function is nonconvex: its subdifferential need not be maximal monotone and its proximal mapping need not be single-valued. Concretely, for \(f=\delta_{\{-1,1\}}\) on \(\mathbb R\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(0)=\arg\min_{u\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1}{2\gamma}|u|^2=\{-1,1\}\] for every \(\gamma>0\). Hence the progressive-hedging scenario update can be set-valued even with a positive quadratic penalty. Without an explicit selection rule and additional nonconvex regularity, the iteration is not a single-valued averaged operator, so convex Douglas–Rachford or ADMM fixed-point convergence cannot be inferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex scenario set can make a penalized scenario update multivalued. The averaged-operator argument behind convex progressive hedging then fails, so convex convergence guarantees do not transfer.
assumptions_latex: At least one scenario objective is allowed to be nonconvex.
The scenario update uses a positive quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonconvexity can destroy single-valued proximal updates and blocks automatic transfer of convex splitting convergence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit two-point counterexample correctly demonstrates a multivalued proximal update and fits a failure-boundary container. External support is still required for the broader convergence-transfer claim, and the statement must specify which nonconvex subdifferential is meant before asserting failure of maximal monotonicity.

children.title: Proximal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Regularization through proximity to a reference master point.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically stabilized master step for a convex cutting-plane model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex, let \(m_k\leq f\) be a finite cutting-plane model, choose a center \(c_k\), and select \(t_k>0\). Compute \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-c_k\|^2\right\}.\] Evaluate \(f(x^{k+1})\) and a subgradient \(g^{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1})\), then add the cut \(f(x^{k+1})+\langle g^{k+1},x-x^{k+1}\rangle\) to the model. Move \(c_k\) to \(x^{k+1}\) after a prescribed sufficient-decrease test; otherwise retain the center. Stop when the model-predicted decrease is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle master minimizes the cutting-plane model plus a quadratic centered at the incumbent, then updates the model and moves the center only after sufficient decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(m_k\) is a finite polyhedral minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized master has a coercive strongly convex objective and therefore a unique minimizer whenever \(m_k\) is proper.

children.title: Bundle Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization through managed collections of cutting information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step/null-step bundle method with a stabilized polyhedral master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a center \(c_k\), a bundle \(B_k\) of evaluated pairs \((x_i,f(x_i),g_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), and \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in B_k}\{f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\}\). Given \(t_k>0\), compute \(y_k=\arg\min_x\{m_k(x)+\|x-c_k\|^2/(2t_k)\}\) and predicted decrease \(v_k=f(c_k)-m_k(y_k)\). For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \(c_{k+1}=y_k\) if \(f(c_k)-f(y_k)\geq\eta v_k\); otherwise set \(c_{k+1}=c_k\). Add a subgradient cut at \(y_k\), optionally aggregate inactive cuts, and stop when \(v_k\) is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bundle stabilization combines accumulated subgradient cuts with a proximal master. Successful trial points become new centers; unsuccessful null steps enrich the model without moving the center.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite-valued convex and subgradients are available at trial points.
The bundle retains enough cuts to preserve its model minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration is classified as a serious step or null step while maintaining \(m_k\leq f\).

notation.meaning: bundle of function values and subgradients

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected algorithm kind fits the terminal container, but no source is supplied. The formulation also needs authoritative support for the definition of predicted decrease, the serious-step test, cut aggregation, and stopping rule. In particular, the assumptions should state the cut-management condition that preserves the center interpolation property used by the predicted-decrease test.

children.title: Master-Stability Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Shared control of unstable master movement or multiplier oscillation.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Stability Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian correspondence between proximal and trust-region stabilized master problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex, let \(c\in\operatorname{dom}m\), and let \(R>0\). Suppose the trust-region master \(\min\{m(x):\|x-c\|\leq R\}\) has a solution \(x_R\) and satisfies Slater's condition. Then there is \(\lambda\geq0\) such that \[0\in\partial m(x_R)+\lambda(x_R-c),\qquad \lambda(\|x_R-c\|-R)=0.\] If \(\lambda>0\), setting \(t=1/\lambda\) makes \(x_R\) the unique minimizer of \(m(x)+\|x-c\|^2/(2t)\). Conversely, a proximal-master minimizer is a trust-region-master minimizer for radius \(R=\|x_t-c\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active Euclidean trust-region stabilization and quadratic proximal stabilization select the same master solution when their radius and multiplier are matched.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The trust-region master attains a solution and satisfies Slater's condition.
The trust-region multiplier is positive for the proximal equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An active trust-region master corresponds to a proximal master through \(t=1/\lambda\), and every proximal solution defines a matching radius.

children.title: Stabilization-Divergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where proximal and bundle interpretations yield materially different structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Divergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete unbounded-master failure prevented by positive quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex objective \(f(x)=|x|\), evaluation at \(x_0=1\) with subgradient \(g_0=1\) gives the valid one-cut model \(m_0(x)=1+(x-1)=x\). The unstabilized cutting-plane master satisfies \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}m_0(x)=-\infty,\] so it produces no trial point. For every center \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(t>0\), the proximal master \(m_0(x)+(x-c)^2/(2t)\) is strongly convex and has the unique minimizer \(x=c-t\). Thus a positive coercive stabilization prevents this escape; if stabilization is removed or its effective curvature tends to zero without other boundedness controls, master iterates may again be unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a valid cut of a bounded-below convex function can yield an unbounded master. Positive quadratic stabilization makes that master coercive; removing it permits escape to infinity.
assumptions_latex: The cutting-plane model may contain only the cut generated at \(x_0=1\).
No explicit bounded feasible region is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unstabilized master is unbounded below, whereas every positively stabilized master has the unique solution \(c-t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-cut example and its stabilized minimizer are correct and fit a failure-boundary container. No citation supports the broader statement about loss of boundedness as effective curvature vanishes, so external source support is required even though the concrete counterexample is self-contained.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Separability of an Objective Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition for large-scale unconstrained objectives; it does not assert a universal convergence rate for methods exploiting the structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is partially separable if it admits a decomposition $f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ in which every component $f_i$ depends only on a small-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (equivalently, only on a small subset or low-dimensional projection of the variables).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective is partially separable when it is a sum of simpler component functions, each depending on only a small-dimensional subspace of the full variable space.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}
m\in\mathbb{N}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x),\quad \text{with each }f_i\text{ depending only on a low-dimensional subspace of }\mathbb{R}^n.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Separable Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard convex regime in which blockwise resolvents and proximal maps are well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\times\cdots\times H_m\) be a finite product of Hilbert spaces. The closed convex separable regime consists of problems \[\min_{x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in H}\left\{F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\right\}\] possibly together with a closed linear coupling constraint, where every \(f_i:H_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and the feasible set is nonempty. For every \(\gamma>0\), \(\partial F=\partial f_1\times\cdots\times\partial f_m\) is maximal monotone and \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(x)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(x_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of proper closed convex block functions has a maximal-monotone product subdifferential, and its proximal map decomposes into independent block proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: Each block function is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The product has finitely many Hilbert-space blocks.
Any imposed linear coupling has a nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subdifferential is maximal monotone and its resolvent evaluates independently across uncoupled blocks.

children.title: Linear-Coupling Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Coupling Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable convex blocks connected solely through a finite-dimensional linear equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\) and \(G\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(f_i:H_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(A_i:H_i\to G\) be linear maps, and let \(b\in G\). A linearly coupled separable problem is \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b.\] Its Lagrangian is \(L(x,y)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)+\langle y,\sum_iA_ix_i-b\rangle\). For fixed \(y\), minimization of \(L\) separates across blocks; all inter-block dependence is carried by the common multiplier \(y\) and the linear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-coupling regime has a separable convex objective and one shared linear equation. Fixing its multiplier separates all primal block minimizations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each \(A_i\) is linear.
The coupling equation has a feasible point in the effective domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(y\), \(\inf_x L(x,y)= -\langle y,b\rangle+\sum_i\inf_{x_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*y,x_i\rangle\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space consensus for finitely many local decision copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(m\ge 2\). The consensus subspace of \(H^m\) is
\[C=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in H^m:x_1=\cdots=x_m\}.\]
A separable problem is in the consensus regime when it has the form
\[\min_{(x_i)_{i=1}^m\in H^m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\iota_C(x_1,\ldots,x_m),\]
where each \(f_i:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\iota_C\) is the indicator of \(C\). Equivalently, it minimizes \(\sum_i f_i(x)\) over one shared variable \(x\in H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus decomposition assigns each component a local copy of the decision variable and constrains all copies to be equal.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(m\ge 2\) and each \(f_i:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in C\) if and only if there exists \(x\in H\) with \(x_i=x\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Consensus subspace of the product space.
Extended-real indicator of the consensus subspace.

children.title: Coupling-to-Consensus Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Reformulations that expose linear coupling through agreement variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-to-Consensus Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting of a two-block linear coupling through image variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Z,Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(c\in Y\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear. Define
\[\phi(y)=\inf\{f(x):Ax=y\},\qquad \psi(w)=\inf\{g(z):Bz=c-w\},\]
where an infimum over the empty set is \(+\infty\). Then
\[\inf_{Ax+Bz=c}\{f(x)+g(z)\}=\inf_{y=w}\{\phi(y)+\psi(w)\}.\]
Thus the linear coupling is represented by consensus between image variables. If the lifted problem has a minimizer and the corresponding fiber infima are attained, the attaining fiber points form a minimizer of the original coupled problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-block linear coupling can be represented as equality of two image variables, with each objective replaced by its infimum over the corresponding linear fiber; recovering an original minimizer requires attainment of the relevant fiber infima.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Z,Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces and \(c\in Y\).
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
Extended-real infima use the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled and lifted-consensus problems have equal infimal values; an attained lifted minimum and attained corresponding fiber infima yield a coupled primal minimizer.

notation.meaning: Right-hand side of the linear coupling constraint.
Value functions obtained by minimizing over linear fibers.
Lifted image variables constrained to agree.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Coupling Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural limitations associated with deficient coupling operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Coupling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of direct variable recovery from a rank-deficient coupling image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear with \(\ker A\ne\{0\}\), and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). For every nonzero \(h\in\ker A\) and every \(x\in X\), one has \(A(x+h)=Ax\). Hence an image variable \(y=Ax\) does not determine \(x\), and assigning the value of \(f\) to \(y\) through an inverse image is not single-valued unless \(f\) is constant on every fiber of \(A\). An exact image-space reduction must retain a primal copy or use the fiber value function
\[\phi(y)=\inf\{f(u):u\in X,\ Au=y\}.\]
Consequently, consensus of coupling images alone cannot certify equality or unique recovery of the original primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient coupling map hides null-space directions, so agreement of image variables does not imply equality or unique recovery of primal variables; an exact image reduction must retain primal variables or minimize over each fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real vector spaces.
\(A:X\to Y\) is linear and \(\ker A\ne\{0\}\).
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal images identify primal variables only modulo \(\ker A\); exact image-space reduction requires fiber minimization or retained primal variables.

notation.meaning: Null space of the coupling map.
Objective value minimized over an image fiber.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric proximal-point iteration for a monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a real Hilbert space \(H\), a maximally monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), an initial point \(x^0\in H\), and self-adjoint strongly positive metrics \(M_k\), compute
\[x^{k+1}=J_{M_k^{-1}A}(x^k)=(I+M_k^{-1}A)^{-1}(x^k).\]
Equivalently, choose \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying \(0\in A x^{k+1}+M_k(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Stop when a prescribed residual, iteration, or computational budget criterion holds, and return the latest iterate. The regime is variable-metric when \(M_k\) may change with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each proximal step uses a possibly changing positive-definite metric, equivalently scaling the monotone inclusion differently at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
Each \(M_k:H\to H\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is the resolvent step \(x^{k+1}=J_{M_k^{-1}A}(x^k)\) in the metric induced by \(M_k\).

notation.meaning: Positive-definite metric operator at iteration k.

children.title: Preconditioned Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-metric preconditioning of a monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a real Hilbert space \(H\), a maximally monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), an initial point \(x^0\in H\), and a bounded, self-adjoint, strongly positive operator \(M:H\to H\), iterate
\[x^{k+1}=J_{M^{-1}A}(x^k)=(I+M^{-1}A)^{-1}(x^k).\]
Equivalently, choose \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying \(0\in Ax^{k+1}+M(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Stop under a prescribed residual, iteration, or computational-budget criterion and output the latest iterate. The operator \(M\) is fixed throughout and acts as a preconditioner; choosing \(M=\gamma^{-1}I\) with \(\gamma>0\) recovers the scalar-step proximal-point update \(J_{\gamma A}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proximal step uses the same positive-definite operator to precondition the inclusion; a positive scalar multiple of the identity gives the usual proximal-point step size.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
\(M:H\to H\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed preconditioning produces \(x^{k+1}=J_{M^{-1}A}(x^k)\), with scalar case \(M=\gamma^{-1}I\) for \(\gamma>0\).

children.title: Block-Structured Metric Design

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Metric Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definiteness condition for a symmetric two-block preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_1\oplus H_2\) and define the self-adjoint block operator
\[M=\begin{pmatrix}P&K^*\\K&Q\end{pmatrix},\]
where \(P:H_1\to H_1\) is strongly positive, \(Q:H_2\to H_2\) is self-adjoint, and \(K:H_1\to H_2\) is bounded. Then \(M\) is strongly positive if and only if its Schur complement
\[Q-KP^{-1}K^*\]
is strongly positive. This predicate permits off-diagonal coupling while ensuring that \(\langle Mx,x\rangle\) defines an equivalent squared norm on the product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric two-block metric is positive definite exactly when one diagonal block and its associated Schur complement are positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H_1\oplus H_2\) is a real Hilbert product space.
\(P\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
\(K\) is bounded and \(Q\) is bounded and self-adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\succ0\) if and only if \(P\succ0\) and \(Q-KP^{-1}K^*\succ0\).

children.title: Metric-Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits imposed by poorly controlled or incompatible metric choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Stability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convergence when variable metrics permit summably small effective steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Uniform positivity alone does not ensure convergence if the metrics are unbounded above. On \(H=\mathbb R\), take \(A=I\), whose unique zero is \(0\), and choose \(M_k=2^k I\). The variable-metric proximal iteration becomes
\[x^{k+1}=\frac{2^k}{2^k+1}x^k.\]
For \(x^0\ne0\), the infinite product \(\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}2^k/(2^k+1)\) is positive because \(\sum_k2^{-k}<\infty\). Hence the iterates converge to a nonzero value and do not solve \(0\in Ax\). An upper metric bound, or an equivalent nonsummability condition on effective steps, excludes this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metrics growing too quickly make effective steps summably small, allowing proximal iterates to stop short of the solution despite positive definiteness.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\mathbb R\), \(A=I\), and \(x^0\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates converge to a nonzero limit, so strong positivity without upper control of \(M_k\) is insufficient.

notation.meaning: Identity monotone operator in the counterexample.

children.title: Randomized-Coordinate Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized-Coordinate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent randomized block updates for a fixed-point problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\), let \(T:H\to H\), and choose \(x^0\in H\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with probabilities \(p_i>0\), and update
\[x_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_i^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_i(x^k)-x_i^k\bigr),&i=i_k,\\x_i^k,&i\ne i_k.\end{cases}\]
Here \(T_i\) is the \(i\)-th block of \(T\), and \(\lambda_k>0\) is a prescribed relaxation. Stop under a residual, iteration, or sampling budget and output the latest iterate or a specified averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, a positively sampled coordinate block performs a relaxed fixed-point update while all other blocks remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) is a finite Hilbert product space.
Every block has sampling probability \(p_i>0\).
The relaxation sequence \((\lambda_k)\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the sampled block \(i_k\) is changed by the relaxed coordinate of \(T-I\).

notation.meaning: The i-th coordinate block of the fixed-point operator.

children.title: Asynchronous Regime
children.top_down_role: Updates formed without globally synchronized worker timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block fixed-point updates computed from a delayed shared state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) be a finite Hilbert product space, let \(T:H\to H\), choose \(x^0\in H\), and set \(x^t=x^0\) for every integer \(t<0\). At logical time \(k\), a worker reads
\[\widehat x^k=(x_1^{k-d_{k,1}},\ldots,x_m^{k-d_{k,m}}),\qquad d_{k,j}\in\mathbb N_0,\]
selects a block \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and, for a prescribed relaxation \(\lambda_k>0\), atomically writes
\[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_{i_k}(\widehat x^k)-\widehat x_{i_k}^k\bigr),\]
while setting \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for every \(j\ne i_k\). Stop under a prescribed residual, iteration, or computational-budget criterion and output the shared iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each logical iteration, a worker updates one block using a possibly stale coordinate read; pre-initial history is identified with the initial point, and the completed block write is atomic.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) is a finite Hilbert product space.

children.title: Randomized-Asynchronous Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of stochastic activation and delayed information.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized-Asynchronous Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified delayed randomized block fixed-point update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) be a finite Hilbert product space, let \(T:H\to H\), and let \(U_i:H_i\to H\) be the canonical injection into block \(i\). Let \(\mathcal F_k\) be the history before the iteration-\(k\) block is sampled, and suppose that \(x^k\), the delayed read \(\widehat x^k=(x_j^{k-d_{k,j}})_{j=1}^m\), and the relaxation \(\lambda_k\) are \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. If
\[\mathbb P(i_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_i>0\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m),\]
then the randomized asynchronous update
\[x^{k+1}=x^k+\lambda_k U_{i_k}\bigl(T_{i_k}(\widehat x^k)-\widehat x_{i_k}^k\bigr)\]
satisfies
\[\mathbb E[x^{k+1}-x^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\lambda_k\sum_{i=1}^m p_iU_i\bigl(T_i(\widehat x^k)-\widehat x_i^k\bigr).\]
Thus random block selection averages the delayed block residuals with their sampling probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pre-sampling-measurable delayed read and relaxation, a randomized asynchronous block update has conditional mean equal to the probability-weighted delayed block residual.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) is a finite Hilbert product space and \(T:H\to H\).
\(U_i:H_i\to H\) is the canonical injection into block \(i\).
\(x^k\), \(\widehat x^k\), and \(\lambda_k\) are measurable with respect to the pre-sampling history \(\mathcal F_k\).
\(\mathbb P(i_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_i>0\) for every block, with \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\).
The write to block \(i_k\) is atomic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional expected increment equals the probability-weighted block decomposition of the residual evaluated at \(\widehat x^k\).

notation.meaning: Canonical injection of block i into the product space.
History available before the iteration-k block sample.
Conditional probability of sampling block i.

children.title: Unbounded-Delay Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of transferable guarantees under uncontrolled information age.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Delay Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A contraction may fail under unrestricted stale reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the scalar contraction \(T(x)=qx\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(0<q<1\), with unique fixed point \(0\). Use the asynchronous update \(x^{k+1}=T(x^{k-d_k})\), initialize \(x^0\ne0\), and choose \(d_k=k\). Every update then reads \(x^0\), so
\[x^{k+1}=q x^0\quad\text{for every }k\ge0.\]
The sequence is eventually constant at a nonfixed point. Therefore contractivity of the underlying operator does not itself guarantee convergence when delays are unbounded and may repeatedly expose a permanently stale state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With unrestricted delays, every update can reuse the initial value, causing even a strict contraction to remain at a nonfixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=qx^0\ne0\) for all \(k\), so the asynchronous iteration does not converge to \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Delay used by the scalar update.

children.title: Integer-Variable Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits arising specifically from integrality restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Variable Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convex proximal structure for integer feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\mathbb Z\subset\mathbb R\) and let \(f=\iota_S\). Its proximal mapping is the nearest-integer correspondence
\[\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb Z}|z-x|^2.\]
At every half-integer \(x=n+\tfrac12\), this set equals \(\{n,n+1\}\), so the proximal mapping is not single-valued. Any single-valued tie-breaking selection is discontinuous at half-integers and therefore cannot be firmly nonexpansive. Thus standard convex operator-splitting guarantees based on single-valued firmly nonexpansive proximal maps do not transfer directly when an integer constraint is represented by its indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal operator of an integer-set indicator is multivalued at half-integers, breaking the firm nonexpansiveness used by convex splitting theory.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\mathbb Z\subset\mathbb R\).
\(f=\iota_S\) is the extended-real indicator of the integer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(n+\tfrac12)=\{n,n+1\}\); hence convex proximal-splitting assumptions fail at the integer-variable boundary.

notation.meaning: Zero on S and positive infinity outside S.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Consensus Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus restricted to a nonconvex local domain can lose convex projection geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two agents and a closed set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), define the restricted consensus set \(C_D=\{(z,z):z\in D\}\). If \(D\) is nonconvex, then \(C_D\) need not be convex. In particular, for \(D=\{-1,1\}\), \(C_D=\{(-1,-1),(1,1)\}\), and \[P_{C_D}(0,0)=\{(-1,-1),(1,1)\}.\] Consequently, consensus projection may be multivalued, placing projection-based splitting outside its standard closed-convex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex local domains induce nonconvex consensus sets whose projections can be multivalued.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(D=\{-1,1\}\), the consensus projection at the origin has two values.

children.title: Convex-Relaxation Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Gaps between splitting behavior on relaxations and the original discrete model.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Relaxation Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An elementary integrality gap between a discrete problem and its convex-hull relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{-1,1\}\) and \(f(x)=x^2\). The discrete problem and its convex-hull relaxation satisfy \[\min_{x\in D}f(x)=1,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)=\{-1,1\},\] whereas \[\min_{x\in\operatorname{conv}D}f(x)=0,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[-1,1]}f(x)=\{0\}.\] Hence solving the convex relaxation produces neither a discrete feasible point nor the discrete optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying a discrete feasible set can change both the optimizer and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation has value \(0\), while the discrete problem has value \(1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiblock Splitting Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of unconditional convergence for direct cyclic extensions of two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the separable convex program \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b,\] where \(m\ge 3\), every \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and a solution exists. These assumptions alone do not imply convergence of the direct Gauss--Seidel multiblock ADMM that minimizes successively over \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) and then updates one multiplier. Additional structure, proximal regularization, or a reformulation is required for a general convergence guarantee.

children.title: Uncontrolled-Composition Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled-Composition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Picard iteration can fail when component maps lack averagedness or relaxation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(T_1=I\) and \(T_2=-I\). Both maps are nonexpansive and share the fixed point \(0\). Their composition is \(T_2T_1=-I\). For any \(x^0\ne0\), the unrelaxed Picard iteration \[x^{k+1}=T_2T_1x^k\] gives \(x^k=(-1)^k x^0\) and therefore does not converge. Thus nonexpansiveness of the component maps and existence of a common fixed point do not alone control a composed Picard iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing nonexpansive maps without averagedness or relaxation can produce a nonconvergent oscillation.
assumptions_latex: \(T_1=I\) and \(T_2=-I\) on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k=(-1)^k x^0\), so the iterates do not converge.

notation.meaning: Identity mapping on the real line.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral condition identifying ill-conditioning in a coupled equality-constrained quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x,z}\ \tfrac12x^\top Qx+\tfrac12z^\top Rz\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,\] where \(Q\succ0\), \(R\succ0\), and \([A\ B]\) has full row rank. The dual Hessian is \(S=AQ^{-1}A^\top+BR^{-1}B^\top\succ0\). The coupling is ill-conditioned at level \(K>1\) when \[\kappa_2(S)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(S)}{\lambda_{\min}(S)}\ge K.\] Small \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\) corresponds to a weakly represented coupling direction and produces high sensitivity in dual-space iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Parameter Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ADMM contraction factor for a scalar strongly convex quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a,b,\rho>0\), apply standard scaled two-block ADMM with penalty \(\rho\) to \[\min_{x,z}\ \tfrac a2x^2+\tfrac b2z^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x-z=0.\] The linear state-update matrix has eigenvalues \(0\) and \[q(\rho)=\frac{\rho^2+ab}{(a+\rho)(b+\rho)}.\] Hence the asymptotic contraction factor depends on the penalty, satisfies \(q(\rho)\to1\) as \(\rho\downarrow0\) or \(\rho\to\infty\), and is minimized at \(\rho=\sqrt{ab}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning–Penalty Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The optimal scalar ADMM penalty depends jointly on both block curvatures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the scalar quadratic ADMM model with curvatures \(a,b>0\), the optimal penalty is \(\rho_\star=\sqrt{ab}\), and the corresponding contraction factor is \[q(\rho_\star)=\frac{2\sqrt{ab}}{a+b+2\sqrt{ab}}.\] Writing \(\kappa=\max\{a,b\}/\min\{a,b\}\), this becomes \[q(\rho_\star)=\frac{2\sqrt\kappa}{(1+\sqrt\kappa)^2}.\] Thus the penalty scale is set jointly by the two curvatures; choosing it from only one block can place the iteration far from its optimal regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best penalty is the geometric mean of the block curvatures, so penalty choice and conditioning cannot be separated.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Based Recovery Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise perturbation bound for an inexact nonexpansive fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, and suppose \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k+e^k\). If \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) and \(z^0=x^0\), then \[\|x^k-z^k\|\leq \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\|e^i\|.\] Hence \(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\|e^i\|<\infty\) gives a uniform bound on the deviation, with error-tail bounds tending to zero. This summability condition marks a genuine worst-case boundary: if \(T=I\), \(e^k=t_k u\), \(\|u\|=1\), \(t_k\geq0\), and \(\sum_k t_k=\infty\), then \(x^k=x^0+(\sum_{i<k}t_i)u\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact nonexpansive iteration deviates from its exact orbit by at most the sum of past error norms. Summable errors give bounded accumulated influence, whereas same-direction errors with divergent total magnitude can make the iterates unbounded.

children.title: Stochastic Error Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Noise-driven local inaccuracies across decomposed computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square accumulation of martingale-difference errors in stochastic splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be a filtration and let \(e^k\) be square-integrable Hilbert-space-valued martingale differences satisfying \(\mathbb E[e^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\). For deterministic coefficients \(\alpha_k\), orthogonality of martingale increments yields \[\mathbb E\left\|\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_ke^k\right\|^2=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2\mathbb E\|e^k\|^2.\] Consequently, \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2\mathbb E\|e^k\|^2<\infty\) makes the accumulated perturbations Cauchy in mean square and convergent almost surely. If this variance series diverges, mean-square control does not follow; independent scalar centered errors provide the canonical failure case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Martingale-difference errors accumulate through the sum of their weighted variances. A finite variance series gives mean-square and almost-sure convergence of accumulated noise.
assumptions_latex: e^k\in L^2(H)\text{ and }\mathbb E[e^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0
e^k\text{ is }\mathcal F_{k+1}\text{-measurable}
\alpha_k\in\mathbb R\text{ is deterministic}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\left\|\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_ke^k\right\|^2=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2\mathbb E\|e^k\|^2

notation.meaning: information available before error k is realized

children.title: Certificate Degradation
children.top_down_role: Loss of stopping reliability or bound interpretation under inexact solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degradation of a fixed-point residual certificate under an inexact operator evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be an operator and suppose an implementation returns \(y=Tx+e\) with a certified error bound \(\|e\|\leq\eta\). The computable residual \(\widehat r=\|x-y\|\) certifies the exact fixed-point residual through \[\max\{0,\widehat r-\eta\}\leq \|x-Tx\|\leq \widehat r+\eta.\] Hence accepting \(x\) when \(\widehat r\leq\varepsilon\) certifies only \(\|x-Tx\|\leq\varepsilon+\eta\). Without a valid bound on \(\eta\), the computed residual alone is not a certificate for the exact operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator-evaluation error enlarges a computed fixed-point residual certificate by its certified norm; without an error bound, the computed residual cannot certify exact stationarity.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a normed space}
y=Tx+e
\|e\|\leq\eta
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{0,\|x-y\|-\eta\}\leq\|x-Tx\|\leq\|x-y\|+\eta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-enlargement certificate follows from the triangle inequality and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Stale-Primal Information
children.top_down_role: Local computations based on outdated primal states.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Primal Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed reads of primal blocks in an asynchronous decomposition update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal blocks \(x_i^k\in X_i\) at logical iteration \(k\), a worker uses stale-primal information if its update is evaluated at \[\widehat x^k=\bigl(x_1^{k-d_{1,k}},\ldots,x_m^{k-d_{m,k}}\bigr),\] where each integer delay satisfies \(0\leq d_{i,k}\leq k\). The read is current precisely for blocks with \(d_{i,k}=0\); it is inconsistent when the delays differ across blocks, so \(\widehat x^k\) need not equal any previously stored complete primal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale-primal information is a blockwise primal vector assembled from earlier iterations, possibly with different delays for different blocks.
assumptions_latex: x_i^k\in X_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m
d_{i,k}\in\{0,\ldots,k\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x^k=(x_i^{k-d_{i,k}})_{i=1}^m

notation.meaning: age of primal block i used at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Dual Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed dual or multiplier values used by a decomposition subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^k\in Y\) denote the dual variable or coupling multiplier at logical iteration \(k\). A subproblem uses stale-dual information when its update is computed using \[\widehat y^k=y^{k-d_k},\qquad d_k\in\{0,\ldots,k\},\] rather than \(y^k\). For blockwise dual variables, one analogously permits \(\widehat y^k=(y_j^{k-d_{j,k}})_j\). Staleness is absent exactly when every applicable delay is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale-dual information is an earlier multiplier or a blockwise collection of earlier multipliers used in the current subproblem update.

d_k\in\{0,\ldots,k\}

children.title: Bounded-Delay Regime
children.top_down_role: Asynchronous operation with controlled information age.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Delay Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform partial-asynchronism condition for delayed block information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A delayed block-update process is in the bounded-delay regime if there exists a finite integer \(D\geq0\) such that every block value used at iteration \(k\) was generated no earlier than iteration \(\max\{0,k-D\}\). Equivalently, all read delays obey \[0\leq d_{i,k}\leq \min\{D,k\}\quad\text{for every block }i\text{ and iteration }k.\] If update participation is also required, partial asynchronism additionally assumes that each block is updated at least once in every window of \(D+1\) consecutive iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded delay means every block read is at most a fixed number of iterations old; partial asynchronism also requires regular block participation.
assumptions_latex: d_{i,k}\in\{0,\ldots,k\}
D\in\mathbb N\text{ is independent of }i\text{ and }k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{i,k}d_{i,k}\leq D<\infty

notation.meaning: delay of block i read at iteration k

children.title: Uncontrolled-Delay Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural failure risks when delays lack useful bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled-Delay Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded delays can destroy convergence even for a scalar smooth strongly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and the delayed-gradient iteration \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha\nabla f(x^{k-d_k})\), where \(0<\alpha<2\). With current information, \(d_k=0\), the iteration converges to zero. If delays are uncontrolled, choose \(d_k=k\); then every update uses \(x^0\), and \[x^k=(1-k\alpha)x^0.\] For any \(x^0\neq0\), the iterates diverge in magnitude. Thus convergence cannot generally be inferred merely from the stability of the corresponding synchronous method when no delay control is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded delay can make stable gradient descent diverge: repeatedly using the initial gradient causes linear drift on a scalar quadratic.
assumptions_latex: f(x)=\tfrac12x^2
0<\alpha<2
d_k=k\text{ and }x^0\neq0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k=(1-k\alpha)x^0\quad\text{and}\quad |x^k|\to\infty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar quadratic counterexample is internally correct and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no evidence source or standard-field rationale is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Subproblem Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided objective certificate from a valid master lower model and feasible subproblem recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+Q(x)\}\). Let \(\underline Q(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and let \(L=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\underline Q(x)\}\). If a master candidate \(\bar x\in X\) admits a feasible subproblem solution with value \(\overline Q(\bar x)\geq Q(\bar x)\), define \(U=f(\bar x)+\overline Q(\bar x)\). Then \[L\leq v^*\leq U.\] The pair \((L,U)\) is a verifiable absolute-gap certificate, and \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of the recovered feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid master lower model supplies a lower bound, while a feasible subproblem recovery supplies an upper bound; their difference certifies the global gap.
assumptions_latex: \underline Q(x)\leq Q(x)\text{ for all }x\in X
\bar x\in X\text{ and }\overline Q(\bar x)\geq Q(\bar x)
L\text{ is computed globally over the master domain}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\leq v^*\leq U,\qquad U-L\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow U-v^*\leq\varepsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The master lower model and feasible recovery yield the stated two-sided certificate, and the certificate content kind fits the topic, but the nontrivial decomposition claim lacks a cited source.

children.title: Pricing-Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that no improving priced object remains within the specified pricing domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pricing certificate for a linear-programming column-generation master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the master LP \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\geq0\}\). Let \(R\subseteq J\), and let \((\lambda^R,\pi^R)\) be primal-dual optimal for the restricted master over \(R\). Exact pricing computes \[r^*=\min_{j\in J}\{c_j-(\pi^R)^{\mathsf T}a_j\}.\] If \(r^*\geq0\), then \(\pi^R\) is feasible for the full dual and the zero extension of \(\lambda^R\) is optimal for the full master. The restricted primal and dual objectives therefore form an exact global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact pricing finds no negative reduced-cost column, the restricted-master dual is feasible for the full dual and the restricted solution is globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: R\subseteq J
(\lambda^R,\pi^R)\text{ is primal-dual optimal for the restricted master}
r^*\text{ is the exact global pricing minimum}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r^*\geq0\Rightarrow \lambda^R\text{ is optimal for the full master LP}

notation.meaning: minimum reduced cost over all columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-pricing optimality certificate is mathematically standard and correctly scoped to the full LP master, but no authoritative column-generation source is cited.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Certificates
children.top_down_role: Optimality evidence expressed through reduced-cost information.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasibility and gap certificate expressed through column reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the master LP with columns \((a_j,c_j)\), define the reduced cost at a candidate multiplier \(\pi\) by \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\). The inequalities \(\bar c_j\geq0\) for every \(j\in J\) certify full-dual feasibility. If \(\lambda\) is full-primal feasible, then \[c^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b^{\mathsf T}\pi=\sum_{j\in J}\bar c_j\lambda_j\geq0.\] Hence the displayed sum is a computable primal-dual gap certificate; it equals zero exactly when every positive column has zero reduced cost, which certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced costs certify dual feasibility, and their activity-weighted sum equals the primal-dual gap for any feasible master solution.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b
\lambda_j\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J
\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b^{\mathsf T}\pi=\sum_{j\in J}\bar c_j\lambda_j\geq0

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost identity and complementary optimality conclusion are correct under the stated primal and dual feasibility conditions, but the record contains no supporting citation.

children.title: Restricted-Master Certification
children.top_down_role: How pricing evidence supports claims about a restricted master.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual optimality certificate for the current restricted column set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R\subseteq J\), consider the restricted master \(\min\{\sum_{j\in R}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in R}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\geq0\}\). A pair \((\lambda^R,\pi^R)\) certifies restricted-master optimality when it satisfies primal feasibility, \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^R\geq0\) for every \(j\in R\), and \[\lambda_j^R\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^R\bigr)=0\quad(j\in R).\] These conditions imply equality of restricted primal and dual objectives. They certify only the restricted master; full-master certification additionally requires valid pricing over every column in \(J\setminus R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, nonnegative restricted reduced costs, and complementary slackness certify optimality only over the current column set; global certification still requires pricing.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{j\in R}a_j\lambda_j^R=b,\quad\lambda_j^R\geq0
c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^R\geq0\text{ for }j\in R
\lambda_j^R(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^R)=0\text{ for }j\in R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in R}c_j\lambda_j^R=b^{\mathsf T}\pi^R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility, restricted dual feasibility, and complementary-slackness conditions correctly certify only the restricted master. An authoritative source is still required.

children.title: Inexact-Pricing Certificate Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on certification when pricing is heuristic or incomplete.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Pricing Certificate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-gap certification requires a lower bound on pricing error and control of total column mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda\) be master-feasible, let \(\pi\) be the restricted-master multiplier, and suppose certified inexact pricing proves \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\geq-\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in J\). If every feasible master solution under consideration satisfies \(\sum_j\lambda_j\leq M\), then \[c^{\mathsf T}\lambda-b^{\mathsf T}\pi=\sum_j\lambda_j(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j)\geq-\varepsilon M.\] Thus \(b^{\mathsf T}\pi-\varepsilon M\) is a valid lower bound. Merely failing to find a negative-cost column is not a certificate: without a global pricing guarantee, or without a finite mass bound \(M\), no finite objective-gap conclusion follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate pricing yields a global gap bound only with a certified reduced-cost lower bound and bounded total column mass; heuristic pricing failure alone proves nothing.
assumptions_latex: c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\geq-\varepsilon\text{ for every }j\in J
\lambda\geq0,\quad A\lambda=b
\sum_j\lambda_j\leq M<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq b^{\mathsf T}\pi-\varepsilon M

notation.meaning: valid upper bound on total column weight

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed bound is algebraically correct when the mass bound applies uniformly to every feasible solution relevant to the global lower bound. Because that condition is model dependent and the record has no source, authoritative support is required before accepting the stated certificate boundary.

children.title: Consensus-Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence based on disagreement among local or scenario copies.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-consensus feasibility certificate for a convex block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear with consensus subspace \(\mathcal C=\ker A\). For the problem \(\min_x\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=0\), define \(r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)=Ax\). With a fixed norm on \(\mathbb R^q\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{con}}\geq0\), the inequality \(\|r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{con}}\) is an absolute consensus-feasibility certificate. Moreover, \(r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The norm of the violated consensus equations certifies approximate feasibility, while a zero residual is equivalent to membership in the declared consensus subspace.
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the function \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The linear map \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), the norm on \(\mathbb R^q\), and the tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{con}}\geq0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\|r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{con}}\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{con}}\)-feasibility for \(Ax=0\), and \(r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)=0\iff x\in\ker A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Residual Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i\), let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and consider \(L(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\langle y,Ax\rangle\) with \(y\in\mathbb R^q\). For selected \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), let \(g=(g_1,

A norm on \(\mathbb R^n\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual}}\geq0\) are fixed.

children.title: Primal–Dual Certificate Crosswalk

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Certificate Crosswalk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT residual crosswalk for convex problems with linear equality coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i\), let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and consider \(\min_x\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=0\). Associate a candidate \((x,y,g)\), where \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), with \[R(x,y,g)=\bigl(\|Ax\|,\|g+A^{\mathsf T}y\|\bigr).\] The first component measures primal feasibility and the second stationarity. Thus \(R(x,y,g)\leq(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d)\) componentwise is the joint residual certificate. Under the stated convexity assumptions, \(R(x,y,g)=(0,0)\) if and only if \((x,y,g)\) satisfies primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity, the equality-constrained KKT conditions represented here.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate vector pairs equality-constraint violation with Lagrangian stationarity error and vanishes exactly when those two convex KKT conditions hold.
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the function \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The map \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) is linear, \(y\in\mathbb R^q\), and \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\) for every \(i\).
Fixed norms are used on \(\mathbb R^q\) and \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(R=(\|Ax\|,\|g+A^{\mathsf T}y\|)\) crosswalks primal feasibility and stationarity, and \(R=(0,0)\) is equivalent to the represented equality-constrained KKT conditions.

children.title: Residual-Stopping Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of residual-only stopping evidence for objective quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Stopping Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute two-residual stopping region and its boundary; relative scaling is external.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_p\in E_p\) and \(r_d\in E_d\), where \(E_p\) and \(E_d\) are fixed normed spaces. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,
\varepsilon_d\geq0\), define \[\mathcal S(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d)=\{(r_p,r_d)\in E_p\times E_d:\|r_p\|\leq\varepsilon_p,\ \|r_d\|\leq\varepsilon_d\}.\] The joint residual stopping condition holds exactly when \((r_p,r_d)\in\mathcal S(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d)\). Its boundary consists of points in this region for which \(\|r_p\|=\varepsilon_p\) or \(\|r_d\|=\varepsilon_d\). If either tolerance is exceeded, this residual criterion does not certify termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is certified when both residuals lie in the declared closed stopping region; equality in at least one active tolerance identifies its boundary.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual residuals belong to fixed normed spaces \(E_p\) and \(E_d\), respectively.

The tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,
\varepsilon_d\geq0\) and all scaling conventions are declared.
Any subgradient data used to form the dual residual are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Stopping is certified exactly on \(\mathcal S(\varepsilon_p,
\varepsilon_d)\), whose boundary is characterized by equality in at least one of its two residual inequalities.

notation.meaning: Simultaneous statistical lower and upper bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic simultaneous-confidence certificate, independent of a particular sampling construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*\) be the optimal value of a minimization problem, and let data of size \(N\) produce random quantities \(L_N\leq U_N\). If their construction guarantees \(\Pr\{L_N\leq v^*\leq U_N\}\geq1-\alpha\), then \([L_N,U_N]\) is a simultaneous confidence bracket for \(v^*\). On any realization satisfying \(G_N:=U_N-L_N\leq\varepsilon\), the bracket is a statistical \((\varepsilon,1-\alpha)\) optimality-gap certificate. The confidence claim concerns the random construction, not the conditional probability after inspecting the realized bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous random lower and upper bound whose width is at most epsilon certifies an epsilon optimal-value bracket at the construction's confidence level.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Optimality-Gap Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the statistical construction. Moreover, unconditional coverage of the random bracket does not by itself imply confidence 1-alpha conditional on observing a small realized width; an authoritative construction or an additional joint/selection-valid guarantee is required.

assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer problem is a minimization problem with optimal value \(v^*\).
The incumbent is feasible with objective value \(U\), and \(L\) is a globally valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The data certify \(L\leq v^*\leq U\), hence \(0\leq U-v^*\leq U-L\); if \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute global-bound certificate for mixed-integer minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a mixed-integer minimization problem, let \(U\) be the objective value of a verifiably feasible incumbent and let \(L\) be a valid lower bound over the entire feasible set, obtained for example from an exhaustive branch-and-bound state or a valid relaxation argument. Then \(L\leq v^*\leq U\), so the absolute incumbent gap \(G=U-L\) bounds the unknown suboptimality by \(0\leq U-v^*\leq G\). Consequently, \(G\leq\varepsilon\) is a globally verifiable \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate; \(G=0\) certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and a valid global lower bound certify optimality within their difference for a mixed-integer minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Global-Bound Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-bound certificate is mathematically standard and correctly typed as a certificate, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.
